module: inference-driver: R/inference.R (estimate_rates, estimate_rates_control, .run_mcem/.run_cem/.run_gam, expand/contract, init_pars logic, cond_fun) + R/emphasis.R (.mcem_dynamic_fresh, .mcem_warn_estep) + the C++ entry they call (src/rcpp_mcem.cpp -> src/mcem.cpp -> src/E_step.cpp / src/M_step.cpp)
purpose: estimate_rates() is the single public entry point for parameter inference. It resolves the model (3-slot binary c(use_N,use_M,use_D)) and link (0/1/2), merges user control with per-method defaults, validates bounds, extracts branching times, builds an optional survival-conditioning closure from a GAM, chooses/validates init_pars (MCEM only), expands compact parameters/bounds to the 8-element C++ layout, dispatches to one of three back-ends (MCEM via .run_mcem -> .mcem_bdi or .mcem_dynamic_fresh; CEM via emphasis_cem; GAM via a likelihood-surface GAM), contracts the 8-element result back, applies the survival correction to the reported MCEM log-likelihood, and returns an "emphasis_fit" (pars, loglik, loglik_var, n_pars, AIC, details). .mcem_dynamic_fresh is the thinning-proposal MCEM driver: each iteration calls em_cpp (one E-step of `sample_size` augmented trees by Poisson thinning + one SBPLX M-step on the IS-weighted complete-data log-likelihood), with a range-scaled parameter-stability stopping rule, failure recovery (double maxN, pull pars 20% toward the bound centre), a wall-clock budget, and a final bootstrap of the IS log-likelihood variance.

key_functions.name: estimate_rates
key_functions.role: Public dispatcher. Resolves model/link, merges control defaults + aliases, validates bounds (length 2+2*sum(model_bin)), builds cond_fun, chooses/validates init_pars (mcem), expands to 8-element layout, dispatches to .run_mcem/.run_cem/.run_gam, contracts result, applies loglik - log P_tree for mcem, computes AIC.

key_functions.name: estimate_rates_control
key_functions.role: Per-method default control lists. Common: lower/upper_bound NULL, verbose FALSE, max_missing 1e4, num_threads 1, max_time 3600 s, rho 1. MCEM: sampling='bdi', sample_size 200, max_iter 200, maxN 2000, xtol 1e-3, tol 1e-3, patience 3. CEM: max_iter 50, num_particles 50, sd_vec NULL, maxN 10, num_trees 1, shared_trees FALSE, disc_prop 0.5, tol 1e-4, patience 5, sd_decay 0.85, sd_min_frac 0.01, bias_correct FALSE. GAM: grid_points 20, sample_size 200, maxN NULL, max_lambda 500, spline_type 'univariate'.

key_functions.name: .resolve_control_aliases
key_functions.role: Syncs old/new names (num_points<->num_particles, sample_size<->num_trees). User-supplied name wins; if both or neither from user, the new name wins. The back-ends read the OLD names (ctrl$sample_size, ctrl$num_points).

key_functions.name: .extract_brts
key_functions.role: Numeric -> sort decreasing; phylo -> ape::branching.times sorted decreasing; simulate_tree list -> $tes, else prune_to_extant($tas).

key_functions.name: .par_names / .contract_pars / .expand_pars
key_functions.role: Compact layout c(beta_0, beta_{active...}, gamma_0, gamma_{active...}) <-> 8-element c(beta_0,beta_N,beta_M,beta_D,gamma_0,gamma_N,gamma_M,gamma_D). Inactive slots are 0; active covariate k (1=N,2=M,3=D) maps to slots k+1 (beta) and k+5 (gamma).

key_functions.name: .validate_linear_init_pars
key_functions.role: Linear link only: for each active covariate, if beta_0 + beta_X*maxX <= 0 (maxX = n_tips for N, crown age for M and D) set beta_X = -0.9*beta_0/maxX clamped to bounds; same for gamma with strict '< 0'. Only guards the positive covariate extreme.

key_functions.name: .build_cond_fun
key_functions.role: Closure pars8 -> log(max(predict_survival(gam, compact(pars8)), 1e-300)). Passed as rconditional to C++ M-step and used in R to correct reported loglik.

key_functions.name: .run_mcem
key_functions.role: Falls back from 'bdi' to 'dynamic_fresh' when !.bdi_supported(model, link) (any M or D term, or gaussian link). maxN default max(2000, 10*sample_size) only if NULL. loglik = last finite fhat in the per-iteration table; loglik_var from driver.

key_functions.name: .run_cem
key_functions.role: sd_vec default (ub-lb)/4 (8-element). Calls emphasis_cem; loglik = raw$best_IS$fhat (already conditioned inside emphasis_cem) else last best_loglik.

key_functions.name: .run_gam
key_functions.role: Builds LHS (ctrl$n_grid>0) or factorial grid in compact space, evaluates IS fhat per point, subtracts log P_tree(grid) if cond, fits GAM, L-BFGS-B over varying dims, expands back. loglik_var NA.

key_functions.name: .mcem_dynamic_fresh
key_functions.role: Thinning MCEM driver loop; see math_as_implemented.

key_functions.name: .mcem_warn_estep
key_functions.role: After 8 consecutive E-step failures: runs a 1-tree/maxN=200 diagnostic em_cpp (rho and conditional NOT passed), regex-parses '<n> zero weights' from the C++ error message; if n > 50 warns about lambda=0 collapse, else generic warning.

key_functions.name: rcpp_mcem (em_cpp)
key_functions.role: Rcpp entry: builds Model(lb8, ub8, model_bin, link, rho), wraps R conditional as std::function, calls emphasis::mcem, throws 'no trees, no optimization' if E-step empty, returns rejected counts, estimates, nlopt status, fhat, time (E+M ms), weights (linear max-scaled), logf, logg.

key_functions.name: emphasis::mcem
key_functions.role: One E_step then one M_step (skipped if no trees). Ignores xtol/lower/upper in E-step; passes them to M-step.

key_functions.name: emphasis::E_step
key_functions.role: TBB parallel_for over maxN attempts; each: augment_tree (thinning), logf = model.loglik, logg = model.sampling_prob, keep if finite(log_w) && exp(log_w) > 0; stop at N accepted; hard 120 s wall limit; throws emphasis_error_E if fewer than N; converts log-weights to linear max-scaled weights; fhat = log(sum_w/(N+n_zero)) + max_log_w.

key_functions.name: emphasis::M_step / objective
key_functions.role: SBPLX (package copy) minimising -sum_i w_i * loglik(theta, z_i) [+ log P_tree(theta) if conditional], bounds = lb8/ub8, xtol_rel = ctrl$xtol, start = current pars.

math_as_implemented:
NOTATION. theta is the 8-vector (beta_0,beta_N,beta_M,beta_D,gamma_0,gamma_N,gamma_M,gamma_D) (R/simulate.R:296-309; inst/include/model.hpp:60-76). y = observed branching times, sorted decreasing, crown age first (R/inference.R:216-232). z_i = augmented tree i (extinct/unsampled lineages added by the thinning proposal). All logs natural.

INTERNAL TIME CONVENTION (C++). create_tree (src/E_step.cpp:19-38) maps brts b_0 > b_1 > ... > b_{m-1} to forward times: node j (j=0..m-2) at time b_0 - b_{j+1} with n = 2 + j (lineage count during the segment ending at that node), plus a final sentinel node at time b_0 (the present) with n = m+1 = number of tips. The crown at forward time 0 with 2 lineages is implicit. The last node is excluded from the speciation product (model.hpp:436).

RATES (model.hpp:117-212). Linear (link 0): lambda = max(0, beta_0 + beta_N N + beta_M M + beta_D D), mu = max(0, gamma_0 + ...). Exponential (link 1): lambda = exp(beta_0 + ...). Gaussian (link 2): lambda = beta_0 * exp(-(beta_N N + beta_M M + beta_D D - 1)^2/2) (intercept excluded from eta). M = pd/n, D = E_s - M.

COMPLETE-DATA LOG-LIKELIHOOD logf(theta, z) = model.loglik (model.hpp:359-471):
  logf = sum_{extinction nodes} log(max(mu, 1e-300)) + sum_{speciation nodes except sentinel} log(lambda) - sum_{segments} dt * n * (lambda + mu) [+ n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1-rho) if rho<1],
  with per-segment closed-form integrals replacing dt*n*(lambda+mu) for D-models on the exponential/gaussian links (model.hpp:381-417).
PROPOSAL log-probability logg(theta, z) = model.sampling_prob (model.hpp:255-...; not in this subsystem).
IS LOG-WEIGHT lw_i = logf(theta, z_i) - logg(theta, z_i), both evaluated at the SAME theta that generated z_i (src/E_step.cpp:90-92).

E-STEP ACCEPTANCE (src/E_step.cpp:94-107). Tree kept iff isfinite(lw_i) && exp(lw_i) > 0; otherwise counted as rejected_zero_weights (this also catches lw = +Inf and underflow lw < ~-745). Augmentation exceptions -> rejected_overruns (> max_missing extinct lineages), rejected_lambda (lambda bound > max_lambda; max_lambda hard-coded 1e6 at R/emphasis.R:50), rejected (other). Loop stops when N = sample_size trees accepted, or maxN attempts, or 120 s elapsed (E_step.cpp:73, default because em_cpp never passes max_time_seconds). If accepted < N: throw (E_step.cpp:128-130) -> R sees NULL.

IS LOG-LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATE (fhat) returned by em_cpp (src/E_step.cpp:132-144, precision_weights.hpp:11-24):
  m = max_i lw_i;  sum_w = sum_{i=1}^{N} exp(lw_i - m)  (computed in 100-digit boost floats);
  fhat = log(sum_w / S) + m,   S = N + rejected_zero_weights.
  i.e. fhat = log[ (1/S) sum_i exp(lw_i) ] with zero-weight completed trees included in the denominator as w=0. This is the E-step's estimate of log p(y | theta_current) — evaluated at the parameters BEFORE the M-step of the same iteration.
  R re-derives the same quantity for final_IS via .is_fhat(logf, logg, n_zero_weight) = log(sum exp(lw - max)) + max - log(n_valid + n_zero) (R/de.R:60-76; R/emphasis.R:155-156).

M-STEP WEIGHTS. After fhat, E.weights[i] is overwritten with the LINEAR max-scaled weight w_i = exp(lw_i - m) in (0,1], NOT normalised (E_step.cpp:133-139; precision_weights.hpp:20). Hence sum_i w_i = sum_w ∈ [1, N].

M-STEP OBJECTIVE (src/M_step.cpp:41-62):
  Q(theta) = sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i * logf(theta, z_i)
  minimise  -Q(theta)                       if no conditional,
  minimise  -Q(theta) + log P_tree(theta)   if conditional (cond returns log P_tree, R/inference.R:337-343).
  Note the unconditioned maximiser is invariant to the weight scale, but the conditioned objective is NOT: the properly self-normalised conditioned EM objective is sum_i (w_i/sum_w) logf(theta,z_i) - log P_tree(theta), i.e. in unnormalised form sum_i w_i logf - (sum_w) * log P_tree. The code uses coefficient 1 instead of sum_w on log P_tree (M_step.cpp:61).
  Optimiser: package SBPLX copy, bounds lb8/ub8, start = theta_current, stop on xtol_rel = ctrl$xtol (relative parameter change, nlopt semantics |dx| <= xtol_rel*|x|) (M_step.cpp:81-89). theta_{k+1} = argmin.

MCEM ITERATION (R/emphasis.R:43-133). For k = 1..max_iter:
  1. em_cpp(theta_{k-1}) -> {fhat_k = fhat(theta_{k-1}), theta_k = M-step estimate, logf/logg of the N trees drawn at theta_{k-1}} (emphasis.R:44-61).
  2. On failure (NULL): fail_streak++, maxN <- min(2*maxN, 50000), theta <- 0.8*theta + 0.2*(lb+ub)/2 clamped to bounds (emphasis.R:64-85); break with stop_reason='e_step_failure' at 8 consecutive failures; prev_pars and streak are NOT updated on failure. On the next success maxN is reset to the ORIGINAL value (emphasis.R:89).
  3. delta_k = max_j |theta_k[j] - theta_{k-1}[j]| / r_j, with r_j = ub_j - lb_j, r_j := 1 where ub_j == lb_j (emphasis.R:28-29, 93). prev_pars <- theta_k.
  4. Row appended: par1..par8 = theta_k, fhat = fhat(theta_{k-1}), delta_max, rejected (unhandled only), num_trees = sample_size, time (E+M ms) (emphasis.R:97-105).
  5. Convergence: if delta_k < tol then streak++ else streak <- 0; stop 'converged' when streak >= patience (emphasis.R:114-122). Sample size N is constant across iterations (no growth, no averaging).
  6. Time budget: stop 'time_budget' if elapsed > max_time (checked after each successful iteration, emphasis.R:125-132).

REPORTED QUANTITIES.
  pars = theta_K of the last successful M-step (or the recovery-perturbed vector if the loop ended on a failed iteration) (emphasis.R:92, 165).
  loglik (unconditioned) = last finite fhat in the table = fhat(theta_{K-1}), the IS estimate at the parameters BEFORE the final M-step (R/inference.R:410-412).
  loglik (reported by estimate_rates, mcem + cond) = fhat(theta_{K-1}) - log P_tree(theta_K) (inference.R:819-822).
  AIC = -2*loglik + 2*n_pars, n_pars = length of compact vector including bound-fixed parameters (inference.R:816, 824).
  loglik_var = Var_B over B=200 bootstrap resamples (with replacement, size N) of the K=2 moment-corrected estimator  l_hat + log(1 + m_2/2), l_hat = mean(lw*), m_2 = mean((lw* - l_hat)^2), computed from the logf/logg of the LAST E-step (theta_{K-1}), WITHOUT the zero-weight denominator term (R/emphasis.R:136-142; R/de.R:476-489, 88-100). So the variance is of a different estimator than the reported loglik.
  final_IS = {logf, logg, lw, fhat via .is_fhat with n_zero_weight, ESS = (sum w)^2/sum w^2 on exp(lw - max), n_rejected = rejected+overruns+lambda, rejected_zero_weights} (emphasis.R:145-161; de.R:111-117).

INIT_PARS (inference.R:714-738). If NULL and method=='mcem': theta_0 = (lb+ub)/2 (compact); for linear link with any active covariate, every slope (compact positions 1+k for beta, n/2+1+k for gamma) is set to clamp(0, lb_j, ub_j). Then, for linear link with covariates, .validate_linear_init_pars applies the lambda>0/mu>=0 guards at the positive covariate extreme (inference.R:256-324). init_pars is expanded to 8 elements (inference.R:754); it is ignored by cem and gam.

BOUNDS. Compact lb/ub -> lb8/ub8 with inactive slots pinned to [0,0] (inference.R:752-753); lb8/ub8 go to the C++ Model and to SBPLX (rcpp_mcem.cpp:75, 90-91; M_step.cpp:84-87), to the range scaling r_j, and to the recovery centre (lb+ub)/2 (emphasis.R:41).

SURVIVAL CONDITIONING. cond_fun(pars8) = log max(P_hat_tree(compact(pars8)), 1e-300) (inference.R:333-344). MCEM: enters the M-step objective as +log P_tree on the minimised function (M_step.cpp:58-61) and is subtracted from the reported loglik at the final pars (inference.R:820-822); the per-iteration fhat table stays unconditioned. CEM: emphasis_cem subtracts cond_fun from each particle's fhat internally (de.R:651-653, 821-822, 868-869) and estimate_rates does not correct again. GAM: surface$fhat - log P_tree(grid) before fitting (inference.R:527-530).
data_flow:
Inputs: tree (phylo | simulate_tree list | numeric brts) -> .extract_brts -> numeric brts sorted DECREASING, crown age first (inference.R:216-232, 704). model -> .resolve_model -> integer c(use_N,use_M,use_D) (simulate.R:254-275; shortcuts cr=000, dd=100, d=001, nd=101, rd/ep=001; formula terms N, D, EP, E). link -> .resolve_link -> 0 linear / 1 exponential / 2 gaussian (simulate.R:247-251). control -> modifyList(defaults, control) -> alias sync -> ctrl; the back-ends read ctrl$sample_size (mcem/gam), ctrl$num_points + ctrl$sample_size (cem). lower/upper_bound are COMPACT (length 2+2*sum(model_bin), order beta_0, beta_active..., gamma_0, gamma_active...) and are the only required control entries (inference.R:689-702).

Parameter layouts: compact (user-facing, named by .par_names) <-> 8-element C++ layout via .expand_pars/.contract_pars; slot map active covariate k in {1:N, 2:M, 3:D} -> beta slot k+1 (1-based), gamma slot k+5. 8-element vectors are what cross into C++ (init_pars, lb8, ub8, estimates) and what cond_fun receives; cond_fun contracts before calling predict_survival with named columns.

MCEM path: estimate_rates -> .run_mcem(brts, ip8, lb8, ub8, ctrl, model_bin, link_int, cond_fun) -> (bdi supported? .mcem_bdi : .mcem_dynamic_fresh) -> per iteration em_cpp(brts, init_pars=theta, sample_size, maxN, max_missing, max_lambda=1e6, lb8, ub8, xtol_rel=ctrl$xtol, num_threads, copy_trees=FALSE, model, link, rho, rconditional) -> rcpp_mcem -> emphasis::mcem -> E_step (TBB, thinning augmentation, logf/logg, fhat, linear weights) -> M_step (SBPLX on weighted sum) -> list(estimates[8], fhat, logf[N], logg[N], rejected*, time ms). Driver returns list(mcem = data.frame(par1..par8, fhat, delta_max, rejected, num_trees, time), pars[8], iterations, stop_reason, loglik_var, final_IS). .run_mcem returns list(pars, loglik = last finite fhat, loglik_var, details = raw). estimate_rates contracts pars, subtracts cond_fun(pars8) from loglik (mcem only), computes AIC, returns class 'emphasis_fit' with details = raw$details (so fit$details$mcem, $final_IS, $stop_reason, $loglik_var are what diagnose_mcem reads, diagnostics.R:373-417).

Time direction: R side works in ages (crown age first, decreasing to 0 at present); C++ E_step converts to forward time from crown (0) to present (b_0) in create_tree, so node.brts inside C++ trees are forward times and the last node is a present-day sentinel. The R driver never sees augmented trees (copy_trees=FALSE); only logf/logg/fhat/estimates return.

Per-iteration index convention in the mcem table: row k holds theta_k (post M-step) next to fhat evaluated at theta_{k-1} (pre M-step). Failed iterations produce no row, so nrow(mcem) = number of successful iterations, not of loop passes.
invariants_assumed: brts are ultrametric branching AGES sorted decreasing with the crown age first; number of tips = length(brts) + 1 (inference.R:259).
Compact bound vectors have length 2 + 2*sum(model_bin) and follow the order beta_0, beta_active(N,M,D order), gamma_0, gamma_active; lower_bound <= upper_bound elementwise (never checked).
Inactive 8-element slots are 0 with lb8 = ub8 = 0, and SBPLX tolerates equal lower/upper bounds on those dimensions.
The C++ E-step draws z_i from q(. | y, theta) and computes logf and logg at the same theta, so lw_i are valid IS log-weights for p(y | theta).

Rejections of type overrun/lambda are 'computational failures independent of theta' and may be dropped from the fhat denominator, while zero-weight completed trees must be included (E_step.cpp:140-143).
The M-step objective's weight scale does not matter (true only when no conditional is supplied).
cond_fun returns log P_tree(theta) (log of a survival probability, <= 0) for the 8-element parameter vector; predict_survival accepts a 1-row data.frame with .par_names columns.
MCEM with a FIXED Monte Carlo sample size and a parameter-stability stopping rule reaches a usable estimate (no sample-size growth or averaging is implemented).
The E-step never legitimately takes more than 120 s (hard-coded in E_step.cpp:73); if it does, the driver treats it as a failure and perturbs the parameters.
maxN >= sample_size for the thinning sampler (documented, not enforced; recovery doubles maxN but resets it after any success).
rho in (0,1]; values outside are silently reset to 1 inside the C++ Model (model.hpp:90), the R layer does not validate.
emphasis_cem's best_IS$fhat is already survival-conditioned, so estimate_rates must not correct it again (it does not).
The 'gam' cond object is an mgcv 'gam' from train_GAM in compact parameter space.
readme_vs_code_discrepancies: README calls the package 'Monte Carlo conditional-likelihood inference' and states ell_cond = ell - log P_theta(survival); in code conditioning is off by default (cond = NULL, inference.R:678) and, when on, the MCEM M-step applies log P_tree with weight 1 against an unnormalised weighted sum whose scale is sum_w in [1, N] (M_step.cpp:45-61, E_step.cpp:139), so the M-step conditioning is effectively ~sum_w times too weak relative to the documented objective.

estimate_rates_control roxygen says sampling: 'Currently only "dynamic_fresh" is implemented' (inference.R:53-54) while the code default is sampling = 'bdi' (inference.R:111) and README says BDI is the default.
estimate_rates_control roxygen says CEM max_iter default 20 (inference.R:75); code sets 50 (inference.R:121).

README's MCEM example uses control sample_size = 1 with model 'dd', link 'gaussian' (README.md:216-223); that combination is not BDI-supported (bdi.R:100-105) so it runs thinning MCEM with one augmented tree per M-step, and loglik_var is NA — the README does not say so.

README says MCEM 'Includes adaptive recovery: if the E-step fails, doubles augmentation attempts and perturbs toward the center' (README.md:152). True for .mcem_dynamic_fresh; the default BDI path only perturbs (bdi.R:778-788), and in the thinning path the doubled maxN is discarded after the next success (emphasis.R:89).
estimate_rates @return says method is 'mcem' or 'cem' and details come from '.mcem_dynamic_fresh or emphasis_cem' (inference.R:650-653); gam and .mcem_bdi are also possible.

estimate_rates @param init_pars says 'ignored for "cem"' (inference.R:616-617); it is also ignored for 'gam', but .validate_linear_init_pars still runs on it for any method when link is linear (inference.R:734-738).

README states the test files test-em.R / test-inference.R skip unconditionally and target earlier APIs (README.md:43); confirmed: test-em.R uses mc_loglik(), estimate_rates(lower_bound=), 'burnin' (test-em.R:12, 34-36); every C++ integration test in test-inference.R is skip()'d (test-inference.R:72, 86, 100). None of the MCEM driver logic (convergence, recovery, conditioning, loglik lag) is exercised by tests.

README says 'The best result across stages is returned' for the pipeline; inside estimate_rates the MCEM loglik is not the loglik at the returned pars (one-iteration lag, see concerns), so cross-stage comparison by loglik compares different things.

concerns.description: Conditioned M-step objective mixes an UNNORMALISED weighted sum with a unit-weight penalty: minimise -sum_i w_i logf(theta,z_i) + log P_tree(theta), where w_i = exp(lw_i - max lw) (E_step.cpp:139) so sum_i w_i ∈ [1, N]. The self-normalised conditioned EM objective is sum_i (w_i/sum_w) logf - log P_tree, i.e. the penalty should carry coefficient sum_w (≈ N when ESS is high, N = 200 by default). In the BDI path weights are normalised to mean 1 (bdi.R:796-799, sum = N) so the mismatch is N-fold there too, but with a different scale than the thinning path.
concerns.why_it_matters: With cond supplied, MCEM returns (approximately) the UNconditioned maximiser while estimate_rates reports a conditioned loglik (inference.R:820-822); pars and loglik describe different objectives and the README's conditional-likelihood claim does not hold for the MCEM stage. Also makes the two samplers inconsistent with each other.

concerns.description: Reported MCEM loglik is fhat from the LAST ROW of the mcem table, but that fhat was computed in the E-step at theta_{K-1} (before the final M-step), while pars = theta_K (emphasis.R:44-61, 92, 99). loglik, loglik_var (emphasis.R:136-142, from the same E-step) and AIC therefore describe the previous iterate, and the survival correction is evaluated at theta_K (inference.R:821), mixing two parameter vectors in one number.
concerns.why_it_matters: Under convergence the lag is small; under max_iter/time_budget/e_step_failure stops (stop_reason is not surfaced in the fit object) it is not. AIC model comparison and the pipeline's best-stage selection use this number.

concerns.description: MCEM uses a constant Monte Carlo sample size (sample_size fixed every iteration, no growth, no averaging of iterates) and declares convergence when the range-scaled max parameter change is < tol (1e-3) for patience (3) consecutive iterations. With N = 200 IS trees the iterate-to-iterate MC noise in theta is generally larger than 1e-3 of the range, so 'converged' can fire by chance on three quiet draws or never fire (stop at max_iter = 200 with a noisy final iterate). Neither the stationary-noise nor the point returned is characterised.
concerns.why_it_matters: Standard MCEM theory needs m_k -> infinity (or averaging) for the iterates to converge to the MLE; as written the returned pars is one draw from the MCEM stationary distribution around the MLE and the convergence flag is not evidence of proximity.

concerns.description: Recovery logic: on E-step failure maxN is doubled AND pars are pulled 20% toward the bound centre (emphasis.R:68-72), but on the next success maxN is reset to orig_maxN (line 89). If the failure cause is structural (sample_size close to or above maxN, high rejection rate, or the 120 s E-step limit in E_step.cpp:73), the loop alternates fail/fail/success and every failure moves the parameters toward the centre of the bounds — a systematic bias unrelated to the likelihood. maxN >= sample_size is documented but never enforced (inference.R:60-63, 365).
concerns.why_it_matters: Estimates drift toward (lb+ub)/2 on hard problems; the user sees no warning unless verbose; the returned pars after 8 failures is the perturbed vector, not the last M-step estimate (line 69, 165).

concerns.description: Hard-coded 120 s wall-clock limit inside the C++ E-step (em_cpp never passes max_time_seconds, rcpp_mcem.cpp:83-94). When exceeded with fewer than N trees, the E-step throws and the R driver treats it as an IS failure: doubles maxN (more work) and perturbs pars toward the centre. The 120 s figure is invisible from R and unrelated to ctrl$max_time.
concerns.why_it_matters: On large trees / single-thread runs a slow-but-healthy E-step is misclassified as collapse and the parameters are corrupted; behaviour depends on machine speed.

concerns.description: loglik_var is the bootstrap variance of a DIFFERENT estimator than the reported loglik: bootstrap replicates use .is_fhat(bias_correct = TRUE, K = 2) = mean(lw) + log(1 + m2/2) without the zero-weight denominator (de.R:476-489, 88-100), while loglik is the C++ log-mean-exp with S = N + n_zero (E_step.cpp:143-144). print.emphasis_fit and compare_models present sqrt(loglik_var) as the MC se of loglik (inference.R:855-856, 917-919).
concerns.why_it_matters: The moment-corrected estimator's variance can differ materially from the log-mean-exp estimator's when weights are heavy-tailed, and the pairwise AIC test in compare_models (inference.R:928-942) rests on it.

concerns.description: max_lambda is hard-coded to 1e6 in the MCEM E-step call, while the package default is 500 (emphasis.hpp:40) and the GAM stage uses ctrl$max_lambda = 500 (inference.R:140, 518). The thinning proposal's lambda bound therefore differs across stages of the same pipeline, and MCEM's 'rejected_lambda' will almost never fire.
concerns.why_it_matters: Different rejection behaviour across stages changes the effective proposal and the fhat denominator; the control list offers no way to set it for MCEM.

concerns.description: On an E-step failure prev_pars is not updated to the perturbed pars and streak is not reset (lines 64-85 'next' before lines 93-122). The next successful delta_max compares theta_k with the pre-perturbation iterate, and a convergence streak can survive interleaved failures.
concerns.why_it_matters: Convergence bookkeeping is inconsistent around failures; low impact unless failures are frequent (in which case the recovery bias dominates anyway).

concerns.description: If every iteration failed, mcem is NULL, so iterations = nrow(NULL) = NULL and .run_mcem's fhat_vec is NULL -> loglik NA; stop_reason ('e_step_failure', 'max_iter', 'time_budget', 'converged') is stored only in details, never in the fit object or the print method.
concerns.why_it_matters: Callers cannot distinguish a converged fit from a max_iter or time-budget stop without digging into details.

concerns.description: .mcem_warn_estep re-runs the E-step diagnostic without rho and without the conditional (defaults rho = 1, rconditional = NULL) and with maxN = 200 fixed, then parses '<n> zero weights' from the C++ message (emphasis.hpp:93) and thresholds at n > 50 while the message text says '/200'.
concerns.why_it_matters: The diagnostic can disagree with the failing configuration (rho < 1 changes augmentation); the warning text may misattribute the cause.

concerns.description: n_pars for AIC = length of the compact vector, counting parameters the user fixed by lower_bound == upper_bound (range_vec treats them as fixed, emphasis.R:29; .run_gam excludes them from optimisation, inference.R:548).
concerns.why_it_matters: AIC over-penalises fixed-parameter models by 2 per fixed parameter; compare_models rankings shift.

concerns.description: .validate_linear_init_pars guards lambda > 0 only at the POSITIVE covariate extreme (N = n_tips, M = D = crown age). D is centred and can be negative (down to about -crown age), so a positive beta_D with negative D, or any slope sign at the other extreme, is unguarded; the comment acknowledges this (lines 263-266). It also uses '<= 0' for lambda but '< 0' for mu, and beta_0 = 0 yields new_slope = 0 with lambda still identically 0.
concerns.why_it_matters: Init can still start in an IS-collapse region for 'd'/'nd' models with the linear link, which is exactly the case the note at inference.R:740-749 warns about.

concerns.description: maxN default handling: ctrl$maxN is 2000 from defaults, so the 'max(2000, 10*sample_size)' fallback only applies if the user explicitly sets maxN = NULL; a user passing num_trees = 1000 keeps maxN = 2000 (2x), and num_trees > 2000 can never succeed without the recovery doubling (which is then reset, see the recovery concern).
concerns.why_it_matters: Silent interaction between two controls; docs say 'must exceed num_trees' but nothing enforces or scales it.

concerns.description: rho is accepted from control without validation in R (inference.R:107, 384, 404); the C++ Model silently resets rho <= 0 or > 1 to 1.0 (model.hpp:90). Also select_diversification_model and .mcem_warn_estep do not forward rho.
concerns.why_it_matters: A typo (rho = 0 or 1.5) runs a complete-sampling model without any message.

concerns.description: The per-iteration 'rejected' column and verbose 'rej=' string use only results$rejected (unhandled exceptions), not overruns/lambda/zero-weight counts; the aggregated n_rejected appears only in final_IS for the last iteration.
concerns.why_it_matters: The iteration trace under-reports IS trouble; a run with 90% zero-weight trees shows rej=0.

concerns.description: Acceptance test isfinite(log_w) && exp(log_w) > 0 counts lw = +Inf (logg = -Inf, i.e. proposal density zero but model density finite) as 'zero weight' and adds it to the fhat denominator; it also counts underflow (lw < ~-745) as zero weight even though exp(lw - max) would be representable after max-scaling.
concerns.why_it_matters: fhat is biased downward by mis-classified trees in heavy-tailed regimes; +Inf weights (proposal support failure) are silently swallowed instead of raising an error.

concerns.description: Roxygen for estimate_rates_control is stale: sampling says only 'dynamic_fresh' is implemented (default is 'bdi'); CEM max_iter documented 20, code 50; tol/patience/sd_decay/sd_min_frac/max_time/rho for CEM and the entire GAM block are undocumented.
concerns.why_it_matters: Users copying documented defaults get different behaviour.

concerns.description: BDI is the default MCEM sampler but bdi.R's M-step passes trees through m_cpp, whose pack() (rcpp_mcm.cpp:11-26) sets pd = 0, tip_start = 0, ids = -1 for every node, so the C++ loglik sees M = pd/n = 0. .bdi_supported excludes M/D models, so this is harmless today — is this the intended reason the gate exists, and does the BDI path use the same fhat/weight conventions as the thinning path (weights normalised to mean 1 vs max-scaled)?
concerns.why_it_matters: The two samplers are 'drop-in replacements' per bdi.R:715 but feed the same M-step differently scaled weights, which matters for conditioning.

concerns.description: For the gaussian link, init_pars = bound midpoint with no slope clamping. Under the gaussian link the CR rate is beta_0*exp(-1/2) (eta_cov = 0, model.hpp:127-130, README says beta_0 is the peak rate) and the covariate slopes act inside a squared term — is the midpoint a sensible start, and should the exponential link's slopes also start at 0 as the linear link's do?
concerns.why_it_matters: Starting far from the mode with a noisy fixed-N MCEM and a 200-iteration cap may end on max_iter rather than convergence.

concerns.description: xtol (ctrl$xtol = 1e-3) is nlopt's xtol_rel (relative to |x|), whereas tol (1e-3) is relative to the bound range. For slope parameters near 0, xtol_rel is a much finer stopping rule than tol; for beta_0 ~ 1 they coincide. Is the M-step optimiser's own tolerance meant to sit below the EM convergence threshold in the same metric?
concerns.why_it_matters: If the M-step stops earlier than tol in range units, the EM stability test can be satisfied by optimiser inertia rather than by likelihood stationarity.

concerns.description: CEM's sd_vec default (ub - lb)/4 is computed on the 8-element bounds, so inactive slots (lb = ub = 0) get sd 0 — fine — but the survival cond_fun and the same 8-element bounds are reused across stages while the GAM stage optimises in compact space; are the fixed-slot conventions (lb = ub = 0) guaranteed to be respected by SBPLX and by emphasis_cem's perturbation?
concerns.why_it_matters: A perturbation that moves an inactive slot away from 0 would silently change the model being fitted.

open_questions: Is the conditioned M-step objective intended to be the self-normalised Q - log P_tree (which needs a sum_w coefficient on the penalty), or was the unit coefficient chosen on purpose? The BDI and thinning paths currently differ in weight scale.
Should the reported MCEM loglik be re-evaluated at the returned pars (a fresh E-step at theta_K, as .run_cem does via best_IS) rather than taken from the E-step at theta_{K-1}?
Is a fixed Monte Carlo sample size across MCEM iterations a deliberate design (with CEM/GAM supplying the global search), or is sample-size growth / iterate averaging planned?

What is the intended semantics of the recovery reset maxN <- orig_maxN after a success, and should recovery perturbation be applied when the failure cause is the 120 s C++ time limit rather than IS collapse?
Should max_lambda for MCEM be a control entry (currently 1e6 hard-coded vs 500 elsewhere)?
Should loglik_var bootstrap the same estimator that produces loglik (log-mean-exp with zero-weight denominator) instead of the K=2 moment-corrected one?
Should n_pars exclude parameters fixed by lb == ub?
Should stop_reason / iterations be surfaced in the emphasis_fit object and its print method?
With the integration tests all skipped, what is the reference run (tree, seed, control) that established the current defaults tol = 1e-3, patience = 3, sample_size = 200, maxN = 2000?

math_as_implemented:
All formulas below are what the tested R code computes; no test evaluates any C++ quantity.

1. IS log-likelihood estimate (R/de.R:60-76), tested at test-de.R:15-25 and test-inference.R:143-159:
   lw_i = logf_i - log_q_i  (de.R:62), n_valid = length(lw), S_completed = n_valid + n_zero_weight (de.R:69).
   fhat = log( sum_i exp(lw_i - max lw) ) + max lw - log(S_completed)   (de.R:73-75)
        = log( (1/S_completed) * sum_i exp(lw_i) ).
   With n_zero_weight = 0 this is log(mean(exp(lw))), which is exactly what test-de.R:19 expects. With n_zero_weight = 5 and n_valid = 10 the difference is log(10/15) (test-inference.R:157). Empty input -> NA (de.R:64). The bias_correct=TRUE branch (de.R:88-100): ell_hat = mean(lw), d = lw - ell_hat, inner = 1 + sum_{k=2}^{K} mean(d^k)/k!, fhat = ell_hat + log(inner) -- NOT tested; it silently falls back to the standard estimator when n_zero_weight > 0 (de.R:82-86).

2. ESS (R/de.R:111-117), tested at test-de.R:27-35:
   lw <- lw[is.finite(lw)]; m = max(lw); w_i = exp(lw_i - m); ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2. Uniform lw -> n; c(100, rep(-1000, 9)) -> 1 (exp(-1100) underflows to 0). Note the non-finite entries are dropped, not counted.

3. Model resolution (R/simulate.R:254-275), tested at test-covariates.R:4-27 and test-simulate.R:58-68:
   model_bin = c(use_N, use_M, use_D). "cr"->(0,0,0), "dd"->(1,0,0), "d"->(0,0,1), "nd"->(1,0,1), "rd"->(0,0,1), "ep"->(0,0,1). Formula terms (upper-cased) map N->slot 1, D/EP/E->slot 3 (simulate.R:282); anything else errors. A numeric vector is accepted iff length 3 and all in {0,1} (simulate.R:268-272), so c(1,1,0) (M active) passes.

4. Compact <-> 8-slot parameter layout, tested at test-covariates.R:52-58, test-inference.R:15-22, test-simulate.R:70-75:
   8-slot layout: pars8 = (beta_0, beta_N, beta_M, beta_D, gamma_0, gamma_N, gamma_M, gamma_D) (simulate.R:296).
   .expand_pars (simulate.R:298-310): expected_n = 2 + 2*sum(model_bin); active = which(model_bin==1); n_lam = 1 + |active|;
     beta  = (pars[1], 0, 0, 0); beta[active+1]  = pars[2 : n_lam]
     gamma = (pars[n_lam+1], 0, 0, 0); gamma[active+1] = pars[(n_lam+2) : length(pars)]
     pars8 = c(beta, gamma).
   .contract_pars (inference.R:347-352): lam = (pars8[1], pars8[active+1]); mu = (pars8[5], pars8[active+5]); c(lam, mu).
   Check: model (1,0,0), compact (0.5,-0.01,0.1,0.02) -> pars8 (0.5,-0.01,0,0,0.1,0.02,0,0) (test-inference.R:16-21, consistent). For model (1,1,1) expand is the identity map, so the test-covariates.R:52-58 "round trip" exercises no reordering.

5. Parameter names / labels (inference.R:235-247, 949-954), tested at test-covariates.R:29-50 and test-inference.R:5-29: names = c("beta_0", "beta_N"[mb1], "beta_M"[mb2], "beta_D"[mb3], "gamma_0", "gamma_N"[mb1], "gamma_M"[mb2], "gamma_D"[mb3]); label = "CR" if no slot active else paste(c("N","M","D")[active], collapse=" + ").

6. AIC table (inference.R:908-924), tested at test-inference.R:117-130 (structure only): rows sorted by AIC; delta_AIC_i = AIC_i - min AIC; AICw_i = exp(-delta_i/2) / sum_j exp(-delta_j/2). Pairwise test when every fit has loglik_var (inference.R:928-942, untested): T_ij = AIC_i - AIC_j, Var(T_ij) = 4(Var(l_i)+Var(l_j)), p_ij = 2*Phi(-|T_ij|/sqrt(Var T_ij)). Note T_ij is looked up by label after sorting: tab$AIC[tab$model == nms[i]] (inference.R:933).

7. Survival GAM (gam.R:37-67), tested at test-gam.R:13-45: survived_i = 1[status_i == "done"]; formula survived ~ s(p_1) + ... + s(p_k) over parameters with >1 unique value (or te(p_a, p_b) over all pairs for spline_type="bivariate"); mgcv::gam(family=binomial). predict_survival = predict(gam, newdata, type="response") (gam.R:81).

8. Likelihood-surface GAM (gam.R:867-910), tested at test-gam.R:47-72: drop rows with non-finite fhat; need >= 10; univariate terms s(p, k=max(3, min(n_unique(p), 10))); bivariate te(p_a, p_b, k=c(max(3,min(n_u,5)), ...)); mgcv::gam(fhat ~ ..., family=gaussian).

9. GAM MLE (gam.R:936-971), tested at test-gam.R:74-92: par_names default = names(gam_fit$var.summary); start = training row with max fitted(gam); optim(method="L-BFGS-B", lower, upper) minimising -predict(gam, newdata=pars, type="response"); returns pars, loglik = -opt$value, convergence code. Test expects the argmax of -5(x-0.5)^2-3 on [0.1,1] to land in (0.3,0.7) and convergence==0.

10. Documented-but-untested formulas (README / index.html): lambda(s,t) = f(beta_0, beta_N N(t) + beta_D D_s(t)) with links linear max(0, beta_0+eta), exponential exp(beta_0+eta), gaussian beta_0*exp(-(eta-1)^2/2) (README.md:81-94; C++ counterparts inst/include/model.hpp:66-74, 117-166 -- only the link-name mapping linear=0, exponential=1, gaussian=2 at R/simulate.R:247-251 is code I verified); D_s = I_s - M with sum_s D_s = 0 (README.md:101); L_theta = int f_theta(y_obs, z) dz estimated by (1/S) sum w_i (README.md:118-124); l_cond = l - log P(survival) (README.md:161); rho factor n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1-rho) (README.md:168; model.hpp:456 has a "Sampling terms" block I did not audit). None of these has a test.
data_flow:
Test flow: tests/testthat.R loads the installed emphasis (under R CMD check / CI) or the load_all'd source (devtools::test) and runs the 7 files. Inputs to the running tests are hand-built objects only: numeric brts vectors (test-inference.R:33, test-de.R:9), synthetic pars matrices and status lists (test-gam.R:17-23), synthetic surfaces data.frame(beta_0, [gamma_0], fhat, n_trees) (test-gam.R:49-51, 62-67, 80-84), and fake structure(list(pars, loglik, loglik_var, n_pars, AIC, method, model, details), class="emphasis_fit") objects (test-inference.R:112-124, 133-135; test-gam.R:109-122). Outputs checked: integer model_bin vectors c(use_N,use_M,use_D) (1-based R slots), compact parameter vectors ordered (beta_0, beta_active..., gamma_0, gamma_active...), the 8-slot vector, character name vectors, scalar fhat/ESS, mgcv gam objects, data.frame columns, printed text. brts convention as tested: .extract_brts returns branching times sorted decreasing (crown age first) (inference.R:216-232; test-inference.R:31-38). module: cem-gam-pipeline (R/de.R, R/gam.R, R/pipeline.R; C++ entry points src/rcpp_mce.cpp [augment_trees], src/loglik.cpp [eval_logf], src/E_step.cpp; dispatch glue in R/inference.R .run_cem/.run_gam/.build_cond_fun)
purpose: Produce initial parameter values and an exploratory likelihood fit before MCEM. Three pieces: (1) auto_bounds() finds a search box by bisection on forward-simulation feasibility and trains a binomial survival GAM used as a conditioning term; (2) the GAM stage evaluates the IS log-likelihood on an LHS grid, smooths it with an additive Gaussian GAM and maximises the smooth with L-BFGS-B; (3) the cross-entropy method (emphasis_cem) evolves a population of 8-element parameter particles scored by an IS log-likelihood estimate fhat, keeps an elite fraction, perturbs with a Gaussian whose SD decays when the best fhat stops improving, and finishes with a "stable" re-evaluation of the final elites and a softmax-weighted parameter mean. emphasis_pipeline() sequences bounds -> gam -> cem -> mcem and returns the most refined stage that produced a finite loglik.

key_functions.name: .is_fhat
key_functions.role: IS log-likelihood estimate from per-tree logf and logg: log-mean-exp over lw=logf-logg with denominator n_valid+n_zero_weight; optional moment-series bias correction truncated at K

key_functions.name: .ess_from_lw
key_functions.role: Effective sample size (sum w)^2/sum w^2 on max-scaled weights, non-finite lw dropped

key_functions.name: .simulate_particle
key_functions.role: Wrapper around C++ augment_trees (rcpp_mce); any C++ error (including emphasis_error_E when fewer than sample_size trees were obtained within maxN attempts) becomes NULL

key_functions.name: .init_population / .init_particle_grid
key_functions.role: Uniform draw of num_points particles in the 8-dim box [lower_bound, upper_bound]; inactive slots have lb==ub==0 so runif returns the constant

key_functions.name: .eval_independent (Mode 1)
key_functions.role: For every particle with NA fhat, simulate sample_size trees at theta_i and compute fhat_i via .is_fhat; optional R-level mclapply parallelism only when sample_size>=10 and enough particles

key_functions.name: .eval_shared (Mode 2)
key_functions.role: Simulate trees at every particle, pool them, and for each particle theta_j score the whole pool with eval_logf at theta_j (both logf and logg at theta_j); bias_correct hard-coded FALSE, zero-weight counts ignored

key_functions.name: .resample_particles
key_functions.role: Elite selection: top ceiling(disc_prop * n_valid) by fhat; all fhat reset to NA; remaining slots filled by Gaussian perturbation (.perturb_value, truncated to bounds by up to 100 rejections then clamp) of randomly chosen elites

key_functions.name: .bootstrap_fhat_var
key_functions.role: B=200 bootstrap resamples of (logf, log_q) pairs, each scored with the bias-corrected K=2 estimator; returns sample variance

key_functions.name: emphasis_cem
key_functions.role: The CEM optimiser: iteration loop (eval -> conditioning subtract -> rescue escalation -> best tracking -> plateau/time stop -> resample -> SD decay), then stable final estimation (re-evaluate top elites with max(20, sample_size) trees, softmax-weighted parameter mean, final IS evaluation, bootstrap variance)

key_functions.name: .run_cem
key_functions.role: Builds sd_vec=(ub-lb)/4 if unset, calls emphasis_cem with 8-element bounds, reports loglik = best_IS$fhat (fresh evaluation at obtained_estim) with fallback to last iteration best

key_functions.name: train_GAM
key_functions.role: Binomial mgcv GAM survived ~ s(p1)+s(p2)+... (or te() pairs) on forward-simulation outcomes; survived = (status == "done")

key_functions.name: predict_survival
key_functions.role: predict.gam(type="response") wrapper

key_functions.name: auto_bounds
key_functions.role: Center from r_hat=log(n_tips/2)/T; feasibility test; Phase 1 axis bisection, Phase 2 compensatory diagonals, Phase 3 seeded random directions; bounds = min/max of feasible points +/- margin*span clamped to .wide_bounds; optional IS diagnostic; trains survival GAM on 500 LHS points

key_functions.name: .test_feasibility
key_functions.role: n_test forward simulations with max_tries=0; feasible iff >= ceiling(n_test/2) have status done and tip count in [tip_lo, tip_hi]

key_functions.name: .bisect_boundary / .bisect_direction
key_functions.role: 8-step bisection between the feasible center and the wide bound (axis) or along a unit direction (clamped to the wide box); returns last feasible point

key_functions.name: .wide_bounds
key_functions.role: Outer box from r_hat and r_max=log(50N/2)/T; log-scale intercept bounds for any link_int != 0

key_functions.name: .observed_covariates
key_functions.role: X_obs per active covariate (N -> n_tips, M/D -> mean of ALL branching times) and index bookkeeping for the compensatory diagonals

key_functions.name: .lhs_sample
key_functions.role: Latin hypercube: column j = lb_j + (perm_j - U)/n * (ub_j-lb_j) with an independent permutation per column

key_functions.name: estimate_likelihood_surface
key_functions.role: For each grid row: augment_trees at theta, eval_logf at the same theta, fhat via .is_fhat with n_zero_weight; sequential path enforces the projected time budget (stop), parallel path does not

key_functions.name: train_likelihood_GAM
key_functions.role: Gaussian mgcv GAM fhat ~ s(p, k=min(n_unique,10)) additive (default) or te() pairs; drops rows with non-finite fhat; needs >= 10 rows

key_functions.name: find_MLE
key_functions.role: L-BFGS-B on -predict(gam) starting from the grid row with the highest fitted value; returns the GAM-predicted value at the optimum as loglik

key_functions.name: .run_gam
key_functions.role: Builds LHS (n_grid) or factorial (grid_points^n_par) grid in compact space, calls estimate_likelihood_surface, subtracts log predict_survival(cond) per grid row, fits train_likelihood_GAM, find_MLE over varying dims; loglik_var = NA

key_functions.name: .build_cond_fun
key_functions.role: pars8 -> log(max(P_surv(compact pars), 1e-300)) via the survival GAM

key_functions.name: emphasis_pipeline
key_functions.role: Stage sequencing, per-stage tryCatch, MCEM init choice (cem first, else gam), final choice (mcem, else cem, else gam), stage log

key_functions.name: rcpp_mce (augment_trees)
key_functions.role: Runs emphasis::E_step with bounds +/-1e6 and returns trees, per-tree logf/logg, rejection counters

key_functions.name: E_step
key_functions.role: TBB parallel_for over maxN attempts; keeps a tree iff log_w finite and exp(log_w)>0, else ++rejected_zero_weights; stops at N valid; THROWS emphasis_error_E if fewer than N valid; 120 s hard limit when max_time_seconds==0

key_functions.name: eval_logf_cpp (eval_logf)
key_functions.role: Re-packs R tree data frames and returns logf = mdl.loglik(pars, tree), logg = mdl.sampling_prob(pars, tree) at the SUPPLIED pars

math_as_implemented:
NOTATION. Trees z_i are augmented trees drawn by the thinning proposal q(z | obs, theta). logf_i = log p(obs, z_i | theta) (model.hpp loglik), logg_i = log q(z_i | obs, theta) (model.hpp sampling_prob). lw_i = logf_i - logg_i (de.R:62; E_step.cpp:92). Parameter vectors inside emphasis_cem are the full 8-slot layout c(beta0,betaN,betaM,betaD,gamma0,gammaN,gammaM,gammaD) because .run_cem passes lb8/ub8 (inference.R:428-429, 752-753); inactive slots have lb=ub=0 (.expand_pars simulate.R:298-310), so they stay at 0. auto_bounds and .run_gam work in the compact layout c(beta_0, [beta_N], [beta_D], gamma_0, [gamma_N], [gamma_D]) (.par_names inference.R:235-246). Branching times are sorted decreasing, crown age first (.extract_brts inference.R:216-234).

C++ ACCEPTANCE AND COUNTERS (E_step.cpp:84-107). For attempt k = 1..maxN: augment, then log_w = logf - logg. Accept iff isfinite(log_w) && exp(log_w) > 0; else ++rejected_zero_weights (this counter therefore also absorbs NaN/-Inf/+Inf weights, and attempts that complete after another thread already reached N, since the zero-weight branch is not guarded by `stop`, lines 104-107). augmentation_overrun -> rejected_overruns; augmentation_lambda -> rejected_lambda; anything else -> rejected. Stop when N accepted (line 101). If accepted < N after maxN attempts, THROW emphasis_error_E (line 128-130); R sees an error, .simulate_particle returns NULL (de.R:151). Time cap: if max_time_seconds == 0 the loop stops after 120 s (line 73); rcpp_mce never passes it (rcpp_mce.cpp:61-68), so every augment_trees call has a hidden 120 s limit after which a short sample raises the same error.

IS ESTIMATE, standard (.is_fhat, de.R:62-75). With n_valid = length(lw), S = n_valid + n_zero_weight (line 69):
  fhat = log( sum_{i=1}^{n_valid} exp(lw_i - max lw) ) + max lw - log S  =  log( (1/S) sum_i exp(lw_i) ).
Returns NA if n_valid == 0 or max lw is not finite (lines 64, 74). Note: with sample_size = 1 (the CEM default, inference.R:126) this is lw_1 - log(1 + n_zero) — one IS draw.

IS ESTIMATE, bias-corrected (.is_fhat, de.R:82-100), used only when bias_correct=TRUE AND n_valid>1 AND n_zero_weight==0:
  ell_hat = mean(lw);  d_i = lw_i - ell_hat;  m_k = mean(d^k);
  fhat_BC,K = ell_hat + log( 1 + sum_{k=2}^{K} m_k / k! ),  default K=2  ->  ell_hat + log(1 + m_2/2).
  NA if 1 + sum <= 0 (line 98). Exact identity when K -> infinity (mean exp(d) = sum_k m_k/k!); K=2 is the truncation. Note this is NOT mu + sigma^2/2 as the roxygen claims (de.R:42-43); it equals that only to first order in m_2.

ESS (de.R:111-117). Drop non-finite lw; w_i = exp(lw_i - max lw); ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2.

BOOTSTRAP VARIANCE (de.R:476-489). For b = 1..B (B=200): idx ~ sample(n, n, replace=TRUE); v_b = fhat_BC,2(logf[idx], log_q[idx]) with n_zero_weight = 0. Return var(v_b over finite b), NA if fewer than 2. This is the variance of the bias-corrected estimator, while the reported loglik is the standard estimator (de.R:866-867).

CONDITIONING. cond_fun(pars8) = log max(P_surv(theta_compact), 1e-300) where P_surv = predict.gam(survival_gam, type="response") (inference.R:333-345). In CEM: fhat_i <- fhat_i - cond_fun(theta_i) applied to every valid particle each iteration (de.R:651-655) and to the final elites and the final estimate (de.R:821-822, 868-870). In GAM: surface$fhat <- fhat - log(P_surv) with no 1e-300 floor (inference.R:527-530). In MCEM: subtracted once at the end in estimate_rates (inference.R:820-822).

MODE 1 (independent) fhat (de.R:230-248): for particle i, trees z ~ q(.|obs, theta_i), fhat_i = .is_fhat(logf(z, theta_i), logg(z, theta_i), bias_correct, n_zero_weight = rejected_zero_weights_i).

MODE 2 (shared) fhat (de.R:317-357): pool Z = union over particles k of {z ~ q(.|obs, theta_k)}; for each particle j, fhat_j = log( (1/|Z|) sum_{z in Z} exp( logf(z, theta_j) - logg(z, theta_j) ) ). Both terms at theta_j (loglik.cpp:84-85); the density the tree was actually drawn from, q(.|theta_k), is never used; n_zero_weight is not passed (denominator = |Z|).

CEM ITERATION (emphasis_cem, de.R:639-754), k = 1..max_iter:
  1. Evaluate all particles with NA fhat (all of them after iteration 1, since .resample_particles resets every fhat to NA, de.R:418, 442).
  2. Subtract cond_fun.
  3. Rescue: while all fhat are NA: maxN <- 10*maxN, max_missing <- 10*max_missing; abort with stop_reason "all_failed" once maxN > 10000 (de.R:659-674). The escalated limits persist for later iterations.
  4. If any overrun occurred this iteration: max_missing <- 1.1 * max_missing (de.R:677).
  5. best_loglik[k] = max valid fhat; best_pars[k,] = argmax (de.R:683-685).
  6. improvement = best_loglik[k] - best_loglik[k-1]; improving = improvement >= tol; plateau_count = 0 if improving else +1 (de.R:698-701). Note best_loglik[k] is the max over re-drawn noisy fhat values, so "improvement" mixes MC noise with search progress.
  7. Stop (adaptive): plateau_count >= patience AND all(sd_vec <= sd_floor(1+1e-8)) (de.R:705-708). Stop (legacy sd_decay=NULL): plateau_count >= patience (de.R:712). Stop: elapsed > max_time -> "time_budget" (de.R:719-726). Otherwise "max_iter".
  8. Resample: valid = !is.na(fhat); k_e = max(1, ceiling(disc_prop * n_valid)); elites = top k_e by fhat; n_add = num_points - k_e new particles: source elite ~ Uniform(elites); new_j = elite_j + N(0, sd_vec_j) truncated to (lb_j, ub_j) by rejection (100 tries) then clamped (de.R:382-389, 427-439). clear_cache = shared_trees (de.R:730).
  9. SD schedule (adaptive, de.R:733-737): if !improving: sd_vec <- max(sd_decay * sd_vec, sd_floor), with sd_floor = sd_min_frac * sd_vec_initial (de.R:603). Defaults sd_decay = 0.85, sd_min_frac = 0.01 (inference.R:131-132), sd_vec_initial = (ub8 - lb8)/4 (inference.R:421). Reaching the floor needs ceil(log(0.01)/log(0.85)) = 29 non-improving iterations. Legacy: sd_vec <- sd_vec - sd_vec_initial/max_iter every iteration (de.R:605, 740).

STABLE FINAL ESTIMATION (de.R:793-886): from final_pop (population snapshot BEFORE the last resample, de.R:694), n_elites = max(1, ceiling(disc_prop * n_valid)); n_final_trees = max(20, sample_size) (de.R:800); for each elite e: fhat_e = .is_fhat(logf, logg, n_zero_weight = rejected_zero_weights) - cond_fun(theta_e), computed WITHOUT bias_correct (de.R:819-820), with maxN = max(input$maxN, 5 * n_final_trees) and the possibly escalated max_missing. Weights w_e = exp(fhat_e - max fhat) / sum (de.R:837-838). obtained_estim = sum_e w_e * theta_e (a weighted mean in the 8-dim parameter space, de.R:839); if only one finite elite, that elite; if none, best_pars[k_ran,] (de.R:844-848). Then one more draw of n_final_trees trees at obtained_estim: best_IS$fhat = .is_fhat(...) - cond_fun, ESS, loglik_var = .bootstrap_fhat_var (de.R:852-886). .run_cem reports loglik = best_IS$fhat, else last best_loglik, else NA (inference.R:457-463).

AUTO_BOUNDS (gam.R:133-396). T = max_t (crown age), N = n_tips (length(brts)+1 for a numeric vector). r_hat = log(max(N,2)/2)/max(T,0.1); mu_hat = 0.2 r_hat; lam_hat = 1.2 r_hat (gam.R:166-168). Center: if link_int == 0 (linear) c(lam_hat, 0..., mu_hat, 0...); ELSE (link_int 1 exponential AND 2 gaussian) c(log(max(lam_hat,1e-4)), 0..., log(max(mu_hat,1e-6)), 0...) (gam.R:170-179). Feasibility(theta) := at least ceiling(n_test/2) of n_test forward simulations (max_tries = 0, max_lin = max(20N, 500)) end with status "done" and tip count in [max(2, floor(0.1N)), ceiling(10N)] (gam.R:161-163, 401-416); "done" means both crown lineages alive at T and lineage count < max_lin (general_tree.hpp:175, 290). Phase 1: for each compact axis j, bisect 8 steps between center[j] (assumed feasible) and wide$ub[j] / wide$lb[j]; keep last feasible value (gam.R:230-242, 456-481). Phase 2: for each active covariate with X_obs (N -> n_tips; M or D -> mean of all branching times, gam.R:557-565, 579-583), for slopes s in unique(X_obs, X_obs/2, X_obs/5, X_obs/20, 1, 0.1), direction (1, -s)/norm in the (intercept, coeff) plane, for lambda and for mu blocks, bisect along +/- direction within the wide box (gam.R:253-312, 603-646). Phase 3: n_random = max(4, n_pars) unit directions drawn with set.seed(12345) (RNG state saved/restored, gam.R:318-341). Bounds: lb = min over feasible points, ub = max; span = max(ub-lb, 1e-6); lb = max(lb - margin*span, wide$lb), ub = min(ub + margin*span, wide$ub), margin default 0.5 (pipeline passes 0.5) (gam.R:344-352). Wide box (gam.R:661-691): r_max = log(50N/2)/T; lam_hi = max(r_max + 0.5 r_hat, 0.1), times 5 if any covariate active; lam_lo = max(0.1 r_hat, 1e-4); cov_hi = max(0.3, 3|r_hat|); linear: beta_0 in [lam_lo, lam_hi], slopes in [-cov_hi, cov_hi], gamma_0 in [0, 0.9 lam_hi]; link_int != 0: beta_0 in [log lam_lo, log lam_hi], gamma_0 in [log lam_lo - 3, log lam_hi]. Survival GAM: 500 LHS points in [lb, ub], simulate_tree(max_tries=0), survived = (status == "done"), mgcv::gam(survived ~ s(p1)+...+s(pk), binomial) over columns with >1 unique value (gam.R:371-388, 34-68).

GAM STAGE (.run_gam inference.R:469-571; gam.R:739-971). Grid: LHS with n_total = n_grid rows in the compact box (pipeline: 150) else factorial grid_points^n_par. For each row i: augment sample_size trees at theta_i (pipeline: 200; maxN = max(2000, 200*sample_size) if NULL), logf/logg from eval_logf at theta_i, fhat_i = .is_fhat(..., bias_correct, n_zero_weight) (gam.R:766-796). Conditioning: fhat_i <- fhat_i - log P_surv(theta_i). Smooth: rows with finite fhat (>= 10 required), fhat ~ sum_j s(p_j, k = max(3, min(n_unique_j, 10))) Gaussian family (gam.R:888-909); bivariate option te(p_a, p_b, k=c(<=5,<=5)) for all pairs. MLE: start = grid row maximising fitted(gam); theta* = argmax_theta predict(gam, theta) under box constraints via optim L-BFGS-B (gam.R:953-963); loglik = predicted smooth value at theta*, not an IS estimate at theta* (gam.R:967). AIC = -2 loglik + 2 n_pars (inference.R:824) uses that smoothed value.

PIPELINE SELECTION (pipeline.R:227-239, 292-302). Init for MCEM = pars of the first of (cem, gam) with finite loglik; final result = the first of (mcem, cem, gam) with finite loglik. No loglik comparison is made across stages; the verbose line "Best init from %s (loglik=...)" reports the loglik of the stage picked by order, not by value.
data_flow: emphasis_pipeline(tree, model, link, stages, control): model -> model_bin (3 slots c(use_N, use_M, use_D); "dd"=c(1,0,0), "d"=c(0,0,1), "nd"=c(1,0,1)); link -> 0/1/2; brts = decreasing branching times. Stage 1 auto_bounds(tree, ...) returns compact named lower_bound/upper_bound, survival_gam (mgcv gam or NULL), center. Only control$bounds$margin, $n_test and top-level control$rho reach auto_bounds; bisect_steps, tip_range, train_surv_gam stay at defaults. If auto_bounds errors the pipeline returns early with best_stage "none"; if it merely fails to find a feasible center it returns the WIDE box with survival_gam=NULL and the pipeline logs the stage as "ok" (pipeline.R:133-145, gam.R:207-214). Stage 2: estimate_rates(method="gam", cond=survival_gam, control=gam_ctrl) where gam_ctrl = {n_grid=150, sample_size=200, bounds, num_threads, max_missing, max_time, verbose} (rho NOT forwarded -> stays 1.0 from estimate_rates_control). Inside: bounds expanded to 8 slots then contracted back; LHS grid in compact space; per-row augment_trees(brts, pars8, sample_size, maxN, max_missing, max_lambda=500, threads, model_bin, link, rho) -> trees/logf/logg/rejection counters; eval_logf(pars8, trees) recomputes logf/logg (identical to the E_step values since same theta); fhat vector -> minus log P_surv -> data frame (compact par columns + fhat + n_trees) -> gam -> optim -> compact MLE -> expand to pars8 -> estimate_rates contracts back, names, computes AIC. Stage 3: estimate_rates(method="cem", control=cem_ctrl) with cem_ctrl = {max_iter=20, num_particles=50, num_trees=5, bounds, ...} (rho again not forwarded); alias sync sets num_points=50, sample_size=5; maxN stays 10 (estimate_rates_control cem default); sd_vec = (ub8-lb8)/4; emphasis_cem runs on 8-slot particles; each particle evaluation is one augment_trees call requiring 5 valid trees within 10 attempts (else NULL -> NA); cond_fun(pars8) applied per particle; result obtained_estim (8-slot) + best_IS$fhat -> .run_cem loglik -> estimate_rates contracts, AIC. Stage 4: estimate_rates(method="mcem", init_pars=best_init compact, cond, control=mcem_ctrl). Final: result list with pars/loglik/AIC from the chosen stage, log data frame, fits list (raw emphasis_fit objects), bounds. C++ side: augment_trees returns trees as data frames with columns brts, n, t_ext, pd, (tip_start, focal_tip_start, id, parent_id); eval_logf re-packs them (loglik.cpp:10-41) and evaluates at whatever pars8 is supplied. Index conventions: compact position 1 = beta_0, 1+k = coefficient of the k-th ACTIVE covariate in slot order N, M, D; extinction intercept at n_lam+1 where n_lam = 1 + #active (gam.R:571-577; inference.R:274, 306). 8-slot: beta in 1..4, gamma in 5..8. Time convention: brts are ages (crown age first); E_step converts to forward times via inplace_cumsum_of_diff (E_step.cpp:19-38).
invariants_assumed: The center point returned/assumed by auto_bounds is feasible under the SAME stochastic test used during bisection (gam.R:226 comments "center is known feasible" although the test is a 5-of-10 or 3-of-5 Bernoulli event).
Feasibility along any ray from the center is monotone (feasible then infeasible), which bisection requires (gam.R:456-481, 603-646).

The set of parameters where forward simulation from the crown yields a surviving tree of comparable size >=50% of the time contains the MLE of the survival-conditioned likelihood (auto_bounds' whole premise).

For link_int != 0 the intercepts beta_0 and gamma_0 live on a log scale (gam.R:170-176, 434-440, 676-688). True for exponential; false for gaussian, where model.hpp:127-130 uses beta_0 as the natural-scale peak rate with no sign clamp.
In shared-tree mode, evaluating both p and q at the target particle gives a valid IS weight for trees drawn at another particle (de.R:294-300, 340-342).
Trees that hit max_missing / max_lambda / other failures are independent of theta and can be dropped from the IS denominator (de.R:66-68; E_step.cpp:140-142).
augment_trees always returns exactly sample_size trees or errors; partial samples never reach R (E_step.cpp:128-130).
The IS estimate at sample_size=1 (one log-weight) is an adequate objective for ranking particles (inference.R:126 default; pipeline overrides to 5).
The softmax-weighted mean of elite parameter vectors lies in a high-likelihood region (unimodality of the elite cloud) (de.R:830-839).
predict.gam of the likelihood smooth is a reliable objective outside the convex hull of the LHS points (find_MLE extrapolates freely inside the box, gam.R:959-963).

P_surv from the binomial GAM (survival to T AND lineage count < max_lin = max(20N, 500)) is the correct normalising probability for conditioning a reconstructed tree (train_GAM label at gam.R:37; general_tree.hpp:175, 290).
column names of the survival GAM predictors equal .par_names(model_bin) so that cond_fun and .run_gam can build newdata (gam.R:375, inference.R:337-340, 528).
control$rho at the pipeline level is meant to apply to every stage (pipeline.R:125 passes it to auto_bounds only).
maxN / num_threads >= 1 in E_step's blocked_range grainsize (E_step.cpp:62-65).
readme_vs_code_discrepancies: README ("Stage 1"): "A second bisection pass tightens bounds where IS augmentation fails." Code: .diagnose_is_bounds is informational only, prints warnings and never modifies bounds (gam.R:487-533, comment at 488), and it only runs when verbose=TRUE (gam.R:363-367).

README ("Estimation pipeline"): "The best result across stages is returned." Code: the first finite-loglik fit in the fixed order mcem > cem > gam is returned (pipeline.R:289-302); no loglik comparison is performed. Likewise the MCEM init is "cem if finite else gam", not the higher loglik (pipeline.R:231-239).

README ("Stage 2 -- GAM-based MLE"): describes the GAM loglik as an IS log-likelihood; code reports the GAM-predicted smooth value at the optimiser's point (gam.R:967, inference.R:569), which is not an IS evaluation at the returned parameters.
README pipeline example output shows stages bounds/gam/mcem with no cem row while the default stages vector includes "cem" (pipeline.R:60); a default run logs four rows.

README says "When the phylogeny samples only a fraction rho ... set rho in the control list": in emphasis_pipeline, control$rho reaches auto_bounds only; the gam/cem/mcem stages keep rho = 1 unless the user also nests it under control$gam / control$cem / control$mcem (pipeline.R:125 vs 168-175, 198-205, 249-257; inference.R:107).

README table says the linear link is max(0, beta_0 + eta) and the gaussian link uses beta_0 as the peak rate; auto_bounds treats gaussian exactly like exponential (log-scale intercept bounds), so the README example emphasis_pipeline(bird.orders, model="dd", link="gaussian") searches beta_0 mostly over negative values (gam.R:170-176, 676-688).

Roxygen for .is_fhat (de.R:41-43) says the K=2 correction is "equivalent to the log-normal correction mu + sigma^2/2"; the code computes ell_hat + log(1 + m_2/2), which equals that only for small m_2.
Roxygen for emphasis_cem @return says converged is one of "annealing", "plateau", "max_iter" (de.R:558-559); the code also returns "time_budget" and "all_failed" (de.R:672, 722).

Roxygen for emphasis_cem says loglik_var is NA if sample_size = 1 (de.R:556-557); the final evaluation always uses n_final_trees = max(20, sample_size) so loglik_var is bootstrapped even when sample_size = 1 (de.R:800, 881-885). The estimate_rates verbose text at inference.R:767-770 repeats the stale claim.

RcppExports/roxygen for augment_trees and eval_logf document model as c(use_N, use_P, use_E) and link as 0/1 only (RcppExports.R:36-37, 65-66); code uses slots c(use_N, use_M, use_D) and link 2 = gaussian (model.hpp:49, 133-139).

README says "The 55 remaining tests pass" and integration tests are skipped; for this subsystem that means emphasis_cem, auto_bounds, estimate_likelihood_surface, .run_gam and emphasis_pipeline have no executed test at all (test-de.R:43-130 all skip; test-inference.R:72-99 skip; no test file references auto_bounds or emphasis_pipeline).

concerns.description: auto_bounds, .find_feasible_center and .wide_bounds branch on `link_int == 0L` else log-scale. link_int 2 (gaussian) therefore gets center beta_0 = log(lam_hat) and bounds [log lam_lo, log lam_hi], but model.hpp:127-130 computes rate = beta_0 * exp(-(eta-1)^2/2) with beta_0 on the natural scale and no clamp, so a negative beta_0 is a negative rate. For bird.orders (N=23, T~28) lam_hat ~ 0.10 -> center beta_0 ~ -2.3. A zero/negative-rate center still passes .test_feasibility because a tree with 2 tips satisfies tip_lo = max(2, floor(0.1 N)) = 2 (gam.R:161), so the degenerate center is accepted and the box for beta_0 spans mostly negative values (lines 170-176, 434-440, 676-688).
concerns.why_it_matters: The gaussian link is the link the README recommends in every pipeline example; the search box handed to GAM/CEM/MCEM is wrong by construction for that link, and the survival GAM is trained over a region where most points have non-positive speciation rate.

concerns.description: Shared-tree mode (Mode 2) computes the weight of tree z_i (drawn from q(.|theta_k)) at particle theta_j as logf(z_i, theta_j) - logg(z_i, theta_j). The proposal density in an IS weight must be the density the sample was drawn from, q(z_i | theta_k) (or the pooled mixture (1/n) sum_k q(z_i|theta_k)); evaluating q at theta_j does not target p(obs, z | theta_j). The docstring (de.R:294-300) asserts the opposite. n_zero_weight is also dropped here (line 355) and bias_correct is forced FALSE.
concerns.why_it_matters: fhat under shared_trees=TRUE is not an estimator of log p(obs|theta_j); its argmax over particles need not be the MLE. Default is shared_trees=FALSE so the pipeline is unaffected, but the option is exposed and documented as correct.

concerns.description: control$rho is forwarded to auto_bounds only. gam_ctrl, cem_ctrl and mcem_ctrl are built from stage sub-lists plus bounds/threads/max_missing/max_time/verbose (lines 168-175, 198-205, 249-257) and never receive rho, so estimate_rates_control's rho = 1.0 applies to every likelihood evaluation.
concerns.why_it_matters: A user following the README ("set rho in the control list") gets an incomplete-sampling diagnostic in stage 1 but complete-sampling likelihoods in stages 2-4, with no warning.

concerns.description: The feasibility criterion that defines the whole search box is 'forward simulation from the crown yields a done tree with 0.1N..10N tips at least half the time'. Regions with high turnover (mu close to lambda) have low unconditional survival probability and are declared infeasible even though the survival-conditioned likelihood, which the package then maximises, is precisely designed to make those regions admissible. Phase 1-3 bisections all use this test (gam.R:401-416).
concerns.why_it_matters: The bounds systematically exclude high-extinction parameter regions before any likelihood is evaluated; the MLE of the conditioned likelihood may lie outside the box, and the survival GAM is only trained inside it (gam.R:374).

concerns.description: With sd_decay=0.85 and sd_min_frac=0.01 the SD reaches its floor only after ceil(log 0.01 / log 0.85) = 29 consecutive non-improving iterations, and the plateau stop (line 705-708) additionally requires plateau_count >= patience. The pipeline sets cem max_iter = 20 (pipeline.R:198), so the adaptive stopping rule can never fire inside the pipeline: CEM always terminates by max_iter with the SD still >= 0.85^19 ~ 4.6% of the initial (ub-lb)/4, i.e. ~1.1% of the box width, if it never improved, and larger otherwise.
concerns.why_it_matters: The 'converged' field will read max_iter for every pipeline run, and the elite cloud used for the final weighted mean is still a wide perturbation cloud rather than a collapsed one; the annealing described in the roxygen never completes.

concerns.description: obtained_estim is the softmax-weighted mean of elite parameter vectors (weights exp(fhat_e - max)). Elite fhat values are re-drawn with 20 trees and typically differ by units, so the weights are near one-hot on a noisy winner; when they are not, the mean of parameter vectors from different modes or from a ridge (lambda-mu trade-off, intercept-slope compensation that auto_bounds itself exploits at gam.R:244-250) is a point off the ridge. The final loglik is then evaluated at that averaged point (line 852-867).
concerns.why_it_matters: The reported CEM estimate can be a point no particle ever visited and whose likelihood is lower than the best elite; this is the value fed to MCEM as init and reported as the CEM stage loglik.

concerns.description: CEM default maxN = 10 (kept by the pipeline, which only overrides max_iter/num_particles/num_trees at pipeline.R:198). In the pipeline each particle needs 5 valid trees within 10 augmentation attempts; E_step.cpp:128-130 throws when fewer than N are valid, .simulate_particle turns that into NULL (de.R:151), and the particle gets fhat = NA and is silently excluded from the elite selection (de.R:410). Only the all-NA case triggers escalation (de.R:659).
concerns.why_it_matters: Particles in regions where augmentation is harder (low lambda, high mu, boundary of the box) are dropped at a rate that depends on theta, which acts as an undocumented, theta-dependent filter on the search rather than a likelihood; the estimate is pulled toward easy-to-augment parameters.

concerns.description: grainsize = maxN / num_threads is integer division and is passed to tbb::blocked_range. With the CEM default maxN = 10 and num_threads = detectCores()-1 on a >=12-thread machine (whitebox has 32), grainsize is 0. In .eval_independent the R-parallel path (which would pass 1 C++ thread) is disabled whenever sample_size < 10 (de.R:223-227), so the default CEM sends all threads to C++. TBB asserts grainsize > 0 in debug builds; release behaviour of a zero grainsize is undefined by the documented contract.
concerns.why_it_matters: Potential crash or hang on the fleet's larger machines with default CEM settings; unobservable on a 10-core Mac.

concerns.description: The GAM stage's loglik is the smooth's predicted value at the L-BFGS-B optimum (find_MLE), not an IS estimate at those parameters. train_likelihood_GAM's default is an additive model sum_j s(p_j) (line 888-894), which cannot represent the lambda-mu or intercept-slope ridges that dominate these likelihoods; the optimum of an additive fit to a ridged surface is generally not on the ridge. This value is turned into AIC (inference.R:824), printed in the pipeline log next to CEM/MCEM values, and used in the README's model-comparison example with stages = c("bounds","gam").
concerns.why_it_matters: Cross-stage and cross-model AIC comparisons on the GAM stage compare smoothed surrogate maxima with different grids and different per-model bounds, not likelihoods.

concerns.description: The stage log presents loglik/AIC per stage side by side, but the values are not comparable: GAM = smoothed surrogate maximum (200 trees/grid point); CEM = log-mean-exp over 20 trees at a weighted-mean point (downward Jensen bias grows as trees decrease); MCEM = 200-tree E-step fhat. All three subtract the same log P_surv when cond is present, but the pipeline neither compares them nor warns; selection is by fixed order (lines 289-302).
concerns.why_it_matters: Readers of result$log will read the CEM stage as 'worse' than MCEM even when the parameters are essentially identical, and any external comparison across stages (or across models fitted with different stages succeeding) is invalid.

concerns.description: When auto_bounds cannot find a feasible center it warns and returns the wide box with survival_gam = NULL and center = NULL (gam.R:207-214). The pipeline logs the bounds stage as "ok" and proceeds with cond = NULL, so the later stages run unconditioned on the widest box; result$cond is FALSE but nothing in the log flags the downgrade.
concerns.why_it_matters: A silent change of the estimand (unconditioned vs conditioned likelihood) between runs of the same call.

concerns.description: loglik_var is the bootstrap variance of the bias-corrected K=2 estimator (line 483: bias_correct = TRUE), while the reported loglik (best_IS$fhat, line 866) is the standard log-mean-exp estimator with the zero-weight denominator; the bootstrap also ignores n_zero_weight. compare_models uses this variance for its Gaussian AIC test (inference.R:927-940).
concerns.why_it_matters: The variance describes a different estimator from the point estimate it is attached to.

concerns.description: The user-facing bias_correct option only affects Mode 1 search-time fhat (line 240). The final elite re-evaluation (line 819-820) and the final estimate (line 866-867) call .is_fhat without bias_correct, and Mode 2 hard-codes FALSE (line 355).
concerns.why_it_matters: bias_correct = TRUE changes the search but not the reported loglik, contrary to the documentation of the option (de.R:533-534).

concerns.description: .observed_covariates takes sorted_brts[seq_len(min(n_tips, length(sorted_brts)))]; since n_tips = length(brts)+1 this is every branching time, so mean_pendant = mean(brts), not a mean pendant age (the comment at lines 553-559 describes something else). It sets X_obs for the M and D compensatory slopes.
concerns.why_it_matters: Phase 2 diagonal directions for D models are scaled by an unrelated quantity; exploratory only, but it makes the 'compensatory' rationale false for D.

concerns.description: .run_gam subtracts log(p_tree) with no floor; predict.gam on the binomial response can return values numerically 0 near the box edge, giving fhat = +Inf... actually -log(0) = +Inf so fhat becomes +Inf, which is.finite drops silently (line 532, gam.R:871). cond_fun floors at 1e-300 (inference.R:344) so CEM/MCEM behave differently at the same points.
concerns.why_it_matters: Grid rows with the lowest survival probability are removed from the smooth rather than penalised, so the GAM surface is biased toward the interior.

concerns.description: Verbose sd% = mean(sd_vec / (sd_floor / sd_min_frac)); inactive 8-slot dimensions have sd_vec = 0 and initial sd = 0, giving 0/0 = NaN, so the mean is NaN for every model (every model has at least beta_M/gamma_M inactive).
concerns.why_it_matters: The iteration trace always prints sd=NaN%, hiding the one diagnostic of the annealing state.

concerns.description: rcpp_mce calls E_step without max_time_seconds, so the default 0 selects a hidden 120 s cap; when it trips, the sample is short and E_step throws, which R turns into NULL / NA fhat with no message distinguishing it from augmentation failure.
concerns.why_it_matters: On slow trees (large N, high max_missing after escalation at de.R:660,677) the CEM can silently lose all particles and report all_failed for a reason unrelated to the parameters.

concerns.description: Rescue escalation multiplies input$max_missing by 10 up to three times (1e4 -> 1e7) and the per-iteration overrun rule multiplies by 1.1 without bound; both persist into the final evaluation (line 813, 857). max_missing is passed through as.integer.
concerns.why_it_matters: Later iterations and the final 20-tree evaluation can run with augmentation limits orders of magnitude larger than the user set, changing runtime and which trees are 'valid'.

concerns.description: .check_time_budget stops with an error when the projected total exceeds max_time (inference.R:151-166); it is applied only on the sequential path of estimate_likelihood_surface. The parallel path (mclapply, lines 808-823) has no budget. In the pipeline the error is caught as 'GAM FAILED' with the partial surface discarded.
concerns.why_it_matters: Behaviour of the time budget depends on num_threads and sample_size (which decide the path), and a nearly complete grid is thrown away rather than used.

concerns.description: train_GAM and train_likelihood_GAM print with cat() unconditionally (gam.R:65, 907), ignoring the verbose flag that every caller threads through.
concerns.why_it_matters: Cosmetic; breaks quiet runs.

concerns.description: The denominator S = n_valid + n_zero_weight with sampling that STOPS at n_valid = N successes is an inverse-binomial design; (1/S) sum w is not the plain-mean IS estimator and its bias is O(1/N). The C++ counter also includes attempts that finish after `stop` was set (E_step.cpp:104-107, not guarded), so n_zero_weight can exceed the number of attempts made before the N-th success.
concerns.why_it_matters: Small but theta-dependent bias in fhat, largest at sample_size = 1 where the estimator is lw_1 - log(1 + n_zero).

concerns.description: The survival label is status == "done", i.e. both crown lineages alive at T (general_tree.hpp:290) AND lineage count never reached max_lin = max(20 n_tips, 500) (general_tree.hpp:175). P_surv therefore includes an upper truncation that is not part of the conditioning event for a reconstructed tree, and it is trained only inside the detected box.
concerns.why_it_matters: Whether log P_surv is the right normaliser for 'conditioned on survival' depends on this definition; the README states the plain survival event.

concerns.description: Plateau detection compares best_loglik[k] to best_loglik[k-1], both maxima of freshly re-drawn noisy fhat values over ~50 particles (all fhat reset each iteration, de.R:418). With 1-5 trees per particle the MC noise of a single fhat is several units, so 'improvement >= 1e-4' is essentially a coin flip and the SD decay schedule is driven by noise rather than search progress.
concerns.why_it_matters: Determines whether the annealing ever behaves as documented.

concerns.description: MCEM is initialised from the CEM point whenever CEM produced a finite loglik, regardless of the GAM result and regardless of the two loglik values; the comment justifies this by 'GAM with low sample_size can produce misleading optima' while the pipeline gives GAM 200 trees per grid point and CEM 5 trees per particle.
concerns.why_it_matters: The rationale in the comment does not match the defaults set a few lines above.

concerns.description: mclapply forks workers that call the C++ augmenter; the C++ RNG source is not visible in rcpp_mce.cpp/rinit.h (rinit.h only exports nlopt pointers). If the augmenter seeds from R's RNG the forks are fine under mc.set.seed=TRUE; if it uses a process-global std engine, forked children start with identical states.
concerns.why_it_matters: Identical RNG streams across forked particles would make the 'independent' evaluations correlated.
