open_questions: Which RNG does emphasis::augment_tree use, and is it re-seeded per forked child in .eval_independent's mclapply path (de.R:259-263)?

What does the forward simulator do with a negative rate under the gaussian link (model.hpp:129 returns a negative number; general_tree.hpp's event-time draw with a negative total rate is not inspected here)? This decides whether the gaussian auto_bounds box merely wastes the search or produces invalid trees.
Is the survival event for conditioning intended to be 'both crown lineages survive to T' (general_tree.hpp:290) with the max_lin truncation, and is it the same event the MCEM M-step conditions on?
Was the shared-tree mode ever validated against the independent mode on a known-answer tree (the tech report referenced at E_step.cpp:142 is not in the repo)?
For the pipeline's cem stage, is maxN = 10 with num_trees = 5 intentional, or an artefact of the 1-tree default (inference.R:126-128)?
Are cross-stage logliks in result$log meant to be comparable (the print method marks the chosen stage with '*' but shows all)?
Does anything downstream (compare_models, select_diversification_model) rely on fits from different stages of the pipeline being comparable via AIC?

module: augmentation-cpp (src/augment_tree.cpp, inst/include/augment_tree.hpp, inst/include/model.hpp, inst/include/model_helpers.hpp, inst/include/general_tree.hpp, src/div_tree.cpp)
purpose: Implements the thinning importance-sampling proposal q(z | y_obs, theta) that inserts latent extinct lineages (and, with rho < 1, unsampled extant lineages) into a reconstructed tree given only its branching times; evaluates the proposal log-density log q (Model::sampling_prob) and the complete-data log-likelihood log f (Model::loglik) on the augmented node list; and provides the forward Gillespie simulator (general_tree.hpp / div_tree.cpp) that generates trees under the same rate model and returns a DDD-style L-table. E_step.cpp (read for context) is the caller: log w = log f - log q per tree.

key_functions.name: detail::create_tree (context: caller)
key_functions.role: Converts R branching times (decreasing, crown first) to the forward-time node list: node i at t_i = b_0 - b_{i+1} (i < k-1), closing node at T = b_0; n = 2 + i; t_ext = t_ext_tip = 1e11; every other field (pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start, clade, id, parent_id) value-initialised to 0.

key_functions.name: augment_tree
key_functions.role: Entry point used by E_step: copies input tree into the thread-local pool, assigns ids 0..k-1 to non-extinction nodes with parent_id = -1, calls do_augment_tree_cont.

key_functions.name: do_augment_tree_cont
key_functions.role: The thinning loop: per inter-node interval computes envelope lambda_max = max(nh_rate(cbt), nh_rate(next_bt)), draws candidate time, accepts with prob nh_rate(t*)/lambda_max, draws extinction time, picks a parent uniformly from alive_ids, inserts species (extinct or unsampled), throws augmentation_lambda / augmentation_overrun; finally compute_pendant_pd.

key_functions.name: insert_species / insert_unsampled_species
key_functions.role: Insert a speciation node (t_ext = draw) and an extinction node (t_ext = 0) or an unsampled node (t_ext = 5e10) via lower_bound, then recompute n on the dirty range with n_after(prev) = prev.n +/- 1.

key_functions.name: make_node / make_extinct_node
key_functions.role: Node constructors for augmented nodes: speciation node tip_start = t, focal_tip_start = 0, pd = 0; extinction node tip_start = focal_tip_start = t_spec.

key_functions.name: compute_pendant_pd
key_functions.role: Post-augmentation pass: (1) tip_start = 0 if parent_id == -1 else brts for non-extinction nodes; (2) pd = calculate_pendant_pd(brts) per node; (3) focal_tip_start via an id -> current tip_start map so a missing daughter records its parent's pendant start and resets the parent's.

key_functions.name: get_next_bt
key_functions.role: upper_bound on brts: next node strictly after cbt, else tree.back().brts.

key_functions.name: augment_trees (vectorised, C++ only)
key_functions.role: One augmentation per parameter vector under tbb::parallel_for; failures -> empty tree. Not called from R (the R symbol augment_trees is rcpp_mce -> E_step).

key_functions.name: Model::nh_rate
key_functions.role: Thinning intensity at time t: lambda(proxy node, pd(t)) * n(proxy node) * (1 - rho * exp(-max(mu,1e-10) * (T - t))), proxy node = lower_bound(t).

key_functions.name: Model::extinction_time
key_functions.role: Draws lifetime: with prob (1-rho)e^{-mu r}/(1-rho e^{-mu r}) returns T+1 (unsampled sentinel), else t_spec + truncated Exp(mu) on [0, T - t_spec]; mu = extinction_rate (no D) of the node at/after t_spec with its stored pd (0 during augmentation).

key_functions.name: Model::speciation_rate / extinction_rate / *_ep, apply_link, gaussian_rate, m_cov, e_s, d_cov
key_functions.role: Rate evaluation on a node for the three links; the _ep variants add beta_D*D / gamma_D*D with D = E - M, E from e_s.

key_functions.name: Model::sampling_prob
key_functions.role: log q of the augmentation: per missing/unsampled node an event term minus log(2*tips + Ne), minus the integral of the thinning intensity (piecewise-constant per segment; exact running-sum integral for D+exponential).

key_functions.name: Model::loglik
key_functions.role: log f(y_obs, z | theta): sum log lambda over speciation nodes (excluding the closing node), sum log mu over extinction nodes, minus integral of N(lambda+mu) (piecewise constant, or exact for D+exp / D+gauss), plus n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1-rho).

key_functions.name: detail::calculate_pendant_pd
key_functions.role: P(tm) = sum over nodes with brts <= tm, not extinction, t_ext > tm of (tm - node.tip_start).

key_functions.name: detail::lower_bound_node, node_less, is_extinction/is_tip/is_unsampled/is_missing, trunc_exp, log_sum
key_functions.role: Sentinel tests on t_ext (0 / 1e11 / 5e10 / anything else = missing extinct), clamped lower_bound, rejection-sampled truncated exponential, product-accumulating log-sum.

key_functions.name: sim_tree::general_div::simulate_tree_ltable
key_functions.role: Forward Gillespie from t = 0 (crown, two lineages) to max_t with true per-lineage pendant ages (tip_start reset at parent speciation); O(1) total rate for N-only and D+exp, O(N) loop for D+linear/gauss; breaks on either crown clade dying (extinction) or N >= max_N.

key_functions.name: simulate_div_tree_cpp
key_functions.role: Rcpp wrapper: runs simulator (with internal retry loop), converts forward times to time-before-present (crown_age - start_date; end -> crown_age - end or -1), returns L-table + status.

math_as_implemented:
TIME AND INDEX CONVENTIONS
- Input brts (R) are decreasing, crown age first: b_0 > b_1 > ... > b_{k-1} (k = n_tips - 1). create_tree (E_step.cpp:19-38) maps to FORWARD time from the crown: node i (i = 0..k-2) at t_i = b_0 - b_{i+1}, plus a closing node at t_{k-1} = T = b_0. The crown itself (t = 0, two lineages) is NOT a node. n_i = 2 + i is "the number of lineages during [t_{i-1}, t_i)" (model_helpers.hpp:58), so the first node has n = 2 and the closing node has n = k + 1 = n_tips. All observed nodes: t_ext = t_ext_tip = 10e10 = 1e11, tip_start = pd = focal_tip_start = 0 (aggregate init). Tree is a vector sorted by brts (model.hpp:41).
- Sentinels (model_helpers.hpp:48-50, 105-108): is_extinction <=> t_ext == 0.0; is_tip <=> t_ext == 1e11; is_unsampled <=> t_ext == 5e10; is_missing <=> none of the above, i.e. an augmented speciation node whose t_ext holds its own extinction time in (t_spec, T).
- Simulator (general_tree.hpp): forward time t in [0, max_t], t = 0 at the crown with two lineages (labels -1 and 2, DDD convention, lines 158-159). Output (div_tree.cpp:45-51): L[,1] = crown_age - start_date, L[,4] = crown_age - end_date or -1 if alive: DDD "time before present". simulate.R:207 passes max_tries = 0 and retries in R.

THINNING LOOP (augment_tree.cpp:128-191)
State: cbt (current time, starts 0), b = T = tree.back().brts (line 133).
For each iteration while cbt < b:
  next_bt = brts of first node with brts > cbt (upper_bound, lines 80-84).
  lambda1 = dirty ? max(0, nh_rate(cbt)) : lambda2_prev     (line 138)
  lambda2 = max(0, nh_rate(next_bt))                          (line 139)
  lambda_max = max(lambda1, lambda2)                          (line 140)
  if lambda_max > max_lambda: throw augmentation_lambda       (line 141)  [bound is on the TOTAL thinning rate N*lambda*(...), not per-lineage lambda]
  t* = cbt - log(u1)/lambda_max, u1 ~ U[0,1)  (lines 143-146; if lambda_max == 0, t* = next_bt, i.e. no event)
  if t* < next_bt:  accept with prob pt = max(0, nh_rate(t*))/lambda_max, u2 < pt  (lines 148-151; pt is NOT clipped at 1)
     ext = extinction_time(t*)                                (line 152)
     alive_ids = ids of nodes with !is_extinction, brts < t*, t_ext > t*   (lines 154-161)  [observed non-crown daughters, missing alive, unsampled; the two crown lineages are never candidates]
     parent = uniform over alive_ids, or -1 if empty          (lines 162-166)
     if ext >= b: insert_unsampled_species(t*) (t_ext = 5e10; n += 1 for every later node)   (lines 167-176)
     else:        insert_species(t*, ext)  (spec node t_ext = ext; extinction node at ext with t_ext = 0; n += 1 on nodes in [t*, ext))   (lines 177-185)
     num_missing++ > max_missing -> throw augmentation_overrun; dirty = true
  cbt = min(t*, next_bt)                                      (line 188)   [on rejection the loop continues from t* with lambda1 := lambda2, i.e. envelope drops to the end-of-interval value]
After the loop: compute_pendant_pd (line 190).

nh_rate(t) (model.hpp:238-252): it = lower_bound(t) (first node with brts >= t, clamped to last). cur = *it with cur.pd := P(t) = calculate_pendant_pd(t, tree). Then
   nh_rate(t) = lambda(cur) * it->n * (1 - rho * exp(-max(mu(cur), 1e-10) * (T - t)))
with lambda/mu = speciation_rate_ep/extinction_rate_ep if model_bin[2] else speciation_rate/extinction_rate. NOTE it->n is the count in [t_{i-1}, t_i) for the node at/after t: at t exactly equal to a node's brts this is the PRE-event count.

P(t) (model_helpers.hpp:216-229): P(t) = sum_{nodes j: brts_j <= t, !is_extinction, t_ext_j > t} (t - tip_start_j). With tip_start = 0 for observed nodes this is k_obs(t) * t + sum_{missing alive} (t - tip_start) where k_obs(t) = number of observed nodes with brts <= t (crown lineages contribute nothing; each observed daughter contributes as if alive since the crown). Verified numerically: observed node at t = 0.05197 with one earlier missing node has pd = 0.10394 = 2 * 0.05197.

COVARIATES ON A NODE (model.hpp:143-190)
   N = node.n ;  M = node.pd / node.n (0 if n == 0) ;
   E = brts - tip_start           if is_extinction(node)
     = brts - focal_tip_start     if parent_id >= 0
     = pd / n = M                 otherwise (observed nodes, and augmented nodes with no parent)  => D = 0
   D = E - M.
compute_pendant_pd (augment_tree.cpp:45-77): pass 1: for non-extinction nodes tip_start = (parent_id == -1) ? 0 : brts; focal_tip_start = 0. pass 2: pd = P(brts) (includes the node itself: +0 for missing nodes with parent, +brts for observed nodes and for missing nodes with parent_id == -1). pass 3 (time order): extinction node -> focal_tip_start = tip_start (= t_spec), erase id; speciation node with parent_id >= 0 -> focal_tip_start = alive_ts[parent] (parent's current pendant start), then alive_ts[parent] = brts; every speciation node registers alive_ts[id] = brts. Observed nodes never have a parent, so an observed lineage's pendant start is only ever reset by a MISSING daughter, never by its own later observed speciations.

LINKS (model.hpp:117-130, 148-212; general_tree.hpp:104-140 identical)
   linear (0):      rate = max(0, eta),  eta = beta_0 + beta_N N + beta_M M [+ beta_D D]
   exponential (1): rate = exp(eta)
   gaussian (2):    rate = beta_0 * exp(-(eta_cov - 1)^2 / 2),  eta_cov = beta_N N + beta_M M [+ beta_D D]  (intercept multiplies, not inside)
   mu likewise with pars[4..7]. Parameter slots: pars = {beta_0, beta_N, beta_M, beta_D, gamma_0, gamma_N, gamma_M, gamma_D}. model_bin[2] (use_D) is the only flag read in C++; model_bin[0], model_bin[1] are never consulted (inactive terms rely on R zero-padding, simulate.R:298-310).

EXTINCTION TIME (model.hpp:217-235)
   it = lower_bound(t_spec); mu = extinction_rate(pars, *it) [NO D term, and *it->pd is whatever is stored: 0 during augmentation, so M = 0]; mu <= 0 -> 1e-10.
   r = T - t_spec; s = exp(-mu r).
   if rho < 1: with prob p_uns = (1 - rho) s / (1 - rho s) return T + 1 (unsampled sentinel).
   else return t_spec + X, X ~ Exp(mu) rejected until X <= r (trunc_exp, model_helpers.hpp:157-165), i.e. density mu e^{-mu x} / (1 - e^{-mu r}) on [0, r].
   Product with the thinning intensity: N lambda (1 - rho s) * (1 - s)/(1 - rho s) * mu e^{-mu x}/(1 - s) = N lambda mu e^{-mu x} (extinct) and N lambda (1 - rho s) * (1-rho) s/(1 - rho s) = N lambda (1 - rho) e^{-mu r} (unsampled), which is what sampling_prob credits IF the same lambda, mu, N are used.

LOG q = sampling_prob (model.hpp:255-328), tree already augmented and pd filled
   tips := tree[0].n (= 2); Ne := 0; prev := 0; T = tree.back().brts.
   For each node i in time order, with lambda_i, mu_i = max(rate_ep or rate, 1e-10) evaluated ON THE NODE (its own n, pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start):
     dt = brts_i - prev.
     Non-(D+exp) path (line 295-296):  inte += n_i * lambda_i * [ dt - (rho/mu_i) (e^{-mu_i (T - brts_i)} - e^{-mu_i (T - prev)}) ]   (exact integral of n lambda (1 - rho e^{-mu (T-t)}) over the segment with n, lambda, mu frozen at the END node's values)
     D+exp path (lines 278-293): mean_lam_n = [ S_b * exp_integral(A_lam, beta_D, prev, brts_i) ] / dt, A_lam = beta_0 + beta_N n_i + (beta_M - beta_D) M_i, S_b = running sum_{alive s} e^{-beta_D ts_s}; inte += mean_lam_n * [ dt - (rho/mu_i)(...) ]  (so the lambda part is the exact per-lineage sum, the survival factor uses the node-level mu).
     tips += is_tip(node_i); Ne -= is_extinction(node_i).
     if is_missing(node_i):   logg += log(n_i mu_i lambda_i) - mu_i (t_ext_i - brts_i) - log(2 tips + Ne);  Ne += 1   (line 304)
     if is_unsampled(node_i): logg += log(n_i lambda_i (1 - rho)) - mu_i (T - brts_i) - log(2 tips + Ne);   Ne += 1   (line 308)
     D+exp running sums (lines 312-323): missing/unsampled node: S += e^{-beta_D brts}; extinction node: S -= e^{-beta_D tip_start} (= t_spec); observed node except the closing one: S += e^{-beta_D brts} (observed lineage's ts taken as its birth time, NOT 0, and its parent is never reset).
   return logg - inte.
   Here 2 tips + Ne = 2 (2 + k_obs(t)) + (#augmented lineages alive before this node) and N(t) = 2 + k_obs(t) + Ne_alive; the two are not equal, and the term does not equal log |alive_ids| (the actual uniform parent-choice probability, line 164).

LOG f = loglik (model.hpp:359-471)
   For each node i: dt = brts_i - prev.
     standard: inte += dt * n_i * (lambda_i + mu_i) (rates from node i, i.e. frozen at the end of the segment).
     D+exp:    inte += S_b exp_integral(A_lam, beta_D, prev, brts_i) + S_g exp_integral(A_mu, gamma_D, prev, brts_i), exp_integral(a,b,t1,t2) = e^a (e^{b t2} - e^{b t1})/b (b -> 0: e^a dt).
     D+gauss:  for each non-extinction lineage s with s.brts <= prev and s.t_ext >= brts_i: inte += gauss_integral(beta_0, base_lam - beta_D s.tip_start, beta_D, prev, brts_i) + same for mu, gauss_integral = intercept sqrt(pi/2)/b [erf(z2) - erf(z1)], z = (A + b t - 1)/sqrt2  (uses s.tip_start, which is 0 for observed lineages and for parentless augmented lineages).
     is_extinction: log_mu_sum += log(max(mu_i, 1e-300)); else if i != last: log_lambda *= lambda_i (log_sum, product with rescaling thresholds 1e-19 / 1e21).
   log_sampling = n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1 - rho), n_obs = 1 + #is_tip nodes = n_tips (k - 1 branching nodes + closing node + 1), n_unsamp = #is_unsampled (lines 459-467); no binomial coefficient.
   loglik = log_mu_sum + log_lambda - inte + log_sampling.
   IS weight (E_step.cpp:90-92): log w = loglik - sampling_prob.

FORWARD SIMULATOR (general_tree.hpp:152-295)
   State: ltable of gbranch{start_date, tip_start, parent_label, label, end_date} in float; N1, N2 = sizes of the two crown clades; sum_tip_start; for D+exp the running sums S_b, S_g (init 2).
   P(t) = N t - sum_{alive} tip_start_s (true pendant PD; line 178), E_s = t - tip_start_s (line 204, 239), M = P/N, D = E - M (lines 119-140).
   total rate: N-only: N (lambda + mu); D+exp: exp(beta_0 + beta_N N + (beta_M - beta_D) M + beta_D t) S_b + same for mu; else sum over alive lineages of lambda_s + mu_s.
   next_time = t + Exp(total_rate) (1e20 if total_rate <= 0); stop if >= max_t (finished). Event selection: N-only: uniform alive lineage, speciation with prob lam/(lam+mu); D-models: lineage weighted by lam_s + mu_s, then Bernoulli(lam_s/(lam_s+mu_s)).
   Speciation: parent tip_start := t, daughter (t, t); sum_tip_start += -old_ts + 2t; S_b += -e^{-beta_D old_ts} + 2 e^{-beta_D t}. Extinction: end_date = t, sum_tip_start -= ts, S_b -= e^{-beta_D ts}.
   Break: N >= max_N -> maxN_exceeded; N1 < 1 or N2 < 1 -> extinction (crown-conditioned survival).
data_flow: R (.extract_brts, inference.R:216-232) -> brts decreasing with crown first -> rcpp_mce (src/rcpp_mce.cpp:45-83, exported as augment_trees) or rcpp_mcem (em_cpp) -> Model(lb8, ub8, model_bin, link, rho) -> E_step (E_step.cpp:43-146): create_tree -> forward-time node list (k nodes: k-1 branching events at b_0 - b_{i+1} with n = 2+i, t_ext = 1e11, tip_start = 0, plus closing node at T = b_0 with n = n_tips) -> augment_tree copies into a thread_local pooled tree, assigns ids 0..k-1 / parent_id -1 -> do_augment_tree_cont inserts missing (t_ext = own extinction time) + extinction (t_ext = 0) node pairs and unsampled nodes (t_ext = 5e10), sharing one id with parent_id from alive_ids -> compute_pendant_pd fills tip_start/pd/focal_tip_start -> loglik and sampling_prob evaluated on the augmented list -> log w = logf - logg; trees with non-finite or zero weight counted as rejected_zero_weights; augmentation_lambda / augmentation_overrun counted separately -> unpack (src/unpack.h) to a data.frame with columns brts (forward time), n, t_ext, pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start, id, parent_id -> R .aug_to_Ltable (simulate.R:414-455) keeps rows with t_ext != 0, parent_id != -1, t_ext < 1e11; L-table birth = max_t - brts, death = max_t - t_ext or -1 for unsampled; parent label found by matching brts[pid + 2] (decreasing vector, 1-based) against L_extant[,1]. eval_logf (loglik.cpp:69-94) re-packs such data frames (missing columns default to 0 / -1) and re-scores logf/logg at arbitrary theta. Forward path: simulate_tree (simulate.R) -> .expand_pars to 8 slots -> simulate_div_tree_cpp -> general_div forward from t = 0 (crown) to max_t -> L-table in time-before-present -> R drops (1-rho) of extant tips by setting L[,4] = max_t -> DDD::L2phylo for tes/tas.
invariants_assumed: Tree vector is sorted by brts at all times; ties are inserted before equal-brts nodes (lower_bound).
node.n[i] = number of lineages during [brts[i-1], brts[i]); first node n = 2 (crown pair); insertions fix n on the dirty range only.

tree.back() is the closing node at T with t_ext = 1e11; every augmented extinction time satisfies t_ext < T (else the lineage is treated as unsampled), which is what keeps the unguarded loop in insert_species (line 101) inside the vector.
t_ext sentinels are exact double compares: 0.0 extinct, 1e11 tip, 5e10 unsampled; R must use the same literal values (bdi.R:544, 577; simulate.R:417-418 do).
Speciation and extinction node of an augmented lineage share the same id; observed nodes have parent_id = -1 and are never linked to each other (no topology is passed to C++).
tip_start = 0 for every observed lineage and for any augmented lineage whose parent_id is -1 (born before the first non-crown branching); the R BDI path documents the same convention (bdi.R:287-291).
Within an inter-node interval the thinning envelope max(nh_rate(start), nh_rate(end)) is assumed to dominate nh_rate(t); the code never checks pt <= 1.
During augmentation node.pd is 0 for every node (compute_pendant_pd runs only at the end); nh_rate recomputes P(t) on the fly but extinction_time does not.
model_bin[2] gates the D term; model_bin[0..1] are assumed to be enforced by zero-padded parameters from R.

RNG: augment loop uses thread_local std::default_random_engine, extinction_time a separate thread_local mt19937_64, simulator its own mt19937, all seeded from clock + thread id; none receive R's seed.
Forward simulator times are float; crown-conditioned survival = both crown clades non-empty.
sampling_prob and loglik must be evaluated on trees carrying the same tip_start/focal_tip_start/pd semantics as compute_pendant_pd produced; eval_logf trusts the data frame's pd column.
readme_vs_code_discrepancies: README (line ~103) says M is 'used only internally to centre D and is not a user covariate', but model.hpp:148-212 and general_tree.hpp:119-140 treat pars[2]/pars[6] (beta_M, gamma_M) as full covariate coefficients, model_bin[1] is 'use_M', and R's .pars_error_msg names beta_M; only zero-padding hides it.

README defines D_s = I_s - M with I_s 'time since it last speciated'. In inference (E_step.cpp:34, augment_tree.cpp:50) observed lineages have tip_start = 0, an observed lineage's pendant start is never reset by its own later speciations (no topology), and observed speciation events use D = 0 (model.hpp:184-185); the simulator (general_tree.hpp:264-267) does reset the parent. The covariate the estimator sees is not the covariate the generator uses.

README: thinning sampler 'Every model and link'. It runs for every model, but log q as computed in sampling_prob matches the density actually sampled only when the M and D coefficients are zero (see concerns on mu/lambda mismatch).

README: 'Poisson-thinning proposal'. The code's dominating rate is the max of two endpoint evaluations per interval (augment_tree.cpp:138-140), not a bound, and the acceptance probability is not clipped.

README: incomplete sampling 'likelihood gains the binomial sampling factor n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1-rho)'. Code has exactly those two terms (model.hpp:466) and no binomial coefficient, although n_unsamp varies across augmentations.
rcpp_mce.cpp:28 and simulate.R:87 document max_lambda as an upper bound on 'the speciation rate'; augment_tree.cpp:141 applies it to N * lambda * (1 - rho e^{-mu(T-t)}), the total thinning intensity.
rcpp_mce.cpp:31, rcpp_mcem.cpp:39 and div_tree.cpp:14 document link as 0 = linear, 1 = exponential only; link 2 (gaussian) is implemented in model.hpp:49 and general_tree.hpp:122.

general_tree.hpp:88 and div_tree.cpp:10 still name the model flags {use_N, use_P, use_E} while model.hpp:63 and README name them {use_N, use_M, use_D}; div_tree.cpp:8 uses beta_M/beta_D. Naming drift only, same slots.

README table says the thinning sampler is selected with sampling = 'dynamic_fresh' in MCEM; emphasis.R calls it with max_lambda = 1e6 (line 50, 182) while simulate_tree/.augment_tree_internal default to 500 (simulate.R:139, 468) and emphasis.hpp:40 defaults to 500 — three different defaults for the same bound.

concerns.description: The envelope at the start of each interval is evaluated with the PRE-event lineage count. lambda1 = nh_rate(cbt) (or the carried-over lambda2 = nh_rate(next_bt_prev)) calls lower_bound_node(cbt) (model_helpers.hpp:119-123), which returns the node AT cbt whose n is the count in [t_{i-1}, t_i), i.e. before the branching/insertion at cbt. After an observed branching the true count is n+1; after an augmented insertion likewise. For constant rates the true intensity just after cbt is (n+1) lambda s(cbt) > max(n lambda s(cbt), (n+1) lambda s(next_bt)) = lambda_max, so pt = nh_rate(t*)/lambda_max exceeds 1 near every interval start and is silently accepted with probability 1.
concerns.why_it_matters: The realised proposal intensity is min(nh_rate, lambda_max), but sampling_prob (model.hpp:295-296) integrates the unclipped n_i lambda_i (1 - rho e^{-mu(T-t)}) over the segment. log q is then not the density of the sampler, so the importance weights f/q are biased; the effect is largest for small N (factor (n+1)/n) and right after each branching event.

concerns.description: lambda_max = max(nh_rate(cbt), nh_rate(next_bt)) is the max of two endpoint evaluations, not a proved upper bound on nh_rate(t) inside the interval. nh_rate(t) contains lambda(M(t)) with M(t) = P(t)/N changing continuously (any nonzero beta_M/beta_D), the survival factor (1 - rho e^{-mu(T-t)}) which decreases in t, and mu(M(t)); the product is not monotone in general. After a rejection (line 188 sets cbt = t*, dirty stays false) the envelope drops to lambda2 alone. No check that pt <= 1 exists (line 150-151).
concerns.why_it_matters: Whenever the envelope is violated the accepted process has intensity min(nh_rate, envelope) while log q assumes nh_rate; the max_lambda guard (line 141) only rejects trees whose envelope is large, it does not detect envelope violations.

concerns.description: Three different mu's are used for one augmented lineage. (a) extinction_time draws the lifetime with mu = extinction_rate(pars, *it) — the non-D rate — on a node whose pd is 0 during augmentation (compute_pendant_pd runs only at augment_tree.cpp:190, make_node sets pd = 0 at line 24, create_tree leaves pd = 0), so M = 0 and no D term. (b) nh_rate's survival factor (line 247-251) uses extinction_rate_ep with pd recomputed at t. (c) sampling_prob (line 274-275) credits mu_i = extinction_rate_ep on the finished node with its final pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start.
concerns.why_it_matters: For any model with gamma_M != 0 or gamma_D != 0 (models 'd' and 'nd', which README routes exclusively to this sampler) the lifetime density credited in log q (mu_i e^{-mu_i lifespan}) is not the density the lifetime was drawn from, and the unsampled/extinct split probability in (a) does not match the (1 - rho e^{-mu(T-t)}) factor in (b)/(c). The cancellation derived in math_as_implemented only holds when all three mu's coincide, i.e. for cr/dd.

concerns.description: The lambda used for acceptance and the lambda credited in log q differ for D-models. nh_rate evaluates speciation_rate_ep on a COPY of the node at/after t (line 243): if that proxy is an observed node, e_s returns M so D = 0; if it is a missing node, e_s = brts_proxy - focal_tip_start where focal_tip_start is still 0 during augmentation (augment_tree.cpp:25), so E = brts of the proxy, not of t. sampling_prob (line 272-273) instead evaluates the finished missing node with focal_tip_start filled by pass 3 (augment_tree.cpp:60-76), so D = (t* - parent_ts) - M. Also nh_rate's P(t*) excluded the node itself while pd at line 57 includes it (+0 with a parent, +t* without).
concerns.why_it_matters: log q term log(n mu lambda) uses a lambda that was never used to accept the event. Same class of q/sampler mismatch as the mu concern; affects 'd' and 'nd' on every link.

concerns.description: For D + exponential link, sampling_prob's integral uses the exact sum over lineages S_b * exp_integral(A_lam, beta_D, ...) (a per-lineage rate sum), whereas the sampler's intensity (nh_rate, line 245-251) is n * lambda(proxy node) — a single representative lineage times N. These are different functions of t, so the integral in log q is not the integral of the intensity that generated the points.
concerns.why_it_matters: For D+exp the sampling density is internally inconsistent even before the mu issues; IS weights for the 'd'/'nd' + exponential configuration cannot be trusted without a separate check.

concerns.description: compute_pendant_pd pass 1 forces tip_start = 0 on every non-extinction node with parent_id == -1, which includes augmented lineages born before the first non-crown branching (alive_ids is empty at that time, line 163, so parent_id = -1). Verified numerically: a missing node at brts 0.0448 with parent_id -1 has tip_start = 0 and pd = 0.0448, while its extinction node keeps tip_start = 0.0448. Consequences: P(t) over-counts that lineage by t_spec; its e_s is P/N (D = 0) instead of the lineage's own age; the gaussian loglik (line 412) and calculate_pendant_pd use ts = 0 while the D+exp running sums (line 443 adds e^{-beta_D brts}, line 446 subtracts e^{-beta_D tip_start = t_spec}) use the true birth. Additionally simulate.R:420 drops all parent_id == -1 augmented rows, so these lineages vanish from the conditional-simulation tas output.
concerns.why_it_matters: Inconsistent covariates across links for the same tree, and silent loss of augmented lineages that attach to a crown lineage — common when many missing species are proposed early.

concerns.description: Because observed nodes carry tip_start = 0 (E_step.cpp:34, augment_tree.cpp:50), P(t) = k_obs(t) * t + sum_missing(t - ts): each observed daughter lineage is counted as alive since the crown, the two crown lineages are not counted at all, and observed lineages' pendant starts are never reset by their own speciations. The forward simulator computes the true pendant PD (general_tree.hpp:178, 264-267). bdi.R:287-291 documents the tip_start = 0 convention as deliberate for the BDI path.
concerns.why_it_matters: M and D evaluated by loglik during inference are not the same random variables as the M and D that generated the data in simulate_tree; estimates of beta_M/beta_D (and beta_N via the M term) are for a different covariate than the one in the paper's model statement. Needs an explicit decision or a topology-aware pendant-age computation.

concerns.description: In the D+exp running sums an observed speciation adds only the daughter (e^{-beta_D brts}) and never resets the parent, while the simulator (general_tree.hpp:270) does -e^{-beta_D old_ts} + 2 e^{-beta_D t}. Within the same file, the exponential path takes an observed lineage's ts as its birth time (line 320, 449) whereas M (via pd) and the gaussian path (line 412) take ts = 0.
concerns.why_it_matters: Mixed conventions for the same lineage in one likelihood; the exponential and gaussian links do not agree on what E_s is even at beta_D -> 0 limits.

concerns.description: The combinatorial term -log(2 tips + Ne): tips starts at tree[0].n = 2 and increments once per observed node (including the closing node), Ne counts augmented lineages alive. So 2 tips + Ne = 2(2 + k_obs(t)) + Ne_alive, which equals neither N(t) = 2 + k_obs + Ne_alive nor |alive_ids| = k_obs + Ne_alive (the set the parent is actually drawn from uniformly, augment_tree.cpp:154-166). The parent choice affects focal_tip_start and hence f for D-models, but its probability 1/|alive_ids| does not appear in log q.
concerns.why_it_matters: If this term is meant to be the number of labelled attachment points it should be derivable; as written it is inherited from the original rpd5c code and I cannot map it to the current proposal. Needs the author's intended derivation.

concerns.description: Incomplete sampling in forward simulation marks dropped tips with L[drop, 4] <- max_t. In the DDD L-table convention column 4 is time-before-present; L2phylo maps it to age - L[,4] = 0, i.e. extinct at the crown, not at the present. Verified: simulate_tree(pars = c(0.6, 0.1), max_t = 6, model = 'cr', rho = 0.5) returns tas with edge lengths down to -5.98. tes is unaffected because dropextinct removes those rows.
concerns.why_it_matters: Outside the C++ files but it is the rho interface of the forward simulator: any use of $tas or $L under rho < 1 (plots, conditional augmentation seeds via $L, tests) is wrong. Setting column 4 to 0 (extinct at present) is presumably what was intended.

concerns.description: log_sampling = n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1 - rho) omits the binomial coefficient choose(n_obs + n_unsamp, n_obs). n_unsamp varies across augmented trees z, so the coefficient is not a constant across the IS sample; whether it belongs in f depends on whether z is treated as a labelled or unlabelled history. Meanwhile the (1 - rho) per unsampled lineage cancels exactly with line 308 in q.
concerns.why_it_matters: Determines whether the rho < 1 weights are correct up to a theta-independent constant.

concerns.description: max_lambda is compared against the total thinning intensity n * lambda * (1 - rho e^{-mu(T-t)}), not the per-lineage speciation rate as documented (rcpp_mce.cpp:28, simulate.R:87). Rejections then scale with N, and the R defaults disagree (500 in simulate.R, 1e6 in emphasis.R, 500 in emphasis.hpp:40).
concerns.why_it_matters: The rejected_lambda diagnostic and the 'lambda' bisection in auto_bounds measure something other than what the docs say; large trees will hit the 500 bound at moderate lambda.

concerns.description: Two independent thread_local engines (std::default_random_engine here, mt19937_64 in model.hpp:218) and a third mt19937 in general_tree.hpp:34-43, all seeded from the clock and thread id; none takes a seed from R. std::default_random_engine is implementation-defined (minstd_rand on libstdc++/libc++).
concerns.why_it_matters: set.seed() has no effect on augmentation or forward simulation; tests and reproducibility claims cannot be exact, and a linear-congruential default engine is weak for a Monte Carlo estimator.

concerns.description: tbb::task_arena arena(num_threads) is constructed but never used (no arena.execute), here and in E_step.cpp:63, so num_threads does not limit TBB. In augment_trees grainsize = vpars.size()/num_threads is 0 when vpars.size() < num_threads (TBB requires grainsize >= 1). The vectorised augment_trees is not reachable from R (the R symbol augment_trees is rcpp_mce -> E_step -> augment_tree).
concerns.why_it_matters: num_threads = 1 does not make the sampler single-threaded; dead code with a latent grainsize bug.

concerns.description: Only model_bin_[2] is ever read; model_bin_[0] (use_N) and [1] (use_M) are ignored. An 8-vector with nonzero beta_N and model = c(0,0,0) silently fits a dd model; correctness relies on R's .expand_pars zero-padding.
concerns.why_it_matters: eval_logf and augment_trees are exported as internal functions that accept raw 8-vectors; inconsistency between model and pars is undetected.

concerns.description: trunc_exp is rejection sampling with acceptance probability 1 - e^{-mu r}; with mu clamped to 1e-10 (model.hpp:222, when the linear link gives mu = 0) a call costs ~1/(mu r) draws. The proposal rate is proportional to the same factor, so expected cost per unit time is bounded, but a single unlucky call can spin for ~1e9 iterations.
concerns.why_it_matters: Explains occasional wall-clock stalls under mu ~ 0; the 120 s E-step budget (E_step.cpp:73) is the only backstop.

concerns.description: The n-recomputation loop `for (++first; first->brts < t_ext; ++first)` has no tree.end() guard; it is safe only because t_ext < b is guaranteed by the caller (line 167 routes ext_time >= b to the unsampled branch).
concerns.why_it_matters: Any future caller passing t_ext >= T walks off the vector.

concerns.description: Simulator stores start_date, tip_start, end_date and t as float (lines 70-74, 85, 212-216); computations are done in double and truncated back. With E-dependence and the linear link, a selected lineage can have lam + mu = 0 only through floating-point fallback (line 250-256), giving bernoulli(NaN).
concerns.why_it_matters: Branching times returned to R carry ~1e-7 relative error, which can break exact-equality matching such as which.min(abs(L_extant[,1] - brts[pid+2])) in simulate.R:428 only by luck; the NaN path is an edge case.

concerns.description: compute_pendant_pd pass 2 calls calculate_pendant_pd for every node, O(N^2) per augmented tree, and nh_rate recomputes P(t) by a full scan at every candidate time.
concerns.why_it_matters: Performance only; with max_missing = 1e4 this dominates E-step time.

concerns.description: The only augmentation test is a skipped mc_loglik smoke test. There is no test that log q equals the sampler's density (e.g. rho = 1, cr model, compare IS estimate of the marginal likelihood to an analytic BD likelihood), no test of rho < 1 augmentation, no test of compute_pendant_pd conventions, and no determinism test (impossible without seeding).
concerns.why_it_matters: Every concern above is currently unfalsified by the test suite.

open_questions: What is the intended derivation of the -log(2*tips + Ne) term in sampling_prob (model.hpp:304, 308)? Is it the number of labelled attachment points from the original emphasis paper, and does it still apply now that the parent is chosen uniformly from alive_ids (which excludes the two crown lineages)?

Is the tip_start = 0 convention for observed lineages (P(t) = k_obs(t) * t) a deliberate mean-field definition of M and D for inference, or a placeholder until topology is passed to C++? The simulator uses true pendant ages, so the covariate names do not currently mean the same thing in simulation and inference.

For models 'd' and 'nd', is the thinning sampler intended to be exact (log q = true density) or merely a heuristic proposal with an approximate q? If exact is intended, the three-mu / two-lambda mismatches need to be closed; if approximate, the IS estimator is biased by design and README should say so.

Should the envelope be a true dominating rate (e.g. evaluate nh_rate with the post-event N and the survival factor at the interval start, or take max over a grid, and reject or clip pt > 1 with a corrected density)?
Is the omission of the binomial coefficient in log_sampling (model.hpp:466) intentional under a labelled-history convention?
simulate.R:221 sets L[,4] = max_t for dropped tips; is 0 (extinct at present) the intended value? tas currently has negative branch lengths under rho < 1.
Should augmented lineages with parent_id = -1 (attached to a crown lineage) keep tip_start = t_spec and be written into the L-table by .aug_to_Ltable, instead of being reset to 0 and dropped?
Is there a reason the C++ RNGs are not seedable from R (e.g. via a seed argument on augment_trees / simulate_div_tree_cpp) given the package advertises reproducible tests?

module: is-core-cpp — importance-sampling E-step / weighted M-step core (src/E_step.cpp, src/M_step.cpp, src/mcem.cpp, src/loglik.cpp, src/rcpp_mcem.cpp, src/rcpp_mce.cpp, src/rcpp_mcm.cpp, inst/include/emphasis.hpp, inst/include/precision_weights.hpp, inst/include/sbplx.hpp, src/rsbplx.cpp); f and q themselves live in inst/include/model.hpp and the proposal sampler in src/augment_tree.cpp, both read because the core is unintelligible without them.
purpose: Given branching times y_obs and a parameter vector theta (8 slots), draw N augmented trees z_i from the thinning proposal q(.|y_obs,theta), score each with log f_theta(y_obs,z_i) and log q(z_i), form IS log-weights log w_i = log f - log q, report fhat = log of the (zero-weight-inclusive) mean weight as the IS estimate of log p(y_obs|theta), and maximise the weighted complete-data log-likelihood sum_i w_i log f_theta(y_obs,z_i) over theta with NLopt SBPLX (bounded, derivative-free) to produce the next MCEM iterate. Three Rcpp entry points expose this: em_cpp (E+M in one call, used by the R MCEM loop), augment_trees (E-step only: trees + logf + logg, used by CEM and GAM), eval_logf (re-score existing trees at another theta), plus m_cpp (M-step only, used by the R-side BDI sampler).

key_functions.name: detail::create_tree / inplace_cumsum_of_diff
key_functions.role: Converts decreasing crown-first brts into forward-time nodes (s_i = T - b_{i+1}, last = T), n_i = 2+i, t_ext = tip sentinel; sorted ascending.

key_functions.name: emphasis::E_step
key_functions.role: TBB parallel_for over maxN attempts; per attempt augment, compute logf, logg, log_w; accept if finite and exp(log_w)>0; stop at N accepted or 120 s; then max-shift weights to linear via calc_sum_w and compute fhat.

key_functions.name: calc_sum_w
key_functions.role: Boost cpp_dec_float_100 sum of exp(log_w_i - max); OVERWRITES each log-weight in place with the linear max-scaled weight; returns the sum as double.

key_functions.name: objective (anonymous)
key_functions.role: NLopt objective: parallel_reduce Q = sum_i w_i * loglik(theta, tree_i); returns -Q, or -Q + log P_tree(theta) when a conditional callback is set.

key_functions.name: emphasis::M_step
key_functions.role: task_scheduler_init(num_threads); SBPLX with xtol_rel, lower/upper bounds (R-supplied, else model bounds); returns estimates, nlopt code, minf, elapsed ms.

key_functions.name: emphasis::mcem / mce
key_functions.role: mcem = E_step then M_step on E.trees/E.weights; mce = E_step only (bounds/xtol args ignored; no caller).

key_functions.name: rcpp_mcem (R: em_cpp)
key_functions.role: Builds Model(lb8, ub8, model_bin, link, rho), wraps R conditional as std::function, runs mcem, returns trees(count or 3-col df), rejection counts, estimates, nlopt, fhat, time, weights (linear max-scaled), logf, logg.

key_functions.name: rcpp_mce (R: augment_trees)
key_functions.role: E_step only with dummy bounds ±1e6; returns full 8-column tree data frames (unpack.h), logf, logg, rejection counts, time. No weights, no fhat.

key_functions.name: rcpp_mcm (R: m_cpp)
key_functions.role: Rebuilds trees from brts/n/t_ext only (pd, tip_start, ids zeroed) and takes weights as given linear multipliers; runs M_step. Only caller: R/bdi.R:820.

key_functions.name: eval_logf_cpp (R: eval_logf) + loglik::pack
key_functions.role: Re-scores a list of tree data frames at arbitrary pars: logf = Model::loglik, logg = Model::sampling_prob (optional tip_start/focal_tip_start/id/parent_id columns).

key_functions.name: Model::loglik (f)
key_functions.role: Complete-data log-likelihood: sum log mu at extinctions + sum log lambda at speciations - integral of N(lambda+mu) + rho sampling terms; exact segment integrals for D+exponential and D+gaussian.

key_functions.name: Model::sampling_prob (q)
key_functions.role: Proposal log-density: per missing/unsampled lineage log(N mu lambda) - mu*lifespan - log(2*tips+Ne), minus thinning-intensity integral.

key_functions.name: Model::nh_rate / extinction_time
key_functions.role: Thinning intensity N*lambda*(1 - rho*exp(-mu(T-t))) and truncated-exponential (or unsampled-sentinel) extinction draw; uses its own thread_local mt19937_64.

key_functions.name: do_augment_tree_cont / augment_tree
key_functions.role: Poisson thinning with envelope max(nh_rate at segment ends); uniform parent choice among alive nodes; throws augmentation_lambda / augmentation_overrun; thread_local std::default_random_engine at line 41.

key_functions.name: sbplx wrapper
key_functions.role: Thin RAII wrapper over nloptr's exported C API (function pointers resolved in rinit.cpp via R_GetCCallable); any negative nlopt_result throws emphasis_error.

key_functions.name: E_step_t / E_step_info_t / emphasis_error_E
key_functions.role: Result containers (trees, weights, logf_, logg_, counters, fhat); error carrying rejection breakdown, message always says 'maxN exceeded'.

math_as_implemented:
TIME/INDEX CONVENTIONS. Input brts is decreasing, crown age first: b_0 = T > b_1 > ... > b_{k-1} (k = n_tips - 1). E_step.cpp:19-26 rewrites in place to forward times s_i = T - b_{i+1} for i < k-1 and s_{k-1} = T; E_step.cpp:33-36 makes node i = {brts = s_i, n = 2 + i, t_ext = 1e11 (tip)} sorted ascending. node.n is the lineage count on [s_{i-1}, s_i) (model_helpers.hpp:58). The last node (s = T) is a present-day sentinel, not an event (model.hpp:436). t_ext sentinels (model_helpers.hpp:48-50, 105-108): 1e11 = observed tip, 0.0 = extinction node, 5e10 = unsampled extant; is_missing(node) = none of those (= speciation node of an augmented extinct lineage). Parameters (model.hpp:58-63): pars = (beta_0, beta_N, beta_M, beta_D, gamma_0, gamma_N, gamma_M, gamma_D), 0-based slots 0..7; model_bin = {use_N, use_M, use_D} but C++ reads ONLY model_bin_[2] (model.hpp:245-247, 256-257, 272-274, 360-361, 420-430); N and M terms always enter and are switched off only by R pinning pars and bounds to 0 (simulate.R:298-310, inference.R:752-753).

RATES (model.hpp:117-212). Covariates at node i: N = n_i; M = pd_i / n_i (pd = "pendant PD", augment_tree.cpp:56-58 via model_helpers.hpp:216-229, where initial-tree nodes have tip_start = 0, augment_tree.cpp:50); D = e_s - M with e_s = brts - tip_start for extinction nodes, brts - focal_tip_start for augmented speciation nodes with parent_id >= 0, and M (so D = 0) for initial-tree nodes (model.hpp:177-185). Linear link: lambda = max(0, beta_0 + beta_N N + beta_M M [+ beta_D D if model_bin[2]]); exponential: exp(same eta); gaussian: beta_0 * exp(-(beta_N N + beta_M M [+ beta_D D] - 1)^2 / 2); mu likewise with gamma (model.hpp:148-212).

PROPOSAL q (what is simulated, augment_tree.cpp:128-191 + model.hpp:217-252). On the current segment [cbt, next_bt): Lambda* = max(nh(cbt), nh(next_bt)), nh(t) = n(t) * lambda(t) * (1 - rho * exp(-max(mu,1e-10) (T - t))) with lambda, mu at the node covering t and pd recomputed at t (model.hpp:238-252); if Lambda* > max_lambda throw augmentation_lambda (line 141). Candidate t* = cbt - log(u1)/Lambda*, accepted with prob nh(t*)/Lambda* (lines 143-151). On acceptance: with prob p_uns = (1-rho) e^{-mu r} / (1 - rho e^{-mu r}), r = T - t*, the lineage is an unsampled extant (sentinel T+1 -> t_ext = 5e10, model.hpp:225-232, augment_tree.cpp:167-176); else t_ext = t* + TruncExp(rate mu(t*), upper r) by rejection (model_helpers.hpp:157-165). Parent chosen uniformly among alive NON-extinction nodes with brts < t* < t_ext (augment_tree.cpp:154-166) — the two crown lineages are not nodes and can never be chosen. num_missing > max_missing throws augmentation_overrun (lines 173, 181).

log q AS EVALUATED (model.hpp:255-328), tips_0 = tree[0].n = 2, tips incremented by each tip node up to and including i (line 299), Ne = (#missing so far) - (#extinction so far) before node i (lines 300, 304):
  log q = sum_{i missing} [ log(n_i mu_i lambda_i) - mu_i (t_ext,i - s_i) - log(2 tips_i + Ne_i) ]
        + sum_{i unsampled} [ log(n_i lambda_i (1-rho)) - mu_i (T - s_i) - log(2 tips_i + Ne_i) ]
        - sum_i n_i lambda_i [ Delta_i - (rho/mu_i)(e^{-mu_i (T - s_i)} - e^{-mu_i (T - s_{i-1})}) ],   Delta_i = s_i - s_{i-1}, mu_i floored at 1e-10 (lines 274-275, 295-296).
  For model_bin[2] && exponential link the integral term instead uses sum_exp_bE * exp_integral(A_lam, beta_D, s_{i-1}, s_i) / Delta_i * [Delta_i - (rho/mu_i)(...)] (lines 278-293), with sum_exp_bE = sum over alive lineages of exp(-beta_D * ts_s) maintained at lines 312-323, A_lam = beta_0 + beta_N N + (beta_M - beta_D) M.

log f AS EVALUATED (model.hpp:359-471), piecewise-constant path (every case except D+exp and D+gauss):
  log f = sum_{i extinction} log max(mu_i, 1e-300) + sum_{i speciation, i != last} log lambda_i - sum_i Delta_i n_i (lambda_i + mu_i) + n_obs log rho + n_unsamp log(1 - rho),
  where "speciation" = tip, missing, or unsampled nodes (lines 433-438), n_obs = 1 + #tip nodes (= n_tips), n_unsamp = #unsampled nodes (lines 459-467). The sum of log lambda goes through log_sum (model_helpers.hpp:126-153): running product flushed to a log when outside [1e-19, 1e21]; lambda = 0 makes prod 0 and result -inf (line 132-135). D+exponential: integral = sum_alive e^{-beta_D ts_s} * exp_integral(A_lam, beta_D, s_{i-1}, s_i) + same for mu (lines 381-392, exp_integral lines 333-336). D+gaussian: per-alive-lineage erf integrals gauss_integral (lines 393-417, 348-357).

IS WEIGHT (E_step.cpp:90-92). log_w_i = logf_i - logg_i, both evaluated at the SAME theta used to augment. Acceptance (E_step.cpp:94): std::isfinite(log_w) && 0.0 < std::exp(log_w) — i.e. an ABSOLUTE test: log_w <= about -745.13 (double underflow) counts as "zero weight" (rejected_zero_weights++), as does log_w = -inf (lambda = 0 at any speciation node). Algebraic consequence of the two formulas above (rho = 1, piecewise-constant path): log w = sum_{obs speciation} log lambda_i + sum_{missing} [log(2 tips_i + Ne_i) - log n_i] - sum_i Delta_i n_i mu_i - sum_i n_i lambda_i (1/mu_i)(e^{-mu_i (T - s_{i-1})} - e^{-mu_i (T - s_i)}); the missing-lineage log(lambda mu) and mu*lifespan terms cancel between f and q. Note the observed speciation log lambda terms and the integrals scale with tree size, so log w is O(n_tips) in absolute value.

NORMALISATION / STORAGE (E_step.cpp:132-139, precision_weights.hpp:10-24). m = max_i log_w_i; w~_i = exp(log_w_i - m) computed in 100-digit decimal, written back into E.weights (so after E_step, E.weights holds LINEAR max-scaled weights in (0,1], never normalised to sum 1 or mean 1); sum_w = sum_i w~_i.

FHAT (E_step.cpp:143-144). S = N + rejected_zero_weights (overrun/lambda/unhandled rejections excluded); fhat = log(sum_w / S) + m = log( (1/S) sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i ) with zero-weight completions contributing 0 to the numerator and 1 to the denominator. Identical to R's .is_fhat with n_zero_weight (de.R:60-76). fhat ignores rho-conditioning and the survival conditional. ESS is NOT computed in C++; R computes ESS = (sum w~)^2 / sum w~^2 from lw = logf - logg over finite lw (de.R:111-117, emphasis.R:147,157).

M-STEP (M_step.cpp:41-62, 66-94). Q(theta) = sum_{i=1}^{N} w~_i * loglik(theta, z_i) (tbb::parallel_reduce, w~ unnormalised max-scaled); NLopt minimises -Q, or -Q + log P_tree(theta) when conditional != nullptr, where log P_tree comes from an R closure (rcpp_mcem.cpp:79-81 -> inference.R:.build_cond_fun, log(max(p_survival,1e-300))). SBPLX (NLOPT_LN_SBPLX, rsbplx.cpp:87) with only xtol_rel set (M_step.cpp:83); bounds: R's lb8/ub8 if non-empty else model bounds (84-87); inactive slots have lb = ub = 0 so are fixed. M.estimates starts at the E-step theta (line 82). Any nlopt_result < 0 throws (rsbplx.cpp:144-146). What converges: nothing inside C++; the R loop (emphasis.R:43-133) iterates em_cpp with fresh trees and constant sample_size each iteration, uses results$estimates as the next theta, and stops when max_j |theta_j - theta_j'| / range_j < tol for `patience` consecutive iterations (lines 93, 114-119), or max_iter, or the R-level max_time (default 3600 s, inference.R:106), or 8 consecutive E-step failures with maxN doubling (cap 50000) and 0.8/0.2 pull toward the bound centre (lines 64-85). fhat is only traced.

maxN / TIMEOUT (E_step.cpp:62-79, 101, 128-130). parallel_for over [0, maxN) attempts (successes AND failures count); collection stops when E.trees.size() == N (line 101) or when elapsed > (max_time_seconds > 0 ? max_time_seconds : 120 s) (line 73); then if num_trees < N throw emphasis_error_E whose message always begins "maxN exceeded" (emphasis.hpp:90). No caller ever passes max_time_seconds (mcem.cpp:27,46; rcpp_mce.cpp:61), so the 120 s cap is always active and unreachable from R.

THREADS / RNG. E_step: tbb::task_arena arena(num_threads) is constructed (line 63) but parallel_for at line 65 is NOT run inside arena.execute, so it runs on the default arena (all cores); num_threads only sets grainsize = maxN / num_threads (line 62). Shared state: mutex-protected pushes to E.trees/weights/logf_/logg_ and counters (96-107, 111-120); per-thread tree buffer thread_local pooled_tree (line 17); std::atomic<bool> stop. M_step: tbb::task_scheduler_init(num_threads) (M_step.cpp:77, legacy TBB API shipped by RcppParallel 5.1.11.2) — the objective's parallel_reduce honours it; the R conditional is called on the calling thread outside the reduce (line 61). RNG: augment_tree.cpp:41 thread_local std::default_random_engine, model.hpp:218 a separate thread_local std::mt19937_64 for extinction times, both seeded from high_resolution_clock + thread-id hash (model_helpers.hpp:78-102); R's RNG is never used, so set.seed() does not affect the E-step.
data_flow:
R MCEM (thinning path, R/emphasis.R:.mcem_dynamic_fresh, reached from inference.R:.run_mcem when ctrl$sampling == "dynamic_fresh" or when BDI is unsupported — any D model or gaussian link): brts sorted decreasing (crown first) + pars8 + lb8/ub8 (inactive slots 0/0 via .expand_pars) + sample_size N + maxN (default max(2000, 10 N), doubled on failure up to 50000) + max_missing + max_lambda = 1e6 + xtol + num_threads + model_bin + link int + rho + optional cond_fun -> em_cpp (rcpp_mcem.cpp) -> Model(lb8, ub8, model_bin, link, rho) -> mcem() -> E_step: create_tree (forward times) -> maxN attempts of augment_tree into a thread-local buffer -> loglik + sampling_prob at the same pars -> log_w -> accept/reject -> copy accepted tree + (log_w, logf, logg) under mutex -> after loop: max-shift to linear weights in place, fhat -> M_step(pars, trees, linear weights, model, lb8, ub8, xtol, threads, conditional) -> SBPLX -> estimates. Returned list: trees (integer count when copy_trees = FALSE, else 3-column data frames brts/n/t_ext), rejected, rejected_overruns, rejected_lambda, rejected_zero_weights, estimates (8), nlopt (result code), fhat (scalar), time (E ms + M ms), weights (linear max-scaled, length N), logf, logg (length N, log scale). R keeps estimates as next pars, records fhat/time/rejected per iteration, and from the LAST successful iteration recomputes lw = logf - logg, .is_fhat with n_zero_weight, ESS, bootstrap variance (emphasis.R:135-161).

CEM / GAM path: augment_trees (rcpp_mce.cpp) with dummy bounds -> E_step -> returns 8-column tree data frames (unpack.h: brts, n, t_ext, pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start, id, parent_id) + logf + logg + counts; R computes fhat itself (.is_fhat) and, in shared-tree mode, re-scores trees at other particles with eval_logf (loglik.cpp: pack reads the 8 columns, computes loglik and sampling_prob at the new pars; bounds ±1e6 irrelevant).

BDI path: R-side sampler produces trees + log-weights, normalises to mean 1 (bdi.R:796-799) and calls m_cpp (rcpp_mcm.cpp), which rebuilds nodes from brts/n/t_ext only (pd = tip_start = focal_tip_start = 0, id = parent_id = -1) and runs M_step with those weights as multipliers.

Index conventions: trees 0-based, sorted ascending by forward brts; node i covers [s_{i-1}, s_i) with n_i lineages; log-weights are natural logs; fhat and logf/logg are natural-log densities; nlopt objective sign is minimisation of -Q.
invariants_assumed: brts passed to C++ is strictly decreasing with the crown age first; otherwise create_tree produces negative/unsorted forward times (E_step.cpp:19-38). R sorts (emphasis.R:20) but rcpp_mce/em_cpp do not check.
tree_t is sorted ascending by brts and node.n equals the lineage count on the half-open interval ending at that node; insert_species/insert_unsampled_species maintain this (augment_tree.cpp:90-125).
The last node has brts == T and is a tip sentinel that is never counted as a speciation event (model.hpp:436) and never has its t_ext used as an extinction.

t_ext sentinel equality (1e11, 0.0, 5e10) is the only way node kinds are distinguished; a real extinction time of exactly 0.0 or an augmented t_ext >= T would be misclassified (model_helpers.hpp:105-108).
pars has exactly 8 elements and inactive slots (including beta_M/gamma_M, slots 2 and 6) are 0 with lower == upper == 0; C++ never reads model_bin_[0] or [1] (model.hpp).
lower_bound and upper_bound have length == pars.size(); M_step passes raw pointers to nlopt with no length check (M_step.cpp:84-87, rsbplx.cpp:108-123).
logf and logg for a tree are evaluated at the same theta used to simulate it (E_step.cpp:84-91); eval_logf deliberately breaks this for shared-tree CEM, relying on q being evaluable at any theta.

E.weights is a vector of log-weights during collection and of linear max-scaled (unnormalised) weights after calc_sum_w; every consumer (M_step objective, em_cpp 'weights' field) must know which (E_step.cpp:133-139).
M-step argmax is invariant to the omitted exp(-max) and to normalisation of the weights — true for -Q alone, NOT when the conditional term is added (M_step.cpp:55-61).
Model is immutable during the parallel region and Model::is_threadsafe() == true (model.hpp:113); the only mutable state in scoring/sampling is thread_local RNG.
The rho < 1 branch assumes the unsampled sentinel T+1 is >= b so it is caught by `ext_time >= b` (model.hpp:231, augment_tree.cpp:167).
N <= maxN, and success means exactly N accepted trees; S_completed = N + rejected_zero_weights assumes trees.size() == N (E_step.cpp:143).
The R conditional callback is only ever invoked on the main R thread (it is called outside the parallel_reduce, M_step.cpp:61).
RcppParallel keeps shipping legacy TBB headers (tbb/task_scheduler_init.h present in RcppParallel 5.1.11.2), otherwise M_step.cpp:77 does not compile.
readme_vs_code_discrepancies: README.md:79-84 gives lambda(s,t) = f(beta_0, beta_N N + beta_D D) and says (line ~104) M = P/N 'is used only internally to centre D and is not a user covariate'; the C++ linear predictor always contains a beta_M * M term (model.hpp:154, 165, 200, 211) and R's .par_names exposes beta_M/gamma_M when model_bin[2] == 1 (inference.R:235-247). Correct only because R pins slot 2/6 to 0 for cr/dd/d/nd.

README.md:124 states the weight is f_theta / q. The evaluated q contains a -log(2*tips + Ne) term per augmented lineage (model.hpp:304, 308) that is not the sampler's actual parent-choice probability (uniform over tips-2+Ne alive nodes, augment_tree.cpp:154-166), so w as computed = (f/q_true) * prod_missing (2 tips+Ne)/(tips-2+Ne) up to the labelling convention — README does not describe this factor.

README.md:61 and 133 describe 'parallel augmentation via TBB' / 'C++ with TBB parallelism' with a num_threads control; E_step never places the parallel_for in the arena it constructs (E_step.cpp:63-65), so num_threads is not enforced there.

README.md:132 says BDI is the default sampler and thinning is `sampling = "dynamic_fresh"`; the roxygen for estimate_rates (inference.R:53-54) still says 'Currently only "dynamic_fresh" is implemented'. The rcpp_* roxygen (rcpp_mcem.cpp:38, rcpp_mce.cpp:30, rcpp_mcm.cpp:41, loglik.cpp:62) documents model as c(use_N, use_P, use_E), the pre-2026-07 layout the README says was replaced by {N, M, D}.

rcpp_mcem.cpp:28 documents maxN as 'maximum number of failed trees'; the code counts every attempt including successes (E_step.cpp:65), matching README ('Total augmentation attempts per E-step', inference.R:60) and rcpp_mce.cpp:26.

rcpp_mcem.cpp:50 documents fhat as 'vector of fhat values'; it is a scalar (E_step.cpp:144, rcpp_mcem.cpp:114). Line 54 documents `weights` without stating they are linear max-scaled, and bdi.R:793 asserts 'The thinning E-step stores log-weights (logf-logg)', which is false for em_cpp output.

README.md:152 says MCEM 'doubles augmentation attempts' on E-step failure — matches emphasis.R:68 — but neither README nor R docs mention the always-on 120 s hard cap inside a single E-step (E_step.cpp:73), the zero-weight-in-denominator fhat convention (E_step.cpp:141-144), or that set.seed() does not control the C++ sampler.
emphasis.hpp:113 header comment says max_time_seconds = 0 means 'no time limit'; E_step.cpp:51,71-73 implement 0 as 'default 120 s'.

README.md:307 says integration tests are dead; concretely tests/testthat/test-em.R and test-augment.R call `mc_loglik`, a symbol that no longer exists in RcppExports.R, and every test there is skip()ped — no test exercises em_cpp, the M-step, the conditional term, or multi-threaded E-steps.

concerns.description: Acceptance test `std::isfinite(log_w) && (0.0 < std::exp(log_w))` is an ABSOLUTE threshold: any tree with log_w < about -745 is classified as zero-weight even though its weight is finite and its relative weight may be as large as any other's. log_w = logf - logg contains the sum over all OBSERVED speciation events of log lambda_i and the -integral n(lambda+mu) terms that q does not cancel (see math), so |log_w| grows linearly with tree size: e.g. 400 tips with lambda ~ 0.2 already give sum log lambda ~ -640 before the integral terms. On such trees every augmentation is rejected as 'zero weight', E_step throws 'maxN exceeded ... zero weights', and R's .mcem_warn_estep (emphasis.R:198-209) blames lambda = 0.
concerns.why_it_matters: Silent, size-dependent failure of the whole thinning MCEM path for large clades (the README says the package is used on atlas trees). The R-side .is_fhat is max-shifted and scale-free; the C++ gate is not. A relative test (log_w > max-so-far - 700) or simply isfinite would fix it, but the intended semantics of 'zero weight' (lambda = 0 => -inf) needs to be preserved.

concerns.description: Race on the stop flag: `if (!stop)` (line 95) is evaluated OUTSIDE the mutex, and `stop = (E.trees.size() == N)` (line 101) is assigned with == inside it. Thread A pushes tree N and sets stop = true; thread B, which already passed the check, pushes tree N+1 and sets stop = (N+1 == N) = false. All threads then resume collecting until maxN or the 120 s cap.
concerns.why_it_matters: With num_threads > 1 (and the default arena actually uses all cores, see next item) the E-step can return more than N trees; line 143 then uses S_completed = N + zero_weights instead of trees.size(), so fhat has the wrong denominator (biased low by log(N/num_trees)), the M-step runs on an unplanned sample size, and runtime balloons toward maxN attempts. Fix is to test stop under the lock or use >=.

concerns.description: `tbb::task_arena arena(num_threads)` is constructed but the parallel_for at line 65 is not executed inside `arena.execute(...)`, so it runs in the default arena with hardware concurrency regardless of num_threads; the only effect of num_threads is grainsize. Same pattern in augment_trees (augment_tree.cpp:221-224). M_step by contrast uses task_scheduler_init (M_step.cpp:77).
concerns.why_it_matters: R callers that set cpp_threads = 1 to combine with mclapply forks (de.R:223-227, 262) still get a fully multi-threaded TBB pool inside each forked child — oversubscription and TBB-after-fork hazards; users cannot limit CPU use; and the race above is exercised even when num_threads = 1 is requested.

concerns.description: grainsize = maxN / num_threads (integer division) is 0 whenever maxN < num_threads; tbb::blocked_range with grainsize 0 treats every non-empty range as divisible and splits a size-1 range into (0,1) forever (assert only in debug builds). Same at augment_tree.cpp:223. CEM's default maxN is 10 (de.R:574) and num_threads is capped only by hardware_concurrency (E_step.cpp:54), which is 16+ on the fleet machines.
concerns.why_it_matters: Potential stack overflow / hang inside the E-step for small maxN with many threads; needs std::max<size_t>(1, ...).

concerns.description: With a survival conditional the objective is -(sum_i w~_i log f_i) + log P_tree(theta) where w~_i are UNNORMALISED max-scaled weights (sum between 1 and N; exactly N on the BDI path, bdi.R:799). The conditioned expected complete-data log-likelihood is (sum_i w~_i log f_i)/(sum_i w~_i) - log P_tree(theta). The comment at lines 58-60 states the normalised objective but the code implements the unnormalised one.
concerns.why_it_matters: The survival-conditioning term is under-weighted by a factor sum_i w~_i that varies from iteration to iteration with the ESS, so the conditioned MLE is not the one documented and the fixed point of the GAM-conditioned pipeline (pipeline.R / inference.R:.build_cond_fun) depends on sampler efficiency.

concerns.description: q charges each augmented lineage -log(2*tips + Ne) (also line 308). The sampler's actual parent choice is uniform over alive non-extinction NODES, |alive_ids| = tips - 2 + Ne (augment_tree.cpp:154-166; the two crown lineages are not nodes), and the lineage count at that time is n_i = tips + Ne. Neither equals 2*tips + Ne, and f is a per-lineage (labelled) density (log lambda per event, model.hpp:437) while q uses n*lambda (any lineage). The comment 'see tech report' (E_step.cpp:142) points to dev/audit and dev/validation, which are empty.
concerns.why_it_matters: Each missing lineage multiplies the IS weight by (2 tips + Ne)/n_i (or /(tips-2+Ne) under the labelled reading), a z-dependent factor that is not 1; if it is not the intended combinatorial correction the IS estimator fhat and the M-step weights are biased toward trees with more augmented lineages. Rated as a question of derivation as much as a bug: it may be a deliberate topology-multiplicity term inherited from the original emphasis derivation, but nothing in the repo documents it.

concerns.description: For D + exponential link the thinning was performed with intensity nh_rate(t) = n * lambda_ep(node covariates, pd(t)) * (1 - rho e^{-mu (T-t)}) (model.hpp:238-252), but sampling_prob evaluates the compensator with a different function — the exact per-lineage sum sum_exp_bE * exp_integral(...) times an 'Approximation: use node-level mu' survival factor (lines 278-293). More generally, for any model with M or D active, nh_rate recomputes pd at the query time t (line 242) so the intensity varies within a segment, whereas sampling_prob integrates lambda_i evaluated at the node's pd (lines 295-296). Only N-only models (pd coefficients pinned to 0) give an exact q.
concerns.why_it_matters: An IS estimator is unbiased only if q is the density of what was actually simulated. For M/D models the evaluated q is not that density, so w = f/q is systematically off; the fhat surface used by CEM/GAM and the MCEM weights inherit the bias. Also the envelope Lambda* = max(rate at both segment ends) assumes monotone intensity within a segment, which fails for the gaussian link and for max(0, .) with time-varying D (augment_tree.cpp:138-151: pt can exceed 1).

concerns.description: f for D models on the linear (and gaussian-without-exact-path) link uses inte += dt * n_i * (lambda_focal + mu_focal), i.e. n times the rate of the focal lineage (D of the node's own lineage) as a stand-in for sum_s lambda_s(t); with max(0, .) and per-lineage D this is not the model's total intensity. The same approximation is used in q and nh_rate so the sampler is self-consistent, but f is then an approximation to the stated model.
concerns.why_it_matters: fhat is not an estimate of the marginal likelihood of the model as written in README.md:79-84 for linear + D; AIC comparisons across links (pipeline compare_models) mix an exact f (exponential) with an approximate f (linear).

concerns.description: Random numbers come from two independent thread_local engines seeded from the wall clock + thread-id hash (std::default_random_engine here — minstd_rand on libc++, a 31-bit LCG — and mt19937_64 in model.hpp:218); R's RNG is never touched. set.seed() has no effect on augmentation, and results differ run to run and by thread scheduling.
concerns.why_it_matters: No reproducible E-step, no reproducible MCEM/CEM/GAM surface, tests that call set.seed(42) (test-de.R, test-em.R) cannot pin values, and the LCG's period (2^31-2) is small relative to the number of uniforms consumed by a 2000-attempt E-step on a large tree.

concerns.description: The 120 s safety cap is hard-coded as the meaning of max_time_seconds = 0, contradicting the header (emphasis.hpp:113 '0 = no time limit'), and no caller passes the argument (mcem.cpp:27,46; rcpp_mce.cpp:61), so it cannot be changed from R. On timeout with < N trees the thrown message says 'maxN exceeded' (emphasis.hpp:90) and R responds by doubling maxN and perturbing pars (emphasis.R:64-85), which cannot help a time-limited failure. The check is per attempt, so one augmentation that inserts up to max_missing lineages (each O(tree) insert + O(tree) nh_rate) is unbounded.
concerns.why_it_matters: Large trees on slow hosts silently fail after 2 minutes with a misleading diagnosis; R's own max_time (default 3600 s) suggests to users that longer budgets are honoured.

concerns.description: rcpp_mcem defines its own 3-column unpack (brts, n, t_ext) instead of the 8-column one in unpack.h used by rcpp_mce; rcpp_mcm::pack (rcpp_mcm.cpp:21) likewise rebuilds nodes with pd = tip_start = focal_tip_start = 0 and id = parent_id = -1.
concerns.why_it_matters: Trees returned by em_cpp(copy_trees = TRUE) cannot be re-scored correctly by eval_logf for any M/D model (e_s and M collapse), and m_cpp can only ever be correct for N-only models — currently true because only the BDI path calls it (bdi.R:820), but nothing enforces it.

concerns.description: Any negative nlopt_result throws 'optimize failed', including NLOPT_ROUNDOFF_LIMITED (-4), which NLopt commonly returns as a benign termination for derivative-free methods. em_cpp then errors and .mcem_dynamic_fresh treats it as an E-step failure (emphasis.R:60-85), applying maxN doubling and parameter perturbation.
concerns.why_it_matters: Misattributed failures, wasted E-steps, and a perturbed trajectory in the MCEM iteration; the estimates that nlopt did produce are discarded.

concerns.description: No check that lower/upper bounds have pars.size() elements before handing .data() to nlopt (rsbplx.cpp:111,120), and no check that model bounds are 8-long when used as fallback.
concerns.why_it_matters: Out-of-bounds read for any C++ or non-standard R caller passing compact (2/4/6-element) bounds with 8-element pars.

concerns.description: tbb::task_scheduler_init is the pre-oneTBB API; it compiles only because RcppParallel 5.1.11.2 still ships tbb/task_scheduler_init.h. The is_threadsafe guard is commented out (line 76). The R conditional (an Rcpp::Function) is called inside the NLopt C call stack (line 61); an R error there unwinds a C++ exception through C frames.
concerns.why_it_matters: Build fragility against future RcppParallel/oneTBB updates; possible undefined behaviour if the GAM predictor errors mid-optimisation.

concerns.description: mu is floored at 1e-300 in f's extinction term (log ~ -690.8) but at 1e-10 in q (line 275) and in nh_rate (250); lambda = 0 in f gives -inf (log_sum) and the tree is rejected, whereas mu = 0 at a sampled extinction gives a finite but astronomically small f and the tree is kept with weight ~ e^-690 relative.
concerns.why_it_matters: Asymmetric handling of the two boundary cases feeds the absolute-threshold gate at E_step.cpp:94 and makes rejected_zero_weights depend on which rate hit zero; harmless for the estimate, confusing for diagnostics.

concerns.description: Each accepted tree is copied into E.trees while holding the global mutex; the else-branch increments rejected_zero_weights even after stop is set (line 104-107) while accepted trees after stop are dropped uncounted.
concerns.why_it_matters: Serialises the parallel region on the copy (performance) and makes the rejection counters slightly inconsistent with the attempts that produced them.

concerns.description: Dead/unused API surface: E_step_info_t::logf and logg scalars (per-tree vectors are used instead), nlopt_f_data destructor that builds an empty tree (M_step.cpp:29-32), mce() which ignores its bounds/xtol arguments and has no caller (mcem.cpp:14-29; rcpp_mce calls E_step directly), sbplx_1 class (never instantiated), and the `plugin` argument of m_cpp (rcpp_mcm.cpp:54, unused).
concerns.why_it_matters: Signals drift between the intended and the actual API and makes the reviewer's job harder; no runtime effect.

concerns.description: The only tests of the E+M path call a non-existent function `mc_loglik` and are all skip()ped (also test-augment.R). test-de.R exercises augment_trees/eval_logf structure only. Nothing tests em_cpp, the M-step objective, the conditional term, the weight scale returned to R, num_threads > 1, or the zero-weight denominator on the C++ side (the R-side .is_fhat test at test-inference.R:143-159 covers only the R replica).
concerns.why_it_matters: All of the concerns above are unguarded by tests; a refactor of E_step.cpp cannot be validated.

concerns.description: For initial-tree (observed) speciation nodes tip_start is set to 0.0, so calculate_pendant_pd counts each observed lineage as pendant since the crown; M = pd/n for observed nodes is therefore not 'mean pendant age' but a mix of time-since-crown (observed) and true pendant ages (augmented). With only branching times (no topology) the true pendant ages of observed lineages are unavailable, so this may be the intended mean-field convention — but README.md:104 describes M as mean pendant age without qualification.
concerns.why_it_matters: M and hence D = E - M are the covariates whose coefficients the 'd'/'nd' models estimate; if the convention is not what the paper describes, beta_D is testing a different quantity.

concerns.description: S_completed = N + rejected_zero_weights treats a lambda = 0 tree as a legitimate zero-weight sample but treats augmentation_lambda (envelope > max_lambda) and augmentation_overrun (> max_missing lineages) as theta-independent computational failures. Both of the latter are strongly theta-dependent (high lambda / high missing counts are consequences of theta), so excluding them from the denominator makes fhat(theta) a conditional-on-completion quantity whose conditioning event changes with theta.
concerns.why_it_matters: The fhat surface fed to CEM/GAM and the MCEM trace is not comparable across theta in regions where overrun/lambda rejections occur; whether this is acceptable is a modelling decision that should be stated.

open_questions: What is the derivation of the -log(2*tips + Ne) term in sampling_prob (model.hpp:304,308)? The code cites a 'tech report' (E_step.cpp:142) but dev/audit and dev/validation are empty; the sampler's parent choice is uniform over tips-2+Ne nodes and n_i = tips+Ne.

Was the absolute zero-weight gate (E_step.cpp:94) ever observed to reject every tree on a large clade? A quick check: run augment_trees on a 300-500 tip tree with lambda < 1 and inspect rejected_zero_weights vs the logf/logg magnitudes of any survivors.
Is max_time_seconds meant to default to 'no limit' (header) or to 120 s (implementation), and should R's ctrl$max_time be threaded through to it?
Was num_threads in E_step ever intended to be enforced (the unused task_arena suggests yes)? How do the mclapply forks in de.R:.eval_independent interact with a full TBB pool inside each child?
Should the conditional M-step objective use normalised weights, i.e. (sum w log f)/(sum w) - log P_tree, as the comment at M_step.cpp:58-60 states?
For M/D models, is q intended to be the exact density of the thinning sampler (currently it is not: node-level pd vs pd(t), and the D+exp compensator uses a different function than nh_rate)?
Is the 8-element `weights` field returned by em_cpp (linear, max-scaled, unnormalised) part of the documented contract, given bdi.R's comment believes it holds log-weights?
Are the counting conventions for fhat's denominator (zero-weight in, overrun/lambda out) the ones used in the paper's definition of the IS estimator?
Which random engine is intended (default_random_engine vs mt19937_64), and should the E-step accept a seed from R for reproducibility?

module: bdi-sampler — R/bdi.R (dispatch from R/simulate.R `.sim_tree_conditional` and R/inference.R `.run_mcem`)
purpose: Pure-R importance sampler that augments a reconstructed tree (crown-age branching times) with extinct lineages by simulating the birth–death process *conditioned on the reconstructed tree* (Nee et al. 1994 "doomed-lineage" rates). Under constant rates (model_bin = c(0,0,0), links linear/exponential) it uses an exact time-change of the inhomogeneous total hazard with an analytic cumulative integral, giving log f − log g constant across draws (ESS = S). Under N-only diversity dependence it first solves a mean-field backward survival ODE and forward mean(+variance) ODEs by fixed-point iteration, then runs a piecewise-frozen-rate Gillespie proposal with rejection of draws that leave missing lineages alive at the present. It converts each draw to the package's tree data frame, scores log f with the C++ `eval_logf`, and either returns (trees, logf, logg, weights, fhat) to `simulate_tree()` or drives an MCEM loop (`.mcem_bdi`) whose M-step is the C++ `m_cpp`.

key_functions.name: .bdi_p_cr
key_functions.role: CR survival probability p(t) of a lineage alive at forward time t to reach tp (Kendall/Nee closed form).

key_functions.name: .bdi_integral_cr
key_functions.role: Analytic cumulative hazard of the conditioned BDI process over [t1,t2] with n missing lineages alive and k observed lineages; returns Inf when t2 == tp and n > 0 (forces extinction before present). Contains a separate (wrong) critical-case branch for |lambda-mu|<1e-15.

key_functions.name: .bdi_find_event_time_cr
key_functions.role: Time-change: solves H(t*) = U (U ~ Exp(1)) by stats::uniroot on the analytic hazard; returns t_max+1 when U >= H(t_max).

key_functions.name: .bdi_supported
key_functions.role: Gate: TRUE only for model_bin of length 3 with slots 2,3 == 0 (N-only: cr, dd) and link in {0,1}. Does not look at rho.

key_functions.name: .bdi_lam / .bdi_mu
key_functions.role: Rate functions in the OLD (N, P, E) covariate layout: eta = pars8[1] + pars8[2]*N + pars8[3]*P + pars8[4]*E; link 0 -> max(0,eta), else exp(eta). Slots 3-4 are beta_M/beta_D in the C++ (N, M=P/N, D=E-M) layout.

key_functions.name: .bdi_solve_p_backward
key_functions.role: RK4 backward integration of dp/dt = lam*p^2 - (lam-mu)*p from p(tp)=1 on a 500-point grid, rates evaluated at mean-field covariates; p clipped to [0,1].

key_functions.name: .bdi_solve_mean_forward
key_functions.role: RK4 forward ODE for mean number of missing lineages m(t) and mean missing pendant PD P_miss(t) (plain mean-field closure; used when use_gaussian_closure = FALSE).

key_functions.name: .bdi_solve_meanvar_forward
key_functions.role: Same plus Var(N) and Cov(N,P) ODEs (Gaussian closure) used to Taylor-correct E[P/N]; default path.

key_functions.name: .bdi_P_obs
key_functions.role: Observed pendant PD k(t)*t under the tip_start=0 convention. Defined but never called (iterate recomputes k_vals*t_grid inline at 315).

key_functions.name: .bdi_iterate
key_functions.role: Self-consistent fixed-point loop (max 20 iters, tol 1e-4): backward p(t) given (N̂,P̂,Ê) -> forward moments -> update N̂ = k + m, P̂ = P_obs + P_miss, Ê = second-order Taylor of E[P/N], clipped to [0,tp]. Returns approxfun interpolants.

key_functions.name: .bdi_augment_one
key_functions.role: Draws one augmentation over the segments between observed branching times: CR branch (435-456) exact time-change; DD branch (458-483) frozen-rate Gillespie; shared event-type selection (489-506) accumulating log g with per-lineage rates; rejects (NULL) on max_missing overflow or any missing lineage alive at tp (514).

key_functions.name: .bdi_to_tree_df
key_functions.role: Builds the (brts, n, t_ext, pd, tip_start, id, parent_id) data frame: observed nodes tip_start=0/t_ext=1e11, missing species as (speciation, extinction) node pairs with tip_start=birth, closing node at tp with id=-1; n computed by a forward scan from 2; pd all zero; parent_id = id of the most recent observed branching before birth (deterministic).

key_functions.name: .augment_tree_bdi
key_functions.role: Wrapper: brts -> forward bt = sort(tp - brts[-1]); runs .bdi_iterate when not CR; draws up to sample_size (CR) or 5*sample_size attempts (DD) trees; scores logf via C++ eval_logf(pars8, trees, model, link, rho) and discards eval_logf's thinning logg; weights = logf - logg; fhat = log-mean-exp over valid trees only.

key_functions.name: .mcem_bdi
key_functions.role: MCEM loop: E-step = .augment_tree_bdi; converts log-weights to self-normalised linear weights with mean 1 (796-799); M-step = m_cpp(plugin='rpd1', model, link, rho, rconditional); convergence on max |Δpars|/range < tol for `patience` iterations; bootstrap loglik_var and final_IS diagnostics from the last E-step.
