key_functions.name: .sim_tree_conditional (dispatch)
key_functions.role: simulate_tree(tree=...) default method='bdi'; silently downgrades to 'thinning' when !.bdi_supported (345); tryCatch -> NULL on error; log_q <- aug$logg (383); phylo via .aug_to_Ltable + DDD::L2phylo.

key_functions.name: .aug_to_Ltable
key_functions.role: Merges augmented rows (t_ext != 0, parent_id != -1, t_ext < 1e11) into the extant L-table; parent label from id via brts[pid+2]; unsampled (t_ext == 5e10) become extant (-1).

key_functions.name: .run_mcem (dispatch)
key_functions.role: ctrl$sampling default 'bdi' (111); if !.bdi_supported(model, link) switches to 'dynamic_fresh' with a message only when verbose (359-364); passes ctrl$rho through to .mcem_bdi (384). Verbose banner prints 'BDI (exact)' for any supported model, including dd (788-790).

math_as_implemented:
Conventions: forward time t in [0, tp], tp = brts[1] (crown age); bt = sort(tp - brts[-1]) are the n-2 non-crown branching times (bdi.R:644); k(t) = 2 + #{bt <= t} observed lineages (426, 431 uses k(t0+1e-12) at each segment start); n = number of missing (doomed) lineages currently alive; pars8 = c(beta0,betaN,betaM,betaD,gamma0,gammaN,gammaM,gammaD) but read as (beta0, betaN, beta_P, beta_E, ...) by .bdi_lam/.bdi_mu (108-116).

Survival probability (CR), bdi.R:16-19: E0 = exp(-(λ0-μ0)(tp-t)); p(t) = (λ0-μ0)/(λ0 - μ0·E0); u(t) := 1-p(t) = μ0(1-E0)/(λ0-μ0E0). λ0 = .bdi_lam(pars8,0,0,0) and μ0 = .bdi_mu(pars8,0,0,0) (416-417), i.e. link applied to the intercept alone.

Conditioned (doomed-lineage) rates, bdi.R:451-456 (CR) and 463-472 (DD): per missing lineage birth la = λ·u(t), per missing lineage death mu_r = μ/u(t) (floored u ≥ 1e-15), immigration from observed lineages nu = 2·k·λ·u(t), total = n·(la + mu_r) + nu. These are the Nee et al. (1994) rates for a BD process conditioned on the reconstructed tree: a doomed lineage speciates into two doomed lineages at λu, dies at μ/u; an observed (surviving) lineage produces a doomed daughter at 2λu (either daughter may be the doomed one).

Analytic cumulative hazard (CR), bdi.R:36-66, for constant n,k on [t1,t2], E_i = exp(-d(tp-t_i)), d=λ0-μ0:
  I_lam = ∫λ0 u dt = μ0(t2-t1) + log[(λ0-μ0E2)/(λ0-μ0E1)]   (54)  [= μ0Δt + log(p(t1)/p(t2))]
  I_mu  = ∫μ0/u dt = λ0(t2-t1) + log[(1-E1)/(1-E2)]           (60)  [only if n>0; returns Inf if 1-E2 < 1e-300 (59)]
  H = (n+2k)·I_lam + n·I_mu                                     (65)
Both identities verified numerically against integrate() (see concerns for the critical branch). Note the doc-comment at line 32 states the I_mu identity in terms of (1-p), which is not what the code uses (1-E); the code is correct, the comment is not.

Time change, bdi.R:76-89: U ~ Exp(1) (437); if not (t_max == tp and n>0) and U >= H(t_cur,t_max) → no event (82); else t* = uniroot(H(t_cur,s) - U, [t_cur+1e-15, t_hi], tol 1e-13) with t_hi = tp - 1e-14 on the final segment when n>0 (86-88).

log g accumulation (CR branch 440-448, DD branch 474-482, events 489-506):
  logg = Σ_{events} log(rate_type at event) - ∫_0^{tp} total(t) dt
  survival: CR: -U per event and -H(t,t1) for the no-event tail of each segment (442, 447); DD: -total·dt with total frozen at the last event/segment start (478, 482).
  event type by r ~ U(0,total): r < n·la → missing birth, logg += log(la) (491); r < n·la + nu → immigration, logg += log(la) (NOT log(nu) nor log(2λu)) (496); else death of a uniformly chosen missing lineage, logg += log(mu_r) (501-502).
  So logg is a per-lineage ("labelled history") density: no factor n on births, no factor 2 on immigration, no 1/n for which lineage dies (cancelled against n·mu_r).
Draw rejected (NULL) if n_total > max_missing (508) or n_alive > 0 at tp (514); the rejection normalising constant is NOT added to logg.

log f (C++, inst/include/model.hpp:359-471, called via eval_logf, bdi.R:687-691), N-only: logf = Σ_{non-extinction nodes except the closing node} log λ(node) + Σ_{extinction nodes} log μ(node) - Σ_i (brts_i - brts_{i-1})·n_i·(λ_i+μ_i) + [rho<1: n_obs·log ρ + n_unsampled·log(1-ρ)], with n_i = lineage count on [brts_{i-1}, brts_i) and λ,μ evaluated at n_i (M = pd/n multiplies beta_M = 0 under the gate).

Weight and estimator, bdi.R:696-699: lw_i = logf_i - logg_i; fhat = log( Σ_i exp(lw_i - max lw) / n_valid ) + max lw (n_valid = accepted trees only). Under CR (λ0>μ0) the per-lineage terms cancel exactly because ∫_{t_b}^{t_d}[λu + μ/u - λ - μ]dt = log u(t_b) - log u(t_d) (from du/dt = -μ + (λ+μ)u - λu²), leaving lw ≡ C = Σ_{j=1}^{n-2} log λ0 + Σ_seg k_j ∫(2λ0u - λ0 - μ0)dt = Σ_j [log λ0 + log p(t_j)] + 2 log p(0) - ∫ k λ0 p dt, which is the Nee et al. crown-age likelihood (unconditioned on survival, labelled-history convention). Verified numerically: sd(lw) ≈ 6e-13, ESS = 200/200, fhat = -16.8672 = C computed independently by integrate(); thinning proposal on the same tree gives -16.89 (ESS 1312/4000).

M-step weights, bdi.R:796-799: w_i = exp(lw_i - max lw), then w_i ← w_i·S/Σw (mean 1) → all exactly 1 under CR; objective in src/M_step.cpp:49 is Σ_i loglik(θ, tree_i)·w_i.

DD mean-field system, bdi.R:129-392 (t on a 500-point grid, RK4):
  backward: dp/dt = λ̂(t)p² - (λ̂(t)-μ̂(t))p, p(tp)=1, λ̂,μ̂ = rates at (N̂,P̂,Ê) (141-146)
  forward (Gaussian closure, 251-269): with la_bdi = λ̂(1-p), mu_bdi = μ̂/(1-p), ν = 2k λ̂(1-p), drift = la_bdi - mu_bdi, infuse = la_bdi + mu_bdi:
    dm/dt = drift·m + ν;  dP_miss/dt = m;  dVar(N)/dt = 2·drift·Var + infuse·m + ν;  dCov(N,P)/dt = drift·Cov + Var
  update (356-366): N̂ = k(t) + m, P̂ = k(t)·t + P_miss, Ê = P̂/N̂ - Cov/N̂² + P̂·Var/N̂³ clipped to [0,tp]; convergence when max|ΔN̂| and max|ΔP̂|/max(P̂,1) < 1e-4 (368-377); non-convergence is silent.
  Under the gate pars8[3] = pars8[4] = 0 (via .expand_pars, simulate.R:298-311), so P̂, Ê, Var, Cov never enter any rate: only N̂ = k + m and p(t) are live.

Tree data frame (bdi.R:527-611): rows sorted by forward brts; observed branching j (1-based over bt_sorted) → id j-1, parent_id -1, t_ext 1e11, tip_start 0; missing species i → two rows with id n_obs+i-1, parent_id = max(0, #{bt_sorted <= birth} - 1), speciation row (brts=birth, t_ext=death, tip_start=birth) and extinction row (brts=death, t_ext=0, tip_start=birth); closing row (brts=tp, t_ext=1e11, id=-1, parent_id=-1); n[1]=2, n[i] = n[i-1] + (t_ext[i-1]==0 ? -1 : +1); pd ≡ 0; no focal_tip_start column (C++ pack() defaults it to 0, src/loglik.cpp:33-34).
data_flow:
Inputs: `tree` (phylo / simulate_tree result / numeric brts) → .extract_brts (inference.R:216-234) → brts decreasing with brts[1] = crown age; `pars` compact (2 + 2·Σmodel_bin) or 8-element (bdi.R:634-638; .mcem_bdi receives ip8 = .expand_pars(init_pars) from estimate_rates, inference.R:754/805); model_bin c(use_N,use_M,use_D); link int (0/1 only after the gate); rho.
Transform: brts → bt = sort(tp - brts[-1]) forward times (644). If any model_bin != 0 → .bdi_iterate (650-657) → p_fun, N̂, P̂, Ê interpolants. Loop attempts (667-677): .bdi_augment_one → list(species = list of c(birth, death)), logg) or NULL → .bdi_to_tree_df → data frame. All accepted trees → eval_logf (C++) → logf (eval_logf's logg discarded). weights = logf - logg; fhat.
Outputs: list(trees, logf, logg, weights, fhat) — same names as augment_trees()/thinning (src/rcpp_mce.cpp) but WITHOUT rejected_* counters. simulate_tree path: log_q = logg (simulate.R:383); phylo via .aug_to_Ltable (parent label = label of lineage born at brts[parent_id+2], simulate.R:424-429) + DDD::L2phylo. MCEM path (.mcem_bdi): e_step list (trees, mean-1 linear weights, rejected*=0, time, fhat) → m_cpp → 8-element estimates; per-iteration row (par1..par8, fhat, delta_max, rejected=0, num_trees = accepted count, time); final list(mcem, pars, iterations, stop_reason, loglik_var, final_IS). .run_mcem takes loglik = last finite fhat.
Index conventions: observed ids 0..n_obs-1 map to bt_sorted[id+1] = tp - brts[id+2] (consistent with C++ create_tree ids and with .aug_to_Ltable's brts[pid+2]); closing node id -1 in BDI vs id n_obs in the thinning tree (src/augment_tree.cpp:201-210). n[i] = lineages on [brts[i-1], brts[i]) in both samplers. t_ext sentinels shared: 1e11 tip, 0 extinction, 5e10 unsampled (never emitted by BDI).
invariants_assumed: λ0 > μ0 (net diversification positive) under CR: the analytic hazard returns Inf for every segment with n > 0 when μ0 > λ0 (1-E2 ≤ 0 < 1e-300 at bdi.R:59), and the sampler then errors inside uniroot — the whole conditioned process is only implemented for d > 0.
rho == 1: the conditioning p(t), the rates and the absence of unsampled-extant lineages all assume complete sampling; rho is forwarded only to eval_logf.

model_bin[2] == model_bin[3] == 0 and pars8[3] == pars8[4] == 0: guaranteed by .bdi_supported plus .expand_pars for compact pars; an 8-element pars with non-zero slots 3/4 bypasses the guarantee and is interpreted in the old (P, E) layout.

The C++ logf is a per-lineage ('labelled history') density with no combinatorial factors — logg is built to the same convention (log la per birth, log mu_r per death, no log n, no log 2 on immigration). Zero variance holds only because BOTH sides drop the same (2k+m) multiplicity per birth.

Rejection at bdi.R:514 (survivors at tp) and :508 (overflow) has a θ-dependent but per-draw-constant acceptance probability that is omitted from logg; fhat is therefore biased upward by -log P(accept) under DD (measured 0.23 and 0.45 nats on a test tree); self-normalised M-step weights are unaffected.
p_fun, N̂ interpolants (approxfun rule=2) are adequate on a 500-point uniform grid; near tp, u = 1-p → 0 linearly and mu_r = μ/u blows up, which is what kills remaining missing lineages.
The tree df's n column is derived only from t_ext == 0 flags after sorting by brts — assumes no ties between missing births/deaths and observed branching times.
Observed lineages have tip_start = 0 (so P_obs = k·t), matching the C++ compute_pendant_pd convention for parent_id == -1 nodes (src/augment_tree.cpp:50).
All accepted trees have finite logf: no filtering of ±Inf logf is performed (thinning's E_step rejects non-finite log_w at src/E_step.cpp:94; BDI does not).
readme_vs_code_discrepancies: README.md:132 and bdi.R:6 claim ESS = sample size / zero IS variance under constant rates — TRUE, verified numerically (sd(lw) ~ 1e-13, fhat equals the Nee likelihood computed independently) but only for λ0 > μ0; for μ0 > λ0 the sampler errors (bdi.R:59, 88) and the README does not say so.

README.md:135 states the gate excludes D-terms and the gaussian link but nothing excludes rho < 1; the sampler ignores rho and returns a different quantity (fhat = C + n_obs·log ρ, measured -22.41 vs thinning's -15.41 at ρ=0.5 on the same tree).
simulate.R:92-95 (roxygen for `rho`) says augmentation inserts unsampled extant lineages when rho < 1 — only true for method='thinning'; the default method='bdi' never emits t_ext == 5e10 rows.
inference.R:788-790 prints 'BDI (exact)' whenever .bdi_supported is TRUE, including dd, while README:132 and bdi.R:404-405 say DD is an approximate proposal with non-zero-variance weights.
bdi.R:26-32 doc-comment gives the identity ∫μ/(1-p)dt = λΔt + ln[(1-p1)/(1-p2)]; the code (line 60) uses ln[(1-E1)/(1-E2)] which is the correct identity — the comment is wrong, the code is right.

bdi.R:40-41 comments 'p(t) = λ(tp-t)/(1+λ(tp-t))' for the critical case; that is the extinction probability, the survival limit of .bdi_p_cr is 1/(1+λ(tp-t)); the branch's integrals are wrong (numeric 4.666 vs code 2.622).

bdi.R:792-795 claims the thinning M-step uses log-weights (logf-logg) as direct multipliers; src/E_step.cpp:132-139 converts them to linear max-scaled weights before M_step, so the premise is false (the BDI conversion to positive weights is still correct).

bdi.R:713-715 calls .mcem_bdi a 'drop-in replacement for .mcem_dynamic_fresh()' but its fhat divides by accepted trees only (bdi.R:699) whereas thinning divides by N + rejected_zero_weights (src/E_step.cpp:143-144), and rejected counts are always reported as 0 (bdi.R:804-807, 851).
README.md:307 / tests: there is no test exercising bdi.R at all (grep 'bdi' in tests/testthat returns nothing); test-de.R only covers augment_trees/eval_logf (thinning).

concerns.description: For μ0 > λ0 (d < 0), E2 = exp(-d(tp-t2)) ≥ 1 so oE2 = 1-E2 ≤ 0 < 1e-300 and .bdi_integral_cr returns Inf for every segment with n > 0. .bdi_find_event_time_cr then calls uniroot on a function that is -U at the lower end and Inf at the upper end and R errors ('f() values at end points not of opposite sign' — reproduced). The whole CR sampler is unusable in the μ > λ half of the parameter space; .mcem_bdi swallows the error (764-775), counts an E-step failure and perturbs pars toward the box centre, so MCEM silently cannot visit or converge to μ ≥ λ.
concerns.why_it_matters: Constant-rate fits on small or old clades routinely have MLEs or starting values with μ close to or above λ; the estimator degrades to 'perturb toward centre' with no warning, and the search space is truncated to d > 0.

concerns.description: rho is forwarded to eval_logf only; the conditioned process (p(t), rates, absence of unsampled-extant lineages) is built for complete sampling. The proposal has zero mass on augmentations containing unsampled extant lineages, which have positive f-mass when rho < 1, so the IS estimator targets f(obs, no unsampled lineages) ≠ f(obs). Measured: BDI fhat = -22.41 (exactly C + 8·log 0.5) vs thinning -15.41 at ρ = 0.5 on the same tree. Neither .bdi_supported (100-105) nor the callers (simulate.R:345, inference.R:359) gate on rho, and 'bdi' is the default everywhere.
concerns.why_it_matters: estimate_rates(..., control = list(rho = 0.7)) with the default sampler returns a wrong likelihood and biased parameter estimates, silently.

concerns.description: Under DD the proposal rates use mean-field N̂, so accepted trees can reach lineage counts where the model's linear-link λ(N) = max(0, β0 + βN·N) is 0; the C++ loglik then returns -Inf, and (because of the sign bug in log_sum::result, inst/include/model_helpers.hpp:129-136) sometimes +Inf. BDI does no finite-weight filtering (thinning does, src/E_step.cpp:94): with pars (1.5,-0.12,0.4,0) 56/300 trees had ±Inf logf, fhat = NaN, and .mcem_bdi's w_norm (796-799) becomes NaN (Inf - Inf), which is handed to m_cpp as multipliers.
concerns.why_it_matters: Realistic dd fits on the linear link can feed NaN weights to the optimiser and record NaN fhat, with no diagnostic.

concerns.description: Under DD, draws with missing lineages still alive at tp are rejected (and at 508 on overflow), so the effective proposal is q(z)/P(accept | θ), but logg omits -log P(accept). fhat (699) is therefore biased upward by -log P(accept), which is θ-dependent (measured acceptance 0.79 and 0.64 on a small tree → +0.23 and +0.45 nats). max_tries = 5·sample_size then silently returns fewer than sample_size trees (680-681) and reports rejected = 0 (804-807, 851).
concerns.why_it_matters: The reported loglik, loglik_var and any cross-θ comparison (CEM, model selection, profile likelihoods) built on BDI-DD fhat are biased by an amount that changes with θ; only the self-normalised M-step is immune.

concerns.description: parent_id for a missing species is deterministic: the id of the most recent observed branching before its birth (never a missing lineage, never a uniform draw among alive lineages, and id 0 — the FIRST non-crown branching, which happens AFTER the birth — for births before bt_sorted[1]). Line 557 is dead code (max(0L, integer(0)) is already 0). The N-only logf does not read parent_id so inference is unaffected, but simulate_tree(method='bdi')$tas / $trees get a topology that is not a draw from the conditional distribution, and species born in the initial 2-lineage period are attached to a lineage younger than themselves in the L-table.
concerns.why_it_matters: Users of the augmented phylo (plots, downstream tree statistics, D-covariate work) get systematically wrong attachment points; DDD::L2phylo silently produced a tree with such a row in my test rather than erroring.

concerns.description: The gate switches to thinning only on (model, link); rho < 1 is passed straight into .mcem_bdi (384), and simulate.R:345 does the same. Combined with the rho concern above, the default configuration is wrong for any incomplete-sampling analysis, and the fallback message is printed only when verbose = TRUE.
concerns.why_it_matters: This is the dispatch point where the wrong-target estimator is selected by default.

concerns.description: Critical branch (|λ0-μ0| < 1e-15): the comment swaps p and 1-p, I_lam = log(a1/a2) should be λΔt - log(a1/a2), and I_mu = λΔt + log(a2/a1) should be λΔt + log((tp-t1)/(tp-t2)); numeric check 4.666 vs code 2.622. Practically unreachable (threshold 1e-15), but the general formula also loses precision as d → 0 (p = d/(λ0-μ0E) with both terms O(d)).
concerns.why_it_matters: Wrong-but-unreachable code, plus a cancellation zone around λ ≈ μ where the exact hazard is numerically noisy.

concerns.description: On the final segment with n > 0, t_hi = tp - 1e-14 and H(t_hi) is finite (~n·30); a draw U > H(t_hi) (probability ~e^{-30·n}) makes uniroot error; more importantly 1 - exp(-d·1e-14) is computed with only ~2 significant digits in double precision, so event times within ~1e-13 of tp are noisy. Negligible in practice but the 'exact' claim rests on this end-point handling.
concerns.why_it_matters: Rare hard error rather than graceful handling; documents the numerical edge of the time-change.

concerns.description: Rate functions read pars8[3] as a coefficient on P (sum of pendant ages) and pars8[4] on E (focal age), the pre-2026-07 layout; the C++ Model reads the same slots as beta_M (M = P/N) and beta_D (D = E - M). The gate + .expand_pars zero these slots for compact pars, but an 8-element pars vector with non-zero slots 3/4 (accepted at 634-635) would be evaluated inconsistently between the R proposal and the C++ logf, and P̂/Ê/Var/Cov machinery (171-284, 338-366) is dead code under every reachable configuration.
concerns.why_it_matters: Latent inconsistency that becomes a real bug the day the gate is relaxed; ~150 lines of Gaussian-closure code cannot currently affect any result.

concerns.description: pd is written as 0 for every row and focal_tip_start is absent, whereas the thinning tree carries pendant pd per node (src/augment_tree.cpp:55-58). Harmless for N-only logf (beta_M = 0) but the two samplers do not return the same tree format, and any M/D-aware scoring of BDI trees would see M = 0.
concerns.why_it_matters: Format divergence between samplers that the README presents as interchangeable.

concerns.description: Immigration events add log(la) = log(λu) to logg although the sampled total immigration rate is 2kλu; missing-lineage births add log(la) although the sampled rate is n·la. This is consistent with the C++ logf's per-lineage convention (both drop the same (2k+m) multiplicity per birth, so the zero-variance property holds — verified), but the convention is undocumented and differs from the thinning sampling_prob, which uses log(n·λ·μ) - log(2·tips + Ne) (inst/include/model.hpp:304). The two 'log q(z|obs,θ)' values are therefore not comparable across samplers even for the same tree.
concerns.why_it_matters: A reviewer checking 'same log q convention' will find two different conventions; agreement of fhat between samplers (-16.87 vs -16.89) is empirical, not by construction.

concerns.description: .bdi_iterate stops silently at max_iter = 20 without reporting non-convergence; no diagnostic of the fixed point (delta) is returned. The forward Cov ODE drops death cross-jumps (documented at 226-228) and Ê is clipped to [0,tp] (366).
concerns.why_it_matters: Under strong DD the mean-field p(t) may be far from the fixed point and the user has no signal beyond low ESS / high rejection.

concerns.description: Under CR max_tries = sample_size, so any max_missing overflow (508) reduces the returned count below sample_size with no retry and no counter; under DD the shortfall is likewise silent. .mcem_bdi's num_trees column reflects the shortfall but 'rejected' is hard-coded 0.
concerns.why_it_matters: ESS and bootstrap variance computed on fewer trees than requested, unannounced.

concerns.description: DD branch breaks out of the segment loop when 1-p < 1e-12 or total < 1e-15 without adding the survival term -total·(t1 - t) for the remainder; with n_alive > 0 this leads to rejection at 514, with n_alive = 0 the omitted term is ≈ 0. Is the intended behaviour to reject, or should the remaining lineages be forced to die as the CR branch does via the divergent hazard?
concerns.why_it_matters: Determines how much of the DD rejection rate is a modelling choice vs a numerical artefact of the 1e-12 cut-off.

concerns.description: P_obs = k(t)·t assigns every observed lineage pendant age t (tip_start = 0), matching the C++ convention for initial-tree nodes, rather than t minus its branching time. Since P̂ never enters a live rate under the gate this is currently inert, but is this convention the intended definition of the M covariate for observed lineages?
concerns.why_it_matters: If the gate is relaxed, the mean-field M for observed lineages would be systematically too large.

concerns.description: For a 2-tip tree (n_obs = 0) `v_id[idx] <- seq(0L, n_obs - 1L)` evaluates seq(0L, -1L) = c(0,-1) assigned to a zero-length index; R tolerates it but it signals the 2-tip case was not exercised.
concerns.why_it_matters: Untested boundary; no BDI tests exist.

open_questions: Is the labelled-history convention (per-lineage λ per birth in logf, per-lineage λu in logg, no (2k+m) multiplicity on either side) the intended definition of f(obs,z), and is the thinning sampling_prob's log(n·λ·μ) - log(2·tips + Ne) meant to be the same density? They agree numerically on one test tree but are derived differently.
Should .bdi_supported also return FALSE for rho < 1 (routing to thinning), or is a rho-aware BDI (p_ρ(t) = ρ(λ-μ)/(ρλ + (λ(1-ρ) - μ)e^{-(λ-μ)(tp-t)}) plus an unsampled-extant event type) planned?
Is the μ0 > λ0 region intentionally out of scope for the CR sampler, or is the Inf return at bdi.R:59 an oversight (the formulas at 54 and 60 are valid for d < 0 if the sign test is removed)?
Under DD, is fhat supposed to be a usable log-likelihood estimate (then the acceptance probability must enter logg or the denominator), or only the M-step weights?
Why does .mcem_bdi keep the P̂/Ê/Gaussian-closure machinery when every reachable configuration zeroes its coefficients — is a (N, M, D) rewrite of .bdi_lam/.bdi_mu intended?

Is the deterministic parent assignment in .bdi_to_tree_df acceptable for simulate_tree()'s returned phylo, given that the D-covariate and any topology-dependent downstream use would need a uniform (2 per observed, 1 per missing) attachment draw?

There are no tests for R/bdi.R; which of the properties above (zero variance under CR, equality with the Nee likelihood, agreement with thinning under DD, behaviour at μ>λ and rho<1) should be pinned by tests before the sampler stays the default?

module: simulation-api (R/simulate.R, R/diagnostics.R, R/RcppExports.R, src/RcppExports.cpp, NAMESPACE, DESCRIPTION; with the C++ forward simulator inst/include/general_tree.hpp + src/div_tree.cpp and the augmentation-df conventions in src/unpack.h, src/E_step.cpp, src/augment_tree.cpp, inst/include/model_helpers.hpp that the R layer hard-codes against)
purpose: simulate_tree() is the single user-facing entry point for (a) forward Gillespie simulation of one tree from the crown under the 8-parameter {N, M, D} model, (b) batch forward simulation over a parameter matrix, and (c) conditional simulation = data augmentation of an observed extant tree with extinct/unsampled lineages via either the R BDI sampler or the C++ thinning proposal. It owns model/link resolution, the compact<->8-element parameter layouts, L-table extraction and the conversion of augmented C++ data frames back into DDD L-tables and ape phylo objects. diagnostics.R exposes diagnose_cem/diagnose_mcem/diagnose_gam (tables + base-graphics plots) and their print methods. RcppExports.R/.cpp are the five .Call bridges (simulate_div_tree_cpp, eval_logf, augment_trees, em_cpp, m_cpp); NAMESPACE exports 9 functions + 6 print methods.

key_functions.name: simulate_tree
key_functions.role: Exported dispatcher: matrix pars -> batch (recursion, optional mclapply); tree != NULL -> .sim_tree_conditional; else forward single simulation with R-level retry loop, survival_prob, rho tip-dropping, DDD::L2phylo conversion.

key_functions.name: .resolve_link
key_functions.role: 'linear'/'exponential'/'gaussian' -> 0/1/2; any numeric passed through as.integer unchecked.

key_functions.name: .resolve_model
key_functions.role: Shortcuts cr/dd/d/nd (+ legacy rd/ep) and formulas -> 3-slot binary c(use_N,use_M,use_D); any length-3 0/1 vector accepted, including slot 2 (M).

key_functions.name: .parse_model_formula
key_functions.role: term.labels upper-cased; N->slot1, D/EP/E->slot3; anything else errors (M not reachable via formula).

key_functions.name: .expand_pars
key_functions.role: Compact c(beta_0, beta_active..., gamma_0, gamma_active...) -> zero-padded 8-vector c(b0,bN,bM,bD,g0,gN,gM,gD).

key_functions.name: .contract_pars
key_functions.role: Inverse of .expand_pars (lives in inference.R, not simulate.R as README says).

key_functions.name: .pars_error_msg
key_functions.role: Builds the 'model = c(...) requires k parameters' message, names beta_M/gamma_M when slot 2 is on.

key_functions.name: .sim_tree_conditional
key_functions.role: Conditional path: brts + L_extant extraction, bdi->thinning fallback via .bdi_supported, tryCatch-wrapped sampler call, per-draw L-table + L2phylo, returns tas/log_q or trees/log_q.

key_functions.name: .extract_tes / .extract_Ltable
key_functions.role: Get the extant phylo / the L-table from a simulate_tree result or phylo. Prefers tree$L (the full simulated L-table) over DDD::phylo2L(tes).

key_functions.name: .aug_to_Ltable
key_functions.role: Merge augmented speciation rows of the C++/BDI data frame into the L-table: parent label via id->brts[pid+2]->nearest L row, new labels max|label|+k with parent's sign, forward->age time flip, unsampled sentinel 5e10 -> extant (-1).

key_functions.name: .augment_tree_internal
key_functions.role: Thin wrapper around augment_trees() (C++ rcpp_mce): expands pars, default maxN = max(2000, 200*sample_size).

key_functions.name: .extract_brts
key_functions.role: numeric -> sort decreasing; phylo -> branching.times decreasing; list -> $tes or prune_to_extant($tas); crown age first.

key_functions.name: .bdi_supported
key_functions.role: TRUE iff model_bin[2]==0 & model_bin[3]==0 & link in {0,1}.

key_functions.name: simulate_div_tree_cpp
key_functions.role: Constructs sim_tree::general_div, runs simulate_tree_ltable() with its own retry loop (R always passes max_tries=0), converts ltable to DDD 4-column matrix in age units, returns list(Ltable, status).

key_functions.name: sim_tree::general_div::simulate_tree_ltable
key_functions.role: Forward Gillespie with N, P, M=P/N, E_s, D_s=E_s-M covariates; three link functions; stops on finished / extinction (either crown clade empty) / maxN_exceeded.

key_functions.name: E_step / create_tree
key_functions.role: Builds the input tree at forward times (c-brts[2],...,c-brts[n-1], c); collects N valid augmentations (finite log_w, exp(log_w)>0) under a 120 s wall-clock cap; throws if fewer than N.

key_functions.name: unpack
key_functions.role: Augmented tree -> data.frame(brts, n, t_ext, pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start, id, parent_id).

key_functions.name: rcpp_mce (R: augment_trees)
key_functions.role: E-step bridge returning trees, logf, logg, rejection counters, time.

key_functions.name: diagnose_cem
key_functions.role: Convergence table, population spread quantiles, IS_quality from details$best_IS, final_pop, up to 2+has_IS+has_rej+n_par base plots.

key_functions.name: diagnose_mcem
key_functions.role: Per-iteration fhat/delta_max/rejected/num_trees/time, IS_quality from details$final_IS incl. acceptance_rate and loglik_var, plots.

key_functions.name: diagnose_gam
key_functions.role: Surface coverage, mgcv summary stats (dev.expl, gcv.ubre, sum edf, r.sq), MLE, 1-D slices + predicted-vs-observed + residual hist.

key_functions.name: print.mcem_diagnostics / print.gam_diagnostics / print.cem_diagnostics
key_functions.role: cat-based summaries; MCEM print hard-codes '(bootstrap, B=200)'.

key_functions.name: R_init_emphasis
key_functions.role: Registers 5 .Call entry points and calls remphasis_init(dll) (nlopt function-pointer init from rinit.cpp).

math_as_implemented:
PARAMETER LAYOUTS. pars8 = (p[0..7]) = (beta_0, beta_N, beta_M, beta_D, gamma_0, gamma_N, gamma_M, gamma_D) [general_tree.hpp:16, div_tree.cpp:24-27]; model_bin = (use_N, use_M, use_D) [general_tree.hpp:18, simulate.R:255-257]. Compact user vector for model_bin with active = which(model_bin==1) (slot 1=N, 2=M, 3=D), n_lam = 1+|active|: pars8[1] = pars[1]; pars8[1+active] = pars[2..n_lam]; pars8[5] = pars[n_lam+1]; pars8[5+active] = pars[(n_lam+2)..end]; all other slots 0 [simulate.R:298-310]. Required length 2+2*sum(model_bin) [simulate.R:196, 299]. Inverse: c(pars8[1], pars8[1+active], pars8[5], pars8[5+active]) [inference.R:347-352]. The model flags NEVER zero a coefficient in C++: inactive terms vanish only because R zero-pads; model[2] (use_D) only selects the algorithm branch [general_tree.hpp:185, 227].

MODEL RESOLUTION. cr=(0,0,0), dd=(1,0,0), d=rd=ep=(0,0,1), nd=(1,0,1) [simulate.R:259-261]; formula terms: N->slot1, D|EP|E->slot3, else error [282-288]; any integer length-3 vector in {0,1} accepted, so c(0,1,0) (M-only) is reachable [268-274]. Link: linear=0, exponential=1, gaussian=2; numeric input -> as.integer with no range check [247-251].

FORWARD SIMULATOR (forward time t in [0, max_t], crown at t=0). State per lineage s: start_date, tip_start(s) (reset to t when s speciates), label, end_date (-1 alive) [general_tree.hpp:69-78]. Covariates at time t: N = N1+N2 alive; P = N*t - sum_{alive} tip_start(s) [178]; M = P/N (0 if N=0) [120]; E_s = t - tip_start(s) [204, 239]; D_s = E_s - M [121]. Linear predictors: eta_lambda = p0 + p1*N + p2*M + p3*D_s; eta_mu = p4 + p5*N + p6*M + p7*D_s [126, 138]. Links: link 0: rate = max(0, eta) [104-107]; link 1: rate = exp(eta) [105]; link 2 (gaussian): lambda = p0 * exp(-(eta_cov-1)^2/2) with eta_cov = p1*N + p2*M + p3*D_s (intercept excluded from the exponent; p0 is the peak), mu likewise with p4 and (p5,p6,p7) [110-113, 122-125, 134-137]. Total rate: if use_D==0: N*(lambda+mu) evaluated with E=0, i.e. D = -M, which is harmless only because p3=p7=0 [185-189]; if use_D==1 and link==1: Sum_s lambda_s = exp(p0 + p1*N + (p2-p3)*M + p3*t) * Sum_{alive} exp(-p3*tip_start(s)) (+ same for mu with p4..p7) via running sums [190-199, 269-271, 282-284]; else O(N) per-lineage sum [200-207]. Waiting time: t_next = t + Exp(total_rate); Exp(lambda<=0) returns 1e20 so a zero/negative total rate ends the run as 'finished' [46, 209-214]. Event: use_D==0: focal = uniform alive lineage, speciation with prob lambda/(lambda+mu) using P recomputed at the new t [219, 228-231]; use_D==1: lineage s with prob (lambda_s+mu_s)/Sum, then speciation with prob lambda_s/(lambda_s+mu_s) [233-256]. Speciation: parent tip_start <- t; daughter (start=t, tip_start=t, parent_label=label(focal), label = +/-tree_id with sign of parent, N1 or N2 += 1) [262-277]. Extinction: end_date <- t, N1/N2 -= 1 [279-288]. Stop: 'extinction' as soon as N1<1 or N2<1 (either crown clade lost, not whole-tree extinction) [290]; 'maxN_exceeded' when N >= max_N checked at loop top [175]; 'finished' when t_next >= max_t [211]. Initial rows: (start 0, parent 0, label -1), (start 0, parent -1, label 2), tree_id starts at 3 [158-160]. Times are stored as float [71-74].

L-TABLE OUTPUT [div_tree.cpp:45-51]: col1 = max_t - start_date (age before present), col2 = parent label, col3 = label, col4 = (end_date >= 0) ? max_t - end_date : -1. status: done | extinct | too_large [53-55]. C++ retries while extinct/maxN and tries < max_tries [33-39]; R passes max_tries = 0 and loops itself: repeat while status != 'done' and n_attempts <= max_tries, so total attempts <= max_tries+1 [simulate.R:204-209]. survival_prob = 1/n_attempts if done else 0 [211]; batch survival_prob = mean over rows of that [168].

RHO < 1, FORWARD [simulate.R:215-223]: extant_idx = rows with col4 == -1; n_drop ~ Binomial(|extant_idx|, 1-rho) capped at |extant_idx|-2; sampled rows get col4 <- max_t. Under DDD::L2phylo (col4 -> age - col4 = 0 forward, col1 -> age - col1 > 0) that is a lineage dying at forward time 0, before its own birth; tes (dropextinct=TRUE) simply drops them, tas gets edge length = 0 - birth < 0 (observed min edge -4.99).

CONDITIONAL PATH. brts = sort(branching.times, decreasing=TRUE), brts[1] = crown age c, length Ntip-1 [inference.R:216-231]; max_t = c [simulate.R:338]. L_extant = tree$L if non-NULL else DDD::phylo2L(tes) [403-410]. Sampler: 'bdi' unless !(model_bin[2]==0 & model_bin[3]==0 & link in {0,1}) -> 'thinning' [345, bdi.R:100-105]. Thinning call: augment_trees(brts, pars8, sample_size=n_trees, maxN = max(2000, 200*n_trees), max_missing, max_lambda, num_threads, model, link, rho) [463-488]. C++ input tree: nodes at forward times (c-brts[2], ..., c-brts[n-1], c) with n = 2+i and t_ext = t_ext_tip [E_step.cpp:19-38]; in augment_tree() non-extinction nodes get id = 0,1,... in that order and parent_id = -1, so id k <-> brts[k+2] (R 1-based) and the last id is the closing node at the present [augment_tree.cpp:196-212]. A draw is accepted iff log_w = logf - logg is finite and exp(log_w) > 0 [E_step.cpp:88-104]; fewer than N accepted (after maxN attempts or the 120 s cap) throws [69-79, 120-122] -> R tryCatch returns NULL -> failure output (tas=NULL, log_q=NA) [348-369]. log_q = aug$logg: thinning -> model.sampling_prob(pars, tree) [E_step.cpp:92]; BDI -> Gillespie-accumulated logg [bdi.R:674]. Augmented df columns [unpack.h:27-34]: brts (forward), n, t_ext (forward extinction time; sentinels t_ext_extinct = 0.0, t_ext_unsampled = 5e10, t_ext_tip = 10e10 = 1e11 [model_helpers.hpp:48-50], duplicated as literals 1e11/5e10 in R [simulate.R:417-418, bdi.R:544, 572]), pd, tip_start, focal_tip_start, id, parent_id. Thinning parent: uniform over node ids with brts < t_spec, t_ext > t_spec, not extinction; -1 if none [augment_tree.cpp:153-166]. BDI parent: id of the latest observed event with bt <= birth, forced to 0 when none [bdi.R:551-552].

.aug_to_Ltable [simulate.R:414-453]: rows kept = t_ext != 0 & parent_id != -1 & t_ext < 1e11 (augmented speciation nodes, incl. unsampled 5e10) [419-421], sorted by forward brts [433]. Parent label p_lbl = aug_labels[pid] if pid is an earlier augmented id, else L_extant[argmin_r |L_extant[r,1] - brts[pid+2]|, 3]; NA (pid<0 or pid+2 > length(brts)) -> L_extant[1,3] [425-440]. New label = (max|L_extant[,3]| + k) with sign(p_lbl) [432, 442]. Row = (c - brts_k, p_lbl, lbl, ext_k) with ext_k = -1 if t_ext == 5e10 else c - t_ext [447-448]. Then DDD::L2phylo(L, dropextinct=FALSE) [377].

data_flow: FORWARD: user pars (compact, length 2+2*sum(model_bin)) --.resolve_model/.resolve_link--> model_bin (3 slots), link_int --.expand_pars--> pars8 --simulate_div_tree_cpp(pars8, model_bin, max_t, as.integer(max_lin), 0L, link)--> C++ general_div (float times, own mt19937 seeded from clock^thread-id, forward time 0..max_t, crown = 2 rows labelled -1 and 2) --> Ltable in DDD age units (col1 birth age, col4 death age or -1) + status; R retry loop (<= max_tries+1 attempts) -> survival_prob = 1/n_attempts or 0; rho<1: Binomial drop of extant rows by setting col4 <- max_t; useDDD: tes = L2phylo(L, dropextinct=TRUE), tas = L2phylo(L, FALSE), both tryCatch->NULL. Output list(tes, tas, L, status, survival_prob). BATCH: matrix rows -> recursive simulate_tree with already-resolved model_bin/link_int (positional args, num_threads=1 inside), lapply or parallel::mclapply on unix; tree==NULL -> list(simulations, survival_prob=mean); tree!=NULL -> plain list of conditional results (undocumented). CONDITIONAL: tree (simulate_tree result | phylo | numeric brts) --.extract_brts--> brts decreasing, crown first; max_t = brts[1]; L_extant = tree$L (full simulated L-table when the input is a simulate_tree result) else phylo2L(tes); method bdi->thinning fallback; thinning: pars8 + brts -> augment_trees (rcpp_mce -> E_step; input nodes at forward times c-brts[2..n-1] plus closing node at c; ids 0..n-2) -> list(trees=df list, logf, logg, rejected*, time); bdi: R sampler -> same shape (trees, logf, logg, weights, fhat). Per df: .aug_to_Ltable (forward->age flip, id->brts[pid+2]->nearest-L-row parent, sign-inherited labels, 5e10->extant) -> L2phylo(dropextinct=FALSE) -> tas; log_q = logg. n_trees==1 -> list(tas, log_q[1]); else list(trees, log_q). Index conventions: R brts 1-based with brts[1]=crown; C++ node ids 0-based starting at the SECOND branching time (crown has no node), closing node id = n-2 at forward time c; augmented ids continue from n-1; extinction nodes carry the species id with t_ext=0; L-table labels: sign = crown clade, magnitude unique; times in the df are forward (0=crown, c=present), in the L-table ages (c=crown, 0=present). DIAGNOSTICS: emphasis_fit$details (or raw list) -> data frames/lists + base-graphics plots; nothing is recomputed from raw trees except mean/sd of finite lw and quantiles of fhat_all.
invariants_assumed: brts is strictly decreasing with the crown age first and length Ntip-1; the observed tree is ultrametric and binary (E_step.cpp:19-38, simulate.R:338, 426-429).

tree$L, when present on the input, is an extant-only L-table whose birth ages coincide with brts (simulate.R:404, 428) -- violated for any simulate_tree() result with extinction (tree$L is the full L-table).

DDD L-table convention: col1 = birth age, col2 = parent label, col3 = label with one crown clade negative, col4 = -1 extant else death age; first two rows are (age,0,-1,-1) and (age,-1,2,-1) (general_tree.hpp:158-159, div_tree.cpp:45-51, DDD::phylo2L tail).
pars8 is zero-padded for inactive covariates; the C++ rate functions read all 8 coefficients regardless of model_bin (general_tree.hpp:126, 138; simulate.R:298-310).
C++ node id k corresponds to brts[k+2] (R 1-based) and the closing node at the present is the last observed id; BDI reproduces the same id scheme (bdi.R:538-560, simulate.R:428).
Sentinel values t_ext_extinct=0, t_ext_unsampled=5e10, t_ext_tip=1e11 are identical in C++ (#define) and in the R literals (model_helpers.hpp:48-50; simulate.R:417-418; bdi.R:544,572).

The augmented df is sorted by forward brts and each augmented species appears as a speciation node (t_ext = death or 5e10) plus, if extinct, an extinction node with t_ext = 0 (augment_tree.cpp:90-125).
rho in (0,1] -- never validated in simulate_tree; rho<1 in the forward path assumes at least 2 extant tips survive the drop (simulate.R:219).
max_t > 0, max_lin > 0, pars numeric non-empty are checked; n_trees, num_threads, max_missing, maxN are coerced with as.integer without range checks (simulate.R:148-149, 191-194, 182-184).
For the gaussian link the intercepts beta_0, gamma_0 are non-negative (rates must be >= 0 for the Bernoulli event choice) -- not checked anywhere in this subsystem (general_tree.hpp:110-113, 231).

Forward-simulation randomness comes from a C++ std::mt19937 seeded from the wall clock and thread id, not from R's RNG; only the rho tip-dropping (rbinom/sample) follows set.seed (general_tree.hpp:37-43, simulate.R:218-221).
DDD and ape are installed (Imports) and DDD::L2phylo/phylo2L accept the produced tables; every conversion failure is swallowed to NULL (simulate.R:228-231, 377, 407).

diagnose_* trust the fit object's stored ESS, lw, fhat, history, final_pop, best_IS/final_IS fields produced by the current de.R/emphasis.R/gam.R code (diagnostics.R:102-104, 137-149, 380-381, 634-635).

RcppExports.R (lines 9, 13, 36-37, 65-66, 97-98, 131-132) and src/div_tree.cpp:10-14 still document model as c(use_N, use_P, use_E) and link as '0 = linear, 1 = exponential' only; the code uses (use_N, use_M, use_D) and link 2 = gaussian (general_tree.hpp:4-18, 122). general_tree.hpp:87-88 comments also say 'beta_E' and '{use_N, use_P, use_E}'.

simulate_tree docs (simulate.R:60-61): 'failed draws are NULL' in `trees`; C++ excludes failed draws entirely (E_step.cpp:96-104), NULL entries arise only from useDDD = FALSE or a L2phylo failure (simulate.R:373-378).
DESCRIPTION:11 says `License: file LICENSE`; README badge and License section say MIT (CRAN form would be 'MIT + file LICENSE').

README line 51 lists select_diversification_model/compare_models under inference.R and says exported functions are nine; NAMESPACE matches nine exports, so README's function-reference table is the inconsistent part.

README says the BDI sampler is the default 'within the scope stated above' and .sim_tree_conditional falls back to thinning (simulate.R:345); the *installed* build (library 0.4) lacks that fallback line, so installed method='bdi' on a D model or gaussian link runs BDI anyway -- the installed package lags the source.

concerns.description: .extract_Ltable prefers tree$L, which for a simulate_tree() result is the FULL simulated L-table including the true extinct lineages. .sim_tree_conditional then appends the augmented lineages to it (line 343, 375). Confirmed: for a cr tree with 30 extant tips and 21 extinct rows, augmented L-tables averaged 70 rows (49 with phylo2L(tes)), 43/50 had a parent that died before its child was born, and 43/50 resulting tas phylo objects had negative edge lengths (80/100 in an earlier run); with DDD::phylo2L(tes) as L_extant both counts were 0/50 for both samplers. Mechanism: L2phylo(dropextinct=TRUE) re-parents extant rows onto extinct ancestors, so tes branching times coincide with birth ages of EXTINCT rows (8 of 28 here), and id_to_label (line 428) maps those events onto extinct labels.
concerns.why_it_matters: The 'augmented' tree returned to users leaks the latent truth (real extinct lineages) into the augmentation and produces invalid phylogenies; any downstream use of tas from a simulated input (plots, simulation studies, D-covariate checks) is wrong, and it only affects simulated inputs, so real-data runs look fine while validation studies are corrupted.

concerns.description: Passing a numeric branching-time vector as `tree` (documented at lines 66-68 and in README) errors: .extract_Ltable does `tree$L` on an atomic vector (line 404) before any tryCatch. Confirmed: simulate_tree(tree = c(5,3,1), pars = c(0.5,0.1)) -> '$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors'.
concerns.why_it_matters: A documented input type of the main exported function is unusable in the conditional path; .extract_brts (inference.R:217-219) supports it, so only this helper blocks it.

concerns.description: rho < 1 forward sampling marks dropped tips with L[drop,4] <- max_t, commented as 'extinct at present'. In DDD's convention col4 is an age, so max_t means extinct at the crown, i.e. before the lineage's own birth; L2phylo(dropextinct=FALSE) yields negative edges (confirmed: tas min edge -4.99 with rho = 0.5) and the returned L carries these impossible rows. Because tree$L is later reused as L_extant (line 404), augmenting such a simulated tree inherits the bogus rows.
concerns.why_it_matters: Any incomplete-sampling simulation study using tas or L is invalid; only tes (dropextinct=TRUE filters col4 == -1) survives. Also n_drop is capped at n_extant-2 without guaranteeing one survivor per crown clade.

concerns.description: Batch survival_prob = mean(1/n_attempts) (line 211), which the roxygen (lines 46-47) describes as the fraction of simulations with status == 'done'. Confirmed with max_tries = 1: values {0, 0.5, 1}, mean 0.383 while the done-fraction was 0.467. The single-tree quantity 1/n_attempts is also a very coarse estimator (with the default max_tries = 1 it can only be 1, 0.5 or 0).
concerns.why_it_matters: auto_bounds/GAM survival training and anyone reading survival_prob as P(survival) get a biased number unless max_tries = 0; the docs and README example (max_tries = 0) hide the dependence.

concerns.description: The forward simulator seeds its own std::mt19937 from high_resolution_clock ^ hash(thread id) at construction, ignoring R's RNG (RNGScope in RcppExports.cpp:18 is irrelevant). Confirmed: two set.seed(42) runs gave L-tables with 29 vs 156 rows. Only the rho tip-dropping (simulate.R:218-221) follows set.seed. R CMD check also flags system RNG use as non-portable (00check.log:108-118 lists abort/assert; RNG policy is the same section).
concerns.why_it_matters: No forward simulation, survival-probability estimate, auto_bounds run or test is reproducible; the skipped tests that call set.seed(42) could never be made deterministic.

concerns.description: The filter parent_id != -1L drops every augmented lineage whose C++ parent search found no candidate node (augment_tree.cpp:153-166), which happens for lineages born between the crown and the first later branching event because crown lineages are not nodes. Confirmed: 33 of 1265 augmented lineages (2.6%) across 100 thinning draws had parent_id == -1 and are absent from tas while still contributing to log_q.
concerns.why_it_matters: tas and log_q describe different augmentations z; the missing lineages are systematically the oldest ones, biasing any topology- or age-based summary of the augmented trees.

concerns.description: id_to_label attaches an augmented lineage to the DAUGHTER row born at the parent event (nearest L row by birth age), never to the continuing parent lineage, and thinning parents are drawn uniformly over event NODES rather than alive LINEAGES (augment_tree.cpp:154-166), so the two crown lineages can never be parents. Fallback L_extant[1,3] (line 440) silently attaches to the first row when the id is the closing node or out of range.
concerns.why_it_matters: The tas topology (which sister lineage an extinct branch hangs from) is a convention, not a draw from the model; for D/age-imbalance covariates the identity of the speciating lineage matters, so tas cannot be used to check D-dependent likelihoods.

concerns.description: BDI parent = max(0L, which(bt_sorted <= birth) - 1L) forces parent 0 for lineages born before the first post-crown event (line 552 `length(parent)==0` is dead code since max() always returns length 1). .aug_to_Ltable then attaches them to the daughter of an event that happens AFTER their birth; L2phylo re-parents them onto that node, shifting their attachment time. Observed 2 such lineages in 50 draws; no negative edges resulted in that run.
concerns.why_it_matters: Same class of tas/log_q mismatch as the thinning parent_id == -1 case, but silent (no drop, wrong attachment).

concerns.description: .resolve_model accepts any length-3 0/1 vector, so model = c(0,1,0) or c(1,1,1) activates the M slot the docs call internal-only (lines 9-11, 24); .expand_pars/.pars_error_msg then demand beta_M/gamma_M (confirmed: .expand_pars(c(1,2,3,4), c(0,1,0)) -> c(1,0,2,0,3,0,4,0)). The formula path rejects M (line 282-288) and .bdi_supported treats slot 2 as unsupported, so behaviour differs by how the model is written.
concerns.why_it_matters: Undocumented parameterisation reachable from the public API; tests only cover c(1,0,1) and c(1,2,0).

concerns.description: .resolve_link passes any numeric through as.integer with no range check; general_tree.hpp:104-107 treats every value other than 1 or 2 as linear, while model.hpp:87 static_casts it to an enum. link = 3 therefore silently behaves as linear in forward simulation and as an out-of-range enum in augmentation.
concerns.why_it_matters: Silent misconfiguration; different behaviour between the two C++ code paths for the same value.

concerns.description: With the gaussian link (or exponential/linear with odd inputs) nothing prevents negative intercepts: lambda = beta_0*exp(...) < 0 when beta_0 < 0. If lambda + mu > 0 the code calls std::bernoulli_distribution(lambda/(lambda+mu)) with p outside [0,1] (undefined behaviour); if the total is <= 0, expon() returns 1e20 and the run ends 'done' with 2 rows (confirmed: pars c(-0.5, 0.1), link gaussian -> status 'done', 2-row L). No R-side validation in simulate_tree.
concerns.why_it_matters: Silent nonsense trees labelled 'done', or UB, from parameter vectors that a bounds search could easily propose.

concerns.description: Both sampler calls are wrapped in tryCatch(error = function(e) NULL) (lines 348-364) and every L2phylo/phylo2L call likewise (228-231, 377, 407), so a genuine bug (bad model_bin, C++ exception, missing DDD, the 120 s E_step cap at E_step.cpp:69-79) is indistinguishable from 'augmentation failed': the user gets tas = NULL, log_q = NA and no message.
concerns.why_it_matters: Hides errors during audits and makes failure rates uninterpretable.

concerns.description: insert_unsampled_species is triggered whenever ext_time >= b regardless of rho; model.hpp:216 says the caller should treat that as an unsampled tip. If model.extinction_time can return >= T with rho = 1, the augmented tree gains an extra extant tip that .aug_to_Ltable marks -1 (line 447), so tas has more extant tips than the observed tree.
concerns.why_it_matters: Would make the augmentation inconsistent with the observed data under complete sampling; depends on extinction_time's conditioning, which is outside this subsystem.

concerns.description: L-table times are stored as float (start_date, tip_start, end_date, and the running time t), i.e. ~7 significant digits; the R side later matches birth ages by which.min(abs(L[,1] - brts)) (simulate.R:428) and prune_to_extant uses tol = 1e-8 on heights (inference.R:16-24).
concerns.why_it_matters: For old crowns (ages ~100) branching-time resolution is ~1e-5, enough to create duplicate/zero-length branchings and to make nearest-match parent lookup ambiguous when a phylo-derived L-table (double) is compared to float-derived brts.

concerns.description: With useDDD = FALSE the conditional path returns tas = NULL and discards both the augmented L-table and the raw data frame; there is no way for a user to obtain the augmentation without DDD, unlike the forward path which returns L.
concerns.why_it_matters: The documented 'or NULL when useDDD = FALSE' leaves log_q with no companion object; inference code has to call the internal .augment_tree_internal instead.

concerns.description: Batch recursion passes 15 positional arguments to simulate_tree (any reordering of the signature breaks it silently), forces num_threads = 1 inside each row, and vapply(sims, `[[`, 0, 'survival_prob') (line 168) fails on try-error objects returned by mclapply when a worker errors. The conditional batch return (line 172) is undocumented.
concerns.why_it_matters: Fragile plumbing; a single failing row in a parallel batch aborts the whole result.

concerns.description: diagnose_cem: `if (!is.na(bi$ESS))` errors ('argument is of length zero') when best_IS lacks ESS (NULL); ESS is taken from the fit rather than recomputed from lw although the roxygen (38-39) states the formula; diagnose_cem and diagnose_mcem are documented to return invisibly (69, 354) but return visibly (305-315, 533-541); @return omits stop_reason and the 'rejected' column (388-397, 533-541); print.mcem_diagnostics hard-codes '(bootstrap, B=200)' (579-580) regardless of what produced loglik_var; diagnose_mcem par_names from names(x$pars) may not match the number of par[0-9]+ columns (374, 387, 457).
concerns.why_it_matters: Diagnostics can crash on older fit objects and report labels that do not reflect the computation.

concerns.description: License field is 'file LICENSE' while README declares MIT; R CMD check (00check.log:67) notes DESCRIPTION meta-information. Compiled-code WARNING: abort/assert entry points in E_step.o, loglik.o, rcpp_*.o (00check.log:108-118).
concerns.why_it_matters: Blocks a clean check/CRAN submission; assert() in E_step can terminate the R session.

concerns.description: log_q for method = 'thinning' is model.sampling_prob from C++ (E_step.cpp:92) while for method = 'bdi' it is the Gillespie-accumulated logg (bdi.R:674); both are returned under the same name and documented as log q(z | obs, theta). Are they normalised over the same event space (e.g. does either include the parent-choice probability or the unsampled-tip factor)?
concerns.why_it_matters: Users mixing draws from the two samplers, or comparing log_q across methods, would be comparing different densities.

concerns.description: Default maxN in the public conditional path is max(2000, 200*n_trees) (also documented at 89-90) but .run_mcem uses max(2000, 10*sample_size) (inference.R:365) and .augment_tree_bdi has its own max_tries = sample_size (CR) or 5*sample_size (bdi.R:663); max_tries is ignored in the conditional path.
concerns.why_it_matters: Three different attempt budgets for the same operation; failure/acceptance statistics are not comparable between simulate_tree() and estimate_rates().

concerns.description: The C++ retry loop (max_tries) is never exercised from R (simulate.R:207 passes 0L); the R loop counts attempts for survival_prob. Is the C++ argument still meant to be part of the API (RcppExports.R:12 documents it)?
concerns.why_it_matters: Dead parameter that a future caller might use, getting retries that survival_prob does not see.

open_questions: Is tas from conditional simulation meant to be a faithful draw of the augmented tree (then .extract_Ltable must use an extant-only L-table and parent choice must be uniform over lineages), or only a visual aid? The current L_extant = tree$L makes it wrong for every simulated input.

What is survival_prob intended to estimate: P(both crown clades survive to max_t) (needs many attempts and max_tries = 0 semantics) or merely 1/attempts as a flag? auto_bounds/train_GAM consumers should be checked against this.
Should the M slot (model_bin[2]) remain reachable through the binary-vector interface, or be rejected as the docs imply?
Does model.extinction_time (model.hpp ~216) guarantee ext_time < T when rho = 1, so that insert_unsampled_species never fires under complete sampling?
Are the two log_q definitions (C++ sampling_prob vs BDI Gillespie logg) the same density up to the same normalising events (parent choice, unsampled tips, closing interval)?
Is forward-simulation non-reproducibility (own mt19937) accepted, or should the simulator draw from R's RNG (unif_rand) so set.seed works and R CMD check's RNG policy is met?

Why does the installed 0.4 build lack the .bdi_supported fallback present in the source .sim_tree_conditional -- is the library copy stale, and are the audit's other findings expected to match the source or the installed build?

Should crown-interval augmented lineages (parent_id == -1 in thinning, parent 0 in BDI) attach to one of the two crown rows (-1 / 2) chosen at random, and should .aug_to_Ltable stop filtering on parent_id?
